explanation: Executing anyway defeats the guard's purpose and performs the exact over-limit action the policy exists to prevent.

text: Hide the denial, reasoning without the policy result
explanation: Hiding the denial removes the policy result from the model's reasoning, so it cannot choose the allowed escalation path it was given.

text: Allow all tools by instruction, leaving deletion and exfiltration open
explanation: Instruction-only limits leave every tool technically reachable, so deletion and exfiltration remain one prompt away despite the task scope.

text: Allow email and delete with confirmation, keeping unneeded risk
explanation: Confirmation reduces but does not remove risk; least privilege requires powers the task never needs, like email and delete, to be removed entirely.

text: Allow only read and save-copy
explanation: Least privilege removes unneeded email and delete powers entirely. Read plus save-copy with a completed-scan gate before save preserves the redaction task while eliminating exfiltration and destructio

text: Require a completed scan before any save
explanation: Least privilege removes unneeded email and delete powers entirely. Read plus save-copy with a completed-scan gate before save preserves the redaction task while eliminating exfiltration and destructio

text: Shorten text, forcing the model to guess productivity
explanation: Shorter responses give the model even less information to distinguish no-match from failure, deepening the guessing that caused the loop.

text: Raise generic exceptions, masking real errors
explanation: Generic exceptions collapse retryable, permission, and no-match cases into one signal, so the loop cannot choose the right recovery.

text: Return bare empty arrays, confusing no-match with failure
explanation: Bare empty arrays are the current defect: the model cannot tell a valid empty result from a transient or permission failure, so it keeps searching.

text: Return explicit no-match status distinct from transient and permission errors
explanation: Retry loops need machine-readable status. An explicit no-match status distinct from transient, permission, and validation errors lets the loop stop correctly instead of inferring from brevity or crash

text: Trust the stale flag, risking deploy of untested code
explanation: The flag describes tests against an older commit; trusting it can deploy code that was never tested after the repository changed.

text: Bind test success to an immutable commit or artifact digest
explanation: Boolean flags go stale when code changes. Binding test success to an immutable commit or artifact digest and rechecking it immediately before deploy blocks deployment against stale validation.

text: Revalidate the digest immediately before deploy
explanation: Boolean flags go stale when code changes. Binding test success to an immutable commit or artifact digest and rechecking it immediately before deploy blocks deployment against stale validation.

text: Accept a confident model review as equivalent to tests
explanation: A confident review is not execution evidence; it cannot substitute for tests bound to the exact artifact being deployed.

text: Prompt agents to avoid slowness, leaving retry storms unchecked
explanation: A prompt does not shed load; agents keep retrying at the transport layer, so the storm exhausts the service pool regardless of instructions.

text: Stuff timeout logs into context, wasting attention without shedding load
explanation: Adding logs consumes context and attention but changes no retry behavior, so the retry storm continues to drain the pool.

text: Trip a circuit breaker and fail fast during cooldown
explanation: Repeated timeouts need load shedding, not reminders or more logs. A circuit breaker trips after the error threshold and fails fast during cooldown, protecting the service pool.

text: Debate root causes in a worker while overload spreads
explanation: Root-cause debate happens after stabilization; while overload spreads, the priority is shedding load, not analysis.

text: Retry indefinitely, stalling the user task
explanation: Retries are already exhausted, so continuing to retry only stalls the task while the endpoint stays overloaded.

text: Route to an evaluated fallback and mark degraded telemetry
explanation: Exhausted retries with quality tolerance call for graceful degradation. Routing to an evaluated fallback model and marking the degraded path in telemetry preserves the task with explicit quality bound

text: Strip quality checks, risking silent bad output
explanation: Removing quality checks removes the safety net exactly when running on a reduced-quality fallback, risking silent bad output.

text: fork_session
explanation: Forking gives each analysis an isolated branch from the same starting evidence.

text: Return partial text as complete, hiding the failure
explanation: Presenting partial output as complete misrepresents the degraded state to the user and hides the failure instead of bounding it.

text: Trust the aggregate, ignoring the failing segment
explanation: Trusting the aggregate is the current blind spot: high overall accuracy conceals the rare document type where misses concentrate.

text: Calibrate by type and sample high-confidence outputs per segment
explanation: Aggregates hide rare-type failures and confidence misleads. Calibrating by document type and sampling high-confidence outputs within each risk segment exposes confident misses where harm concentrates.

text: Review only low confidence, missing confident misses
explanation: Confidence-based routing misses exactly the confident errors this segment produces, since its scores stay high while its miss rate climbs.

text: Raise the global threshold, overloading review without targeting risk
explanation: A higher global threshold floods review with low-risk items while still never sampling the high-confidence outputs where the rare-type errors live.

text: Pass only the relevant fields plus provenance
explanation: Attention needs minimal sufficient context with provenance. Passing only relevant fields plus source into the model while retaining the full result outside context preserves grounding without dilution

text: Retain the full result outside context for audit or lookup
explanation: Attention needs minimal sufficient context with provenance. Passing only relevant fields plus source into the model while retaining the full result outside context preserves grounding without dilution

text: Pass all fields, diluting attention with noise
explanation: Passing dozens of irrelevant fields dilutes the model's attention with noise and increases the chance the decision-relevant fields are overlooked.

text: Pass prose without sources, losing verifiability
explanation: Prose without provenance cannot be verified or traced back to the source record, so any decision built on it is ungrounded.

text: Infer confirmation from sentiment, opening without consent
explanation: Inferred sentiment is not recorded consent; opening an irreversible account on an inference bypasses the explicit customer confirmation policy requires.

text: Open after KYC then confirm, making reversal impossible
explanation: Opening before confirmation reverses the gate order, so the irreversible action happens before the consent that must precede it.

text: Require current KYC success
explanation: Irreversible actions need conjunctive gates. Account creation must require both current KYC success and an explicit confirmation record; sentiment inference, deferred confirmation, or either/or logic

text: Require an explicit confirmation record
explanation: Irreversible actions need conjunctive gates. Account creation must require both current KYC success and an explicit confirmation record; sentiment inference, deferred confirmation, or either/or logic

text: Treat old prose as durable approval, enabling stale authorization
explanation: Prose from an hour-old conversation is stale authorization: nothing binds it to the current change, so the agent can fish for permissive-sounding sentences.

text: Require fresh structured approval bound to the exact change and actor
explanation: Old conversation text is not authorization. Production changes need fresh, structured approval bound to the exact proposed change and actor, preventing stale or inferred consent.

text: Let the agent infer approval, inviting self-authorization
explanation: Agent-inferred approval is self-authorization: the same system proposing the change also decides the consent exists, with no independent evidence.

text: Accept two agents agreeing the tone sounds permissive
explanation: Two agents agreeing on tone is still inference, not authorization; neither is an accountable human actor bound to the specific change.

text: Log actor, action, argument digest, and timestamps with trace ID
explanation: Reconstruction needs full attempt history. Sufficient logs capture actor, action, argument digest, timestamps with trace ID plus policy decision and result, explicitly including blocked attempts that

text: Log policy decision and result, including blocked attempts
explanation: Reconstruction needs full attempt history. Sufficient logs capture actor, action, argument digest, timestamps with trace ID plus policy decision and result, explicitly including blocked attempts that

text: A single shared mutable prompt
explanation: A shared mutable prompt lets one analysis contaminate the other's reasoning.

text: Deleting the original context
explanation: Deleting context removes the shared evidence both analyses need.

text: Forcing both analyses into one tool call
explanation: One tool call mixes both reasoning chains, which the scenario forbids.

text: State a clear goal and relevant context
explanation: Goal plus context plus constraints plus quality criteria make delegation reliable.

text: List constraints and quality criteria
explanation: Goal plus context plus constraints plus quality criteria make delegation reliable.

text: Provide no task details
explanation: A subagent without task details produces a result the coordinator cannot use.

text: Tell it to use every available tool
explanation: Unlimited tools add risk without addressing the brief; scope should match the task.

text: A prompt chain with sequential stages
explanation: Fixed repeatable sequences fit a prompt chain, not dynamic planning.

text: Unbounded dynamic decomposition
explanation: Dynamic decomposition adds cost and variance to a task with a known fixed sequence.

text: Log only successes, erasing blocked and failed attempts
explanation: Logging only successes erases the blocked and failed attempts the audit is explicitly required to reconstruct.

text: A random subagent selection
explanation: Random selection does not guarantee the required sequence of checks.

text: Parsing prose for completion
explanation: Prose parsing is an unreliable completion signal and unrelated to sequencing checks.

text: Check the synthesis for gaps
explanation: Evaluate the synthesis, then re-route targeted follow-ups instead of inventing results.

text: Send focused follow-up tasks
explanation: Evaluate the synthesis, then re-route targeted follow-ups instead of inventing results.

text: Confirm missing evidence as found
explanation: Treating missing evidence as found fabricates results and hides the gap.

text: End the workflow without recording the gap
explanation: Ending without recording the gap makes the incomplete synthesis look complete.

text: Include "Task" in allowedTools
explanation: The coordinator can only call Task if it is explicitly allowed.

text: Log only final messages, losing tool-level evidence
explanation: Final messages summarize outcomes but drop the per-call evidence — actor, arguments, decisions — needed to reconstruct every attempt.

text: Only the phrase "needs help"
explanation: A bare phrase forces the human to redo the investigation from scratch.

text: Customer ID, escalation reason, and recommended action
explanation: ID plus reason plus recommendation lets the human act without rework or leaking reasoning.

text: The full hidden chain of thought
explanation: Dumping internal reasoning leaks unreviewed content and buries the actionable summary.

text: No findings, so the human restarts
explanation: Withholding findings wastes the work already done and delays resolution.

text: Send multiple Task calls in one coordinator turn
explanation: Parallel Task calls in one turn let independent work run concurrently.

text: Merge all tasks into one vague request
explanation: A merged vague request produces one blended result instead of three independent checks.

text: Wait for end_turn before assigning any task
explanation: Serializing independent tasks wastes the concurrency the scenario needs.

text: Give every subagent the same scope
explanation: Identical scopes duplicate work and produce overlapping results.

text: A pre-execution interception hook
explanation: A pre-execution hook enforces the threshold in code before the tool runs.

text: A polite reminder in the user prompt
explanation: Reminder prompts are advisory and can be ignored; they cannot enforce a threshold.

text: A final-answer formatting rule
explanation: Formatting rules act after execution, when the refund may already have run.

text: An arbitrary retry count
explanation: Retry counts govern retries, not policy thresholds.

text: Inform the agent about the file changes
explanation: Stale findings mislead, so the agent must learn what changed before reuse.

text: Assume old findings are still current
explanation: Assuming currency after source changes risks acting on outdated conclusions.

text: Delete every source file
explanation: Deleting sources destroys the evidence base entirely.

text: Hide the changes from the agent
explanation: Hiding changes guarantees the agent reasons over stale state.

text: Assign distinct coverage areas to reduce duplication
explanation: Distinct scopes minimize duplication and make aggregation clean.

text: Give all subagents the full request unchanged
explanation: Unchanged full requests duplicate work and produce overlapping findings.

text: Let each subagent pick a random topic
explanation: Random topics leave gaps and overlaps the coordinator cannot predict.

text: Avoid aggregating the results
explanation: Without aggregation the pieces never form a complete answer.

text: Identify the separate aspects before assigning tasks
explanation: Mapping all aspects first prevents a narrow plan that misses work.

text: Assign only the first aspect noticed
explanation: Assigning the first noticed aspect leaves the rest of the request unaddressed.

text: Remove all constraints from subagents
explanation: Removing constraints adds risk without widening coverage of the request.

text: Skip task decomposition completely
explanation: Skipping decomposition delegates the whole complexity to one subagent, losing coverage.

text: A single free-form text field
explanation: Free text invites ambiguous identifiers and cannot be validated as a customer reference.

text: A required customer_id field with a defined type
explanation: A required, typed customer_id validates input and avoids ambiguous free text.

text: No input fields
explanation: Without an input field the tool cannot target a specific customer.

text: An optional field named details
explanation: An optional vaguely named field lets calls proceed without a valid identifier.

text: A generic server failure
explanation: A server failure misreports a valid no-match condition as an error.

text: A fabricated invoice
explanation: Fabricating an invoice invents data the system does not contain.

text: A structured empty result
explanation: A structured empty result distinguishes 'no match' from errors and lets the agent proceed.

text: No response
explanation: No response leaves the agent unable to distinguish timeout, failure, or no match.

text: Failure type, attempted query, and retry guidance
explanation: Failure type, attempted query, and retry guidance let the agent decide whether and how to retry.

text: "Tool failed" only
explanation: A bare failure message gives the agent nothing to act on for recovery.

text: An empty success result
explanation: An empty success hides the timeout and prevents a correct retry decision.

text: The original user prompt only
explanation: The original prompt contains no information about the failure or how to retry.

text: To increase prompt length
explanation: Longer prompts add cost; they do not constrain destructive actions.

text: To make errors less visible
explanation: Hiding errors makes destructive mistakes harder to catch, not safer.

text: To let the model infer missing targets
explanation: Inferred targets are exactly how destructive tools hit the wrong records.

text: To reduce unintended actions
explanation: A narrow, explicit schema forces clear targets and reduces accidental destructive actions.

text: Clear purpose, inputs, outputs, and constraints
explanation: Purpose, inputs, outputs, and constraints help the model choose the right tool for the task.

text: A vague name only
explanation: A vague name gives the model no basis to distinguish similar tools.

text: Implementation source code only
explanation: Source code bloats context and describes mechanics, not when to use the tool.

text: No description
explanation: With no description, selection among similar tools is a guess.

text: Remove all tool constraints
explanation: Removing constraints grants unrelated dangerous capabilities just to enable Task.

text: Set stop_reason to end_turn first
explanation: stop_reason is an API response field, not something the application sets to enable tools.

text: Give subagents shared hidden memory
explanation: Subagents do not share hidden memory; context is passed explicitly.

text: When prior results are stale
explanation: A fresh session with a summary drops stale context instead of carrying it forward.

text: Whenever any tool exists
explanation: Tool availability is unrelated to whether prior context is still valid.

text: Only after a successful end_turn
explanation: end_turn completion does not decide whether old context is stale.

text: Never; always resume sessions
explanation: Always resuming carries stale context forward and degrades reliability.

text: Guess the value
explanation: Guessing a high-impact input risks charging the wrong account or the wrong amount.

text: Use the last unrelated value
explanation: An unrelated value is not the missing order ID and will trigger a wrong refund.

text: Call the tool with blank input
explanation: A blank input either fails or applies to an unintended default target.

text: Ask for the missing information
explanation: Guessing high-impact inputs risks wrong actions; asking for missing data is safest.

text: Send many identical requests immediately
explanation: Hammering a rate-limited service extends or escalates the limit.

text: Claim the operation completed
explanation: Claiming completion fabricates a result for work that did not happen.

text: Follow retry guidance or wait before retrying
explanation: Respecting retry guidance or backoff avoids hammering a limited service.

text: Switch to a destructive tool
explanation: Switching to a destructive tool is unrelated to the limit and adds serious risk.

text: Accept any sentence
explanation: Free sentences yield values outside the allowed set and break validation.

text: Infer priority from punctuation
explanation: Punctuation is not a reliable encoding of priority and produces inconsistent results.

text: Define allowed enum values in the schema
explanation: A schema enum constrains input to allowed values and makes validation predictable.

text: Omit the input description
explanation: Without a description the model cannot know valid priority values at all.

text: Resume, refresh live health, and retain unchanged topology
explanation: Only health values are stale while topology holds. The proportionate move resumes the session, explicitly refreshes live health data, and retains unchanged topology findings instead of trusting stalen

text: Trust old health, acting on stale availability
explanation: Acting on stale health values means routing decisions based on availability that may no longer hold, the exact hazard the refresh exists to remove.

text: Discard topology and restart, repeating settled analysis
explanation: Restarting discards still-valid configuration and topology analysis, repeating settled work for no reliability gain.

text: Average old and new health, fabricating a value
explanation: Averaging old and new health readings fabricates a value that matches neither the current nor the prior state, corrupting the basis for action.

text: Rely on model memory, risking duplicate tickets
explanation: Model memory of a prior attempt is not durable state; after the timeout the model can still re-issue the call and create a duplicate ticket.

text: Shorten timeouts and retry faster, multiplying duplicates
explanation: Faster retries increase the number of attempts racing an unknown outcome, multiplying duplicates instead of preventing them.

text: It makes every action irreversible
explanation: Irreversibility is a property of the action, not a benefit of separating tools.

text: It enables different permissions and safety controls
explanation: Separate tools allow different permissions and safety controls for reads versus writes.

text: It removes the need for schemas
explanation: Each tool still needs its own schema regardless of separation.

text: It guarantees faster networks
explanation: Separation has no effect on network speed.

text: Schedule load tests before confirming residency
explanation: Load testing validates performance, not compliance; it neither confirms the residency scope nor fixes a design that may already breach it.

text: Add residency dashboards without confirming scope
explanation: Dashboards observe behavior but cannot change it; without confirming the constraint's actual scope, the system keeps routing data in violation while merely reporting on it.

text: Ask what failure looks like concretely
explanation: Adjectives become requirements via concrete failure cases and one measurable reviewer behavior. Vendor and date questions skip elicitation entirely.

text: Ask which model vendor they prefer
explanation: Vendor preference is a solution constraint, not a requirement; it does not translate the vague adjectives into anything testable.

text: Ask for one measurable reviewer behavior
explanation: Adjectives become requirements via concrete failure cases and one measurable reviewer behavior. Vendor and date questions skip elicitation entirely.

text: Ask for the preferred launch date first
explanation: A launch date is a schedule input, not a requirement definition; it leaves the vague adjectives exactly as ambiguous as before.

text: Record both demands as runtime toggles now
explanation: Implementing toggles defers the risk-tolerance decision into code, so the conflict between legal and product remains unresolved and someone must still choose at runtime.

text: Facilitate risk-tolerance agreement first
explanation: Conflicting mandates are resolved by facilitating explicit risk-tolerance agreement before designing. Recording toggles, imposing one side, or splitting the difference avoids the decision.

text: Always return every internal field
explanation: Returning all fields dilutes attention with data the task does not use.

text: Return a focused structured response
explanation: A focused response with only needed fields saves context and reduces misinterpretation.

text: Return only prose
explanation: Prose loses the structured fields the agent needs to act reliably.

text: Remove all fields
explanation: Removing everything also removes the fields the agent needs.

text: Ask the agent not to delete
explanation: Prompt instructions cannot prevent a delete call; only tool scope can.

text: Expose delete but hide its description
explanation: A hidden-description tool remains callable and undocumented, which is worse.

text: Grant only read-scoped tools
explanation: Read-scoped tools enforce least privilege; prompting alone does not prevent deletes.

text: Send an idempotency key with the request
explanation: Timeouts after side effects need exactly-once mechanics. An idempotency key plus querying operation status before repeating prevents duplicate tickets without disabling all retries.

text: Check operation status before repeating the side effect
explanation: Timeouts after side effects need exactly-once mechanics. An idempotency key plus querying operation status before repeating prevents duplicate tickets without disabling all retries.

text: Stop at a URL count, counting duplicates as coverage
explanation: A URL count treats syndicated duplicates as independent coverage, so the agent can stop while several evidence areas rest on a single underlying article.

text: Stop on model confidence, ignoring provenance diversity
explanation: Self-reported confidence is an unreliable stopping signal and ignores whether sources are independent, letting duplicated coverage look sufficient.

text: Stop on token budget, leaving evidence gaps uncovered
explanation: A token budget measures spending, not evidence coverage, so the agent stops with evidence gaps still unfilled.

text: Stop when evidence categories and independent-source criteria are met
explanation: URL counts and confidence confuse quantity with coverage. Stopping when required evidence categories and independent-source criteria are satisfied handles syndication duplicates and enforces provenanc

text: Increase retry count with the same prompt, repeating deterministic failure.
explanation: Failures repeat identically on identical context, so they are deterministic; more retries with the same prompt just multiply the same failure and grow the ledger.

text: Classify the failure, revise context or method, reroute only if plausible.
explanation: Identical retries repeat deterministic failure; classification plus context/method revision enables plausible recovery.

text: Broadcast every failure to all workers, multiplying cost and inconsistency.
explanation: Broadcasting every failure to every worker multiplies cost and produces inconsistent handling where a targeted classification and reroute would do.

text: Suppress failed tasks from the ledger, publishing false completeness.
explanation: Removing failed tasks from the ledger hides the work that never completed, publishing a false picture of completeness.

text: Early reports consume more tokens, misdiagnosing cost as correctness risk.
explanation: Token consumption is a cost property, not a correctness one; the risk is a draft presenting itself as complete while coverage is still unverified.

text: Fast workers are lower quality, so wait for the slowest indefinitely, stalling delivery.
explanation: Completion speed says nothing about report quality, and waiting indefinitely for the slowest stalls delivery without addressing the actual completeness gate.

text: The draft can claim completeness before required units return or fail declared.
explanation: Streaming early drafts risks completeness claims before all required units return or fail declared.

text: Any intermediate text revokes permission for extra workers, misstating constraints.
explanation: Publishing an intermediate draft does not revoke permission to spawn additional workers; the constraint being violated is the completeness claim, not spawning rights.

text: Renegotiate token price keeping volume intact
explanation: Renegotiating the token price leaves the bloated volume of 9 chunks and 4 retries untouched, so the savings still cannot close the gap to the 3-cent cap.

text: Cut chunks retries turns before repricing
explanation: B cuts volume (chunks, retries, turns) before unit price. Costs: A costs savings on still-bloated volume; B costs recall validation work; C costs vendor churn without measurement; D costs budget theat

text: Change vendors without measuring token volumes
explanation: Changing vendors without measuring token volumes is repricing theater; the per-case cost is driven by work volume that no vendor switch addresses.

text: Retry delete calls slowly
explanation: Slower retries still delete records; the action itself is the problem.

text: Store model weights
explanation: Model weights live with the model provider, not in MCP servers.

text: Expose tools and resources through a standard protocol
explanation: An MCP server standardizes how tools and resources are exposed to models.

text: Replace all application logic
explanation: MCP exposes capabilities; it does not replace the application around the model.

text: Guarantee every tool call succeeds
explanation: No protocol can guarantee success; tools still return errors and timeouts.

text: Redact the secret before returning the result
explanation: Redacting secrets the model does not need prevents leakage into context or answers.

text: Cap monthly spend without changing volumes
explanation: Capping monthly spend without changing volumes either blocks service or hides the overage; the underlying per-case cost stays above the cap.

text: Confirm residency rule before routing design
explanation: A constraint mentioned in passing must be confirmed before routing or storage decisions. Retaining central routing, load testing, or dashboards without confirmation leaves violation intact.

text: Retain central routing and note assumption
explanation: Routing transactions to a central store on an unconfirmed residency assumption risks a data-residency violation that a written note cannot cure.

text: Run load tests before confirming residency
explanation: Load testing measures performance, not legal constraints, so it cannot confirm or resolve the residency question that decides the routing design.

text: Add residency dashboards without confirming scope
explanation: Dashboards only observe outcomes after the fact; they do not confirm the residency rule that must shape the routing decision before it is made.

text: Keep reranker, slip the release date
explanation: The release date is fixed and immovable, so slipping it violates a stated constraint regardless of accuracy or latency gains.

text: Drop reranker, hold 0.92 within p99
explanation: Accuracy clears 0.90 with headroom, but p99 breaches a fixed budget with capped GPUs and date. Trading 0.95 to 0.92 buys p99 with explicit budget.

text: Keep reranker, double GPU spend cap
explanation: Doubling GPU spend breaks the explicitly capped budget, which cannot be traded away to keep the reranker.

text: Add cache, tolerate the p99 breach
explanation: Tolerating the breach leaves a hard p99 budget violated; a cache added under a fixed date cannot be validated in time to close the gap.

text: Stratified accuracy reporting by document type and field
explanation: Aggregate metrics mask segments, so accuracy is measured by document type and field before any automation decision; stratified sampling surfaces the error pattern the 97 percent mean conceals. The cost is segmenting the golden set and its reporting.

text: Add legacy registers until the aggregate score reaches 99
explanation: eval-blindness — more of the same aggregate raises a number that never resolves the buried segment.

text: A/B against a versioned golden set, keeping only non-regressing winners
explanation: Changes ship only when the versioned golden set shows the new prompt winning on tracked metrics without regressing any category. The comparison is reproducible; the trade-off is versioning discipline and golden-set upkeep.

text: Send both prompt versions to a larger model and compare outputs
explanation: scale-not-strategy — a bigger model is an unmeasured, unrelated variable that attributes nothing cleanly to the prompt.

text: Raise the manual spot-check sample from eight up to thirty
explanation: eval-blindness — more ad hoc glances are still unversioned, and the regressed hub was never in the sample.

text: Watch inbound customer complaints for one week at full traffic
explanation: convenience-over-safety — full-traffic exposure makes every traveler absorb the regression while the team waits for signals.

text: Retrain the deployed model on the handbook during the next alignment pass
explanation: scale-not-strategy — training-time alignment is general by design and happens before any deployment, so it never sees the firm's handbook.

text: Trust the refusals observed in testing as proof of handbook coverage
explanation: compliance-theater — observed refusals cover broad harm classes and prove nothing about a specific rule that lives in no layer.

text: Encode the handbook rules as application-layer instructions paired with runtime controls
explanation: The alignment boundary leaves deployment-specific policy to the application layer: trained behavior reduces broad harm but never saw the firm's handbook, so instructions must be paired with screening, authorization, or review, or the rule lives in no layer.

text: Add a system-prompt paragraph summarizing the handbook and close the gap
explanation: prompt-as-guarantee — instructions steer one request but are not enforcement; without a paired control, the steering leaves the rule unenforced.

text: Input screening before the model call and authorization before side effects
explanation: A guarded path has three control points at different places answering different questions; with only output screening, nothing decides whether requests reach the model and nothing authorizes side-effecting actions, which is exactly the payout that executed unchecked.

text: A second judge on the response so toxicity scoring gains redundancy
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — both checks would sit at the same final point; the duplicates still decide nothing about inputs or tool actions.

text: Longer system instructions telling the model when to call the payment tool
explanation: prompt-as-guarantee — instructions steer behavior but do not authorize the payout; the side effect still runs without a permission check.

text: A fail-closed switch that blocks responses whenever the toxicity judge errors
explanation: valid-but-early — worthwhile once the path has more than one control, but it only hardens the single filter already there.

text: Add stronger phrase-matching patterns to the existing user-input screening rules
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — the instructions ride in after input screening has already passed the request, so the entry-point check cannot see them.

text: Pin the supplier list so no new senders reach the model
explanation: convenience-over-safety — a sender allowlist does nothing for instructions embedded inside an approved supplier's own documents.

text: Wrap retrieved documents in quotes so the model treats them as data
explanation: prompt-as-guarantee — marking text as data steers the model's reading but does not enforce which embedded instructions it follows.

text: Screen retrieved content and tool outputs before they enter context
explanation: The dominant injection vector in deployments with retrieval or tool use rides in through retrieved content and tool outputs, so those sources need their own screening pass, with the classifier used on user input, before they are appended to context.

text: Cache the last known-good verdicts and reuse them during screening outages
explanation: stale-fact — reused verdicts describe the previous conversation state, not the unscreened response currently waiting on delivery.

text: Whether the guardrail fails open, passing traffic, or fails closed
explanation: A screening service that errors while traffic keeps flowing gives the appearance of protection without the function; the failure direction is a deliberate architectural choice, because the surrounding code's default almost always lets requests through the unprotected path.

text: Move the screening call after delivery to remove its latency
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — screening after delivery observes nothing; the check exists to decide whether the response is safe to reach the user.

text: Use 2048-token chunks for all sources
explanation: One uniform large chunk size optimizes the already-passing pod manuals while further fragmenting short driver tickets and blurring tariff table rows.

text: Use ticket-level chunks with thread metadata
explanation: Driver tickets need small thread-aware chunks; tariff tables need row-structured indexing. Uniform large chunks optimize the already-passing manuals.

text: Index tariff tables as structured rows
explanation: Driver tickets need small thread-aware chunks; tariff tables need row-structured indexing. Uniform large chunks optimize the already-passing manuals.

text: Merge sources into one flat index
explanation: Merging into one flat index erases the per-source structure that ticket threads and tariff fields need, keeping the failing metrics unchanged.

text: Renegotiate token rate keeping volume fixed
explanation: Renegotiating the token rate is unit-price-only: the wasted volume of chunks and retries stays intact, so the gap to the 3-cent cap barely moves.

text: Deduplicate chunks and cache repeated prefixes
explanation: B/D cut quantity via dedup, caching, and bounded retries; A/C only reprice or scale unchanged volume. Costs: A costs unchanged volume at lower rate; B costs dedup validation; C costs headroom without

text: Raise concurrency limits without volume change
explanation: Raising concurrency moves speed, not cost or latency at the tail, and leaves per-case volume unchanged against the cap.

text: Cap retries with targeted fallback policy
explanation: B/D cut quantity via dedup, caching, and bounded retries; A/C only reprice or scale unchanged volume. Costs: A costs unchanged volume at lower rate; B costs dedup validation; C costs headroom without

text: Check caller roles via prompt instructions
explanation: Prompt instructions are not authorization; privilege checks in prompt text are exactly what allowed the two bypasses.

text: Authorize each payout call server-side
explanation: Bypasses need per-invocation server-side checks; untraceable payouts need I/O spans with outcome labels. Prompt checks and counters do neither.

text: Track aggregate success counters only now
explanation: Aggregate counters hide both failures: they cannot attribute a payout write to an approval or expose a per-call privilege bypass.

text: Trace tool I/O with outcome labels
explanation: Bypasses need per-invocation server-side checks; untraceable payouts need I/O spans with outcome labels. Prompt checks and counters do neither.

text: Single dispatch caller uses direct call
explanation: Single dispatch callers stay direct, shared routing APIs gain one MCP server, and bulk manifest exports stay on CLI scripts. One-shot exception tools and full-catalog injection are unsound.

text: Shared routing API uses one MCP server
explanation: Single dispatch callers stay direct, shared routing APIs gain one MCP server, and bulk manifest exports stay on CLI scripts. One-shot exception tools and full-catalog injection are unsound.

text: Multi-turn exception handling uses one-shot tool
explanation: A one-shot tool cannot deliberate across the multiple turns exception handling requires, so this interaction shape mismatches the tool type.

text: Inject all 150 schemas every turn
explanation: Injecting every schema each turn is monolithic context that bloats tokens and latency instead of loading schemas on demand per intent.

text: Bulk manifest export uses direct CLI script
explanation: Single dispatch callers stay direct, shared routing APIs gain one MCP server, and bulk manifest exports stay on CLI scripts. One-shot exception tools and full-catalog injection are unsound.

text: Searchable catalog loading schemas on demand
explanation: Progressive discovery loads schemas on demand and scopes per intent; full injection and prompt-stuffed secrets are monolithic context.

text: Full 150 schemas injected every turn
explanation: Injecting all 150 schemas each turn is monolithic context: it bloats every request regardless of the current intent.

text: Task-scoped subset injected per intent now
explanation: Progressive discovery loads schemas on demand and scopes per intent; full injection and prompt-stuffed secrets are monolithic context.

text: All runbooks plus secrets in system prompt
explanation: Stuffing runbooks and secrets into the system prompt injects everything on every request — the definition of monolithic context — and leaks secrets besides.

text: Single root rule applied to all paths
explanation: A root-wide rule is what already misfires: it forces one set of conventions across both subsystems with conflicting styles.

text: Personal user override for every developer
explanation: Per-developer overrides fragment the shared baseline and reintroduce the inconsistent habits the monorepo needs to eliminate.

text: Directory CLAUDE.md inside frontend folder
explanation: Subsystem differences call for directory-scoped CLAUDE.md. A root-wide rule would force frontend conventions onto backend code.

text: Standalone slash command run each time
explanation: A slash command is a manual prompt shortcut run on demand, not persistent scoped configuration that applies to the right files automatically.

text: Glob-scoped rule for migration file paths
explanation: High-risk paths need glob-scoped rules that trigger only on migrations. Global rules add friction everywhere else.

text: Global rule applied to every source file
explanation: A global rule applies the backup check to every edit, exactly the slowdown the scenario says is unacceptable.

text: Personal memory entry on each laptop
explanation: Personal memories are per-machine and unenforced, so the mandatory backup check would be inconsistently applied and easily missed.

text: Repeated ad-hoc prompt every review
explanation: Relying on an ad-hoc prompt each review is manual and error-prone; it does not enforce the check automatically on migration edits.

text: Simple slash command prompt shortcut
explanation: A slash command is only a prompt shortcut; it cannot package the scripts, checklist execution, and fixed report format the audit requires.

text: Global CLAUDE.md style rule entry
explanation: A style rule in CLAUDE.md shapes conventions passively; it does not execute a multi-step audit workflow or produce a report artifact.

text: RAG for guides, live API for orders
explanation: Conceptual guides suit semantic RAG with a live order API; exact IDs also need keyword fusion. Snapshots or one index preserve staleness.

text: Fuse BM25 with vectors for identifiers
explanation: Conceptual guides suit semantic RAG with a live order API; exact IDs also need keyword fusion. Snapshots or one index preserve staleness.

text: Snapshot work orders nightly into vectors
explanation: Nightly snapshots are exactly what produces the 24% stale answers; work-order state changes during the day and must be queried live.

text: Use one semantic index for everything
explanation: A single semantic index keeps the exact-ID failure at 0.47 and still serves stale snapshot data for live work orders.

text: Keep long prompt accepting error rate
explanation: Keeping the long prompt accepts a 24% schema violation rate against a 5% bar, failing the quality constraint outright.

text: Route everything to flagship model always
explanation: Routing everything to the flagship model breaks the 2-cent-per-document cost cap, trading one violated constraint for another.

text: Add constraints to same long prompt
explanation: Adding more constraints to an already-too-long prompt compounds the steerability problem for a smaller model that cannot follow it.

text: Simplify prompt fitting smaller model limits
explanation: D fits prompt complexity to the smaller model's instruction-following. Costs: A costs persistent 24% violations; B costs flagship latency and spend; C costs more constraints the model cannot follow; D

text: Compress prompts by five percent only
explanation: A five percent prompt compression shaves marginal time and leaves the three sequential tool calls that actually cause the p99 tail untouched.

text: Truncate every output to fifty tokens
explanation: Truncating every output to fifty tokens sacrifices answer quality across all cases and barely affects the tool-call latency dominating the tail.

text: Parallelize calls then stream partial results
explanation: C attacks the sequential-call tail then streams partials. Costs: A costs effort for negligible p99 gain; B costs accuracy for blind truncation; C costs orchestration complexity; D costs UX masking wit

text: Add spinners masking delays from users
explanation: Spinners change only perceived latency; the p99 breaches the SLO either way because the sequential calls still run in series.

text: Cache prefixes with TTL plus invalidation rules
explanation: A captures repeat savings while bounding staleness. Costs: A costs TTL and invalidation logic; B costs full price on every repeat; C costs silent stale refunds; D costs latency with zero savings.

text: Disable caching paying full price every time
explanation: Disabling caching pays full price on the 45% of repeat cases, forfeiting the cost savings while the safety constraint is never actually at risk.

text: Cache forever without any invalidation controls
explanation: Caching forever serves stale refund policy with no invalidation path, directly violating the binding safety constraint.

text: Re-retrieve everything fresh for each query always
explanation: Re-retrieving everything fresh adds latency and cost on every repeat with zero savings, failing the cost objective the caching was meant to serve.

text: Track lab accuracy demo win rates
explanation: Lab accuracy and demo win rates are lab-side metrics; the 20% override rate shows real users rejecting drafts, so these numbers prove nothing about production acceptance.

text: Monitor uptime average token usage only
explanation: Uptime and token usage measure infrastructure health, not whether users accept the agent's work product.

text: Sample chats for subjective vibe scores
explanation: Subjective vibe scores are not behavioral evidence of acceptance and cannot counter the objective 20% override signal.

text: Track overrides reopens task resolution rates
explanation: D measures overrides, reopens, and resolution as acceptance. Costs: A costs lab optimism while agents override; B costs infrastructure health mistaken for success; C costs vibe scores without outcomes

text: Task success ≥90% with safety violations tracked
explanation: A gates quality plus safety and C gates tail latency plus unit cost. Costs: A costs safety instrumentation; B costs hidden tail risk and spend; C costs latency/cost plumbing; D costs quality-blind inf

text: Average helpfulness score without any cost tracking
explanation: A helpfulness average with no cost tracking misses the per-case cost cap and the p99 bound, and it gates neither safety nor latency.

text: p99 latency bound with per-case cost cap
explanation: A gates quality plus safety and C gates tail latency plus unit cost. Costs: A costs safety instrumentation; B costs hidden tail risk and spend; C costs latency/cost plumbing; D costs quality-blind inf

text: Total tokens and server uptime alone daily
explanation: Token totals and uptime are infrastructure measures that say nothing about task success, safety leaks, latency, or per-case cost.

text: Reuse demo cases with exact-match grading
explanation: Reusing demo cases keeps the clean-invoice over-representation and exact-match grading cannot assess forged layouts or safety denials.

text: Weight cases by production failure frequency
explanation: B fixes coverage with failure-weighted sampling; D fixes grading with code plus human review. Costs: A costs inflated demo scores; B costs curation effort; C costs similarity scores missing safety; D

text: Grade safety denials with similarity scores only
explanation: Similarity scores like BLEU cannot judge the safety correctness of refund denials, leaving the highest-stakes outputs graded by proxy.

text: Pair code checks with human safety review
explanation: B fixes coverage with failure-weighted sampling; D fixes grading with code plus human review. Costs: A costs inflated demo scores; B costs curation effort; C costs similarity scores missing safety; D

text: Randomize assignment isolating one single variable
explanation: A enforces randomization with one isolated variable; D confirms on untouched held-out data. Costs: A costs traffic and router work; B costs time-confounded comparisons; C costs overfit selection; D co

text: Run variant mornings variant evenings separately
explanation: Splitting variants across morning and evening traffic re-introduces the weekly seasonality as a confound, invalidating the comparison.

text: Select winner using the tuning dataset
explanation: Selecting the winner on the tuning dataset overfits selection to data the variants were developed against, so the 87% bar is not credibly tested.

text: Confirm winner on held-out evaluation set
explanation: A enforces randomization with one isolated variable; D confirms on untouched held-out data. Costs: A costs traffic and router work; B costs time-confounded comparisons; C costs overfit selection; D co

text: Tune generator before measuring retrieval recall
explanation: Tuning the generator before measuring retrieval recall risks optimizing the wrong stage while the logs still cannot attribute the misses.

text: Test generator on gold-standard retrieved context
explanation: B isolates retrieval via gold context; C isolates instruction-following via prompt-only probes. Costs: A costs tuning the wrong stage; B costs rerun effort; C costs baseline construction; D costs two

text: Probe model using prompt-only baseline cases
explanation: B isolates retrieval via gold context; C isolates instruction-following via prompt-only probes. Costs: A costs tuning the wrong stage; B costs rerun effort; C costs baseline construction; D costs two

text: Change retriever prompt simultaneously right now
explanation: Changing retriever and prompt simultaneously entangles both stages, so the 32% miss rate stays unattributable.

text: Reduce chunks and cap retry loops
explanation: A cuts chunks and retries; C bounds agentic turns with early stops. Costs: A costs recall validation; B costs discount theater on bloated volume; C costs stop-rule tuning; D costs blind quality loss.

text: Chase small discount retaining full volume
explanation: A 10% discount on a 10-cent cost only reaches 9 cents, nowhere near the 3-cent cap, because the wasted volume of chunks and retries is untouched.

text: Bound tool turns with early-stop rules
explanation: A cuts chunks and retries; C bounds agentic turns with early stops. Costs: A costs recall validation; B costs discount theater on bloated volume; C costs stop-rule tuning; D costs blind quality loss.

text: Truncate outputs blindly across all cases
explanation: Blind truncation degrades answer quality on every case without addressing the retry and chunk inflation driving the cost.

text: Code assertions verify JSON schema fields
explanation: A is sound for structured JSON; C is sound for rubric-graded tone; E is sound with humans calibrating safety edges. Costs: A/C/E cost pipeline and sampling effort; B costs BLEU missing safety; D costs

text: BLEU scores grade refund safety decisions
explanation: BLEU measures textual similarity, not safety correctness, so it cannot grade refund denial decisions and will silently pass unsafe outputs.

text: Judge rubric scores apology tone quality
explanation: A is sound for structured JSON; C is sound for rubric-graded tone; E is sound with humans calibrating safety edges. Costs: A/C/E cost pipeline and sampling effort; B costs BLEU missing safety; D costs

text: Humans grade every nightly regression case
explanation: Human-grading all 800 nightly cases does not scale, and it wastes scarce reviewer time that sampled-edge calibration already covers.

text: Humans adjudicate sampled safety edge cases
explanation: A is sound for structured JSON; C is sound for rubric-graded tone; E is sound with humans calibrating safety edges. Costs: A/C/E cost pipeline and sampling effort; B costs BLEU missing safety; D costs

text: Lab accuracy alone proves user acceptance
explanation: Lab accuracy is a vanity signal here: the 17% override rate shows users rejecting drafts despite the 91% lab score.

text: Override rate flags rejected agent drafts
explanation: B/C/E reveal acceptance via overrides, reopens, and resolution. Costs: A costs lab-only optimism; B/C/E cost downstream event plumbing; D costs infrastructure health mistaken for task success.

text: Ticket reopen rate signals unresolved work
explanation: B/C/E reveal acceptance via overrides, reopens, and resolution. Costs: A costs lab-only optimism; B/C/E cost downstream event plumbing; D costs infrastructure health mistaken for task success.

text: Server uptime alone proves task success
explanation: Uptime measures service availability, not whether users' tasks actually got resolved, so it cannot evidence acceptance.

text: Resolution rate confirms completed user goals
explanation: B/C/E reveal acceptance via overrides, reopens, and resolution. Costs: A costs lab-only optimism; B/C/E cost downstream event plumbing; D costs infrastructure health mistaken for task success.

text: Add searchable tool discovery on demand
explanation: On-demand discovery plus per-intent scoping fix tokens and misrouting together. Bigger windows or retries preserve the bloated context.

text: Inject full catalog into bigger window
explanation: Enlarging the window to fit all 150 schemas keeps the full catalog in every prompt, so token bloat and wrong-tool selection both persist.

text: Inject task-scoped tool subsets only
explanation: On-demand discovery plus per-intent scoping fix tokens and misrouting together. Bigger windows or retries preserve the bloated context.

text: Retry wrong-tool calls automatically always
explanation: Automatic retries act after a wrong-tool call has already happened; they reduce neither the 42k-token prompts nor the 18% misrouting rate.

text: Keep bulk exports on direct CLI script
explanation: One-off pipeline callers stay direct and bulk exports stay on CLI scripts, while eight billing tenants share one MCP server. Wrapping the single caller or chatting exports adds latency.

text: Publish one MCP server for billing
explanation: One-off pipeline callers stay direct and bulk exports stay on CLI scripts, while eight billing tenants share one MCP server. Wrapping the single caller or chatting exports adds latency.

text: Wrap single transcode caller in MCP server
explanation: A single caller gains no reuse from an MCP wrapper, and the added hop plus new host risks the fixed Friday ship date.

text: Route nightly exports through chat agent
explanation: Unattended bulk jobs need no conversational surface; pushing 50GB nightly exports through a chat agent adds overhead with no interaction benefit.

text: Set a stricter confidence threshold so the judge blocks more responses
explanation: knobs-not-design — a threshold trades false positives for coverage; it says nothing about what happens when the screening dependency itself errors.

text: Live inventory uses nightly vector snapshot
explanation: Inventory is live state that changes during the day, so a nightly snapshot serves stale answers exactly when availability matters.

text: Exact shipment IDs use hybrid keyword-vector path
explanation: Shipment IDs need hybrid paths, privileged calls need per-invocation server checks, and incidents need I/O traces with outcomes. Snapshots and prompt trust fail.

text: Trust tenant tier asserted in prompt text
explanation: A tier asserted inside prompt text is client-supplied and spoofable; identity must come from a verified server-side layer instead.

text: Authorize each privileged call server-side now
explanation: Shipment IDs need hybrid paths, privileged calls need per-invocation server checks, and incidents need I/O traces with outcomes. Snapshots and prompt trust fail.

text: Trace tool I/O with outcome labels
explanation: Shipment IDs need hybrid paths, privileged calls need per-invocation server checks, and incidents need I/O traces with outcomes. Snapshots and prompt trust fail.

text: Each developer personal CLAUDE.md file
explanation: Personal files fragment the baseline: each developer keeps different habits, which is the very problem the team wants to eliminate.

text: Versioned shared project CLAUDE.md file
explanation: Team conventions must be versioned and shared, so they belong in project CLAUDE.md. User-level config is for personal preferences only.

text: Private chat transcripts shared by leads
explanation: Chat transcripts are unstructured, unversioned, and not read by the tool, so they cannot act as an enforced shared baseline.

text: Local IDE defaults kept fully unversioned
explanation: Unversioned local defaults drift per machine and cannot be centrally updated or shared across the ten developers.

text: Enter plan mode to align the approach
explanation: Ambiguous scope plus high blast radius demands plan mode alignment first. Direct execution locks in untested assumptions.

text: Execute the full refactor directly now
explanation: Executing directly on an unclear-boundary legacy module locks in untested assumptions and risks breaking payments with no agreed approach.

text: Generate broad new files immediately
explanation: Generating broad new files before understanding the module's boundaries multiplies the blast radius and duplicates the old behavior blindly.

text: Skip tests for faster initial iteration
explanation: Skipping tests on payment logic removes the only safety net during a high-risk change, trading short-term speed for unverified correctness.

text: Open formal plan mode for alignment
explanation: Plan mode is for large ambiguous changes; a single-file typo with known expected text needs no alignment overhead.

text: Draft design doc before any change
explanation: A design doc for a one-line typo fix is pure overhead; the change is fully understood before any work begins.

text: Edit directly then run focused tests
explanation: A small well-understood fix does not need plan overhead. Direct execution with tests is faster and sufficient.

text: Schedule architecture review before fixing
explanation: An architecture review cannot improve a single error-message typo and stalls a trivial fix behind a heavyweight process.

text: Store team command in user home only
explanation: A user-home command is personal to one machine, so other squads never discover or share the /new-service definition.

text: Store command in project commands directory
explanation: Team commands must be project-scoped with descriptive frontmatter and parameters. User-scoped or undescribed commands do not scale.

text: Omit description to keep files shorter
explanation: Without a description the command is undiscoverable — users cannot see what it does or when to invoke it in the command list.

text: Add frontmatter with args and description
explanation: Team commands must be project-scoped with descriptive frontmatter and parameters. User-scoped or undescribed commands do not scale.

text: Generate full code then add tests later
explanation: Generating code first bakes in whatever rounding behavior the model produced; tests written afterward tend to assert that behavior instead of the spec.

text: Write failing test then minimal code
explanation: TDD uses a tight failing-test loop with minimal implementation. Generating all code first defeats regression protection.

text: Copy similar tests without running them
explanation: Copied tests that are never run prove nothing; they may not compile, may not match the helper's contract, and provide no regression safety.

text: Skip red phase to save iteration time
explanation: Skipping the red phase means the test is never shown to fail, so it may pass vacuously and never actually guard the rounding behavior.

text: Run interactive session with open prompts
explanation: An interactive session blocks forever when an approval prompt appears with no developer present — the exact hang already happening in CI.

text: Pause pipeline awaiting developer input
explanation: Pausing for input overnight leaves runners idle and queues builds, which is the current failure mode rather than a fix.

text: Reuse personal login session in CI
explanation: A personal login in CI is an unmanaged credential with broad rights; it does not solve prompting and violates least-privilege for runners.

text: Run headless with fixed permissions flags
explanation: CI must run headless with explicit permissions and timeouts. Interactive prompts hang runners indefinitely.

text: Comment on every possible style nit
explanation: Commenting on every nit multiplies the trivial-comment flood that made developers ignore the reviewer in the first place.

text: Repost identical findings on each commit
explanation: Reposting duplicate findings on every commit adds noise without new signal, burying real defects further.

text: Tier severity and suppress low confidence
explanation: Precision comes from scoped rules, severity tiers, and suppressing low-confidence findings. More comments without tuning increases ignore rates.

text: Run review without scoping any paths
explanation: Unscoped review ranges over everything and surfaces more marginal findings, increasing the false-positive flood that eroded trust.

text: Permission allowlist entry for shell
explanation: An allowlist entry only grants permission to run commands; it carries none of the audit procedure or report contract.

text: Packaged Skill with helper scripts
explanation: Executable multi-step workflows with scripts belong in a Skill. A slash command alone is only a prompt shortcut.

text: Auto-allow scoped test and format tools
explanation: Allowlist safe, reversible tools and gate destructive ones. Broad auto-allow or disabling prompts trades safety for speed.

text: Auto-allow shell deletion and force push
explanation: Auto-allowing deletion and force push repeats last quarter's outage: destructive, hard-to-reverse actions must require approval, not frictionless access.

text: Require approval for destructive database drops
explanation: Allowlist safe, reversible tools and gate destructive ones. Broad auto-allow or disabling prompts trades safety for speed.

text: Disable all permission prompts team-wide
explanation: Disabling prompts removes the only guardrail on destructive commands, repeating the outage with no human checkpoint at all.

text: Pin exact Claude agent version in CI
explanation: Pin versions, run non-interactive, and gate risky merges by humans. Auto-merge on bot approval and secret leakage are failures.

text: Run agents in non-interactive CI mode
explanation: Pin versions, run non-interactive, and gate risky merges by humans. Auto-merge on bot approval and secret leakage are failures.

text: Auto-merge whenever bot review passes
explanation: Bot-passed auto-merge removes the human gate on irreversible merges, which is how the silent risky merges already slipped through.

text: Paste production secrets into prompts
explanation: Secrets pasted into prompts leak into logs, transcripts, and model context; credentials must stay in secret stores injected at runtime.

text: Require human gate for risky migrations
explanation: Pin versions, run non-interactive, and gate risky merges by humans. Auto-merge on bot approval and secret leakage are failures.

text: Anchor tests on spec plus edge cases
explanation: Tests must be anchored on the specification and edge cases, not on current code. Mirroring buggy output bakes bugs in.

text: Mirror current code output as oracle
explanation: Using current output as the oracle asserts the rounding bug as expected behavior, which is exactly how the generated tests already missed it.

text: Maximize line coverage without assertions
explanation: Coverage without assertions executes code but checks nothing, so the rounding bug would pass untouched no matter how much is covered.

text: Accept generated tests without review
explanation: Accepting generated tests unreviewed leaves the spec-mirroring problem in place; a human must check tests against the spec and edge cases.

text: Freeform prompt written per incident
explanation: Per-incident freeform prompts are the source of the divergence; each operator's improvised steps guarantee different resolutions.

text: Packaged Skill embedding runbook checks
explanation: On-call needs a packaged Skill embedding the runbook, checks, and escalation. Freeform prompting varies by operator.

text: Personal user memory from last on-call
explanation: A personal memory is one operator's recollection on one machine; it cannot standardize the response across the whole on-call rotation.

text: Global style rule describing incidents
explanation: A style rule governs code conventions passively; it does not execute the incident runbook steps or enforce escalation paths.

text: Team standards stored in home directory
explanation: A home directory is per-user storage; team standards placed there become personal configuration that never reaches the rest of the team.

text: Personal aliases stored in user config
explanation: Personal prefs belong in user config; executable workflows belong in Skills. Team standards do not belong in home dirs, nor do one-shot prompts replace Skills.

text: Multi-step audit as one-shot prompt
explanation: A one-shot prompt cannot carry the state, scripts, and step sequencing an executable multi-step audit needs to run reliably.

text: Executable audit workflow as Skill
explanation: Personal prefs belong in user config; executable workflows belong in Skills. Team standards do not belong in home dirs, nor do one-shot prompts replace Skills.

text: Reproduce the failure before changing code
explanation: Reproduce first, change one variable at a time, and keep observability context. Fix-first or unreviewed generated fixes hide causes.

text: Apply generated fix before any reproduction
explanation: Applying a fix before reproduction is guesswork; without a repro you cannot tell whether the fix addressed the real cause or even changed anything.

text: Change one variable per test iteration
explanation: Reproduce first, change one variable at a time, and keep observability context. Fix-first or unreviewed generated fixes hide causes.

text: Commit AI fixes without human review
explanation: Committing AI fixes unreviewed repeats the past failures: unverified changes reach the codebase with no human accountable checkpoint.

text: Attach logs and traces to debug context
explanation: Reproduce first, change one variable at a time, and keep observability context. Fix-first or unreviewed generated fixes hide causes.

text: Token-budget exhaustion — replay archived audit logs to reconstruct past requests
explanation: scale-not-strategy — replaying logs documents what happened; it neither caps padded archived scans nor watches the budget they consume.

text: Indirect prompt injection — treat the retrieved archive text as untrusted before screening
explanation: Retrieved content carries instructions the model treats as trusted; mitigation is to treat that text as untrusted and screen tool and content inputs, not just the citizen's typed question.

text: Direct prompt injection — the audit log records every request the user makes
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — logging observes the request after the fact; only input screening stands between the user's override and the model.

text: A prototype residents can react to in usability tests
explanation: valid-but-early — testing a sketch feels productive, yet it duplicates what the four question buckets would have established earlier.

text: Build minimal reproduction script first
explanation: Reproduce first, then narrow with traces and bisect. Rewriting or broadening scope before isolation wastes effort and hides cause.

text: Rewrite service before isolating the cause
explanation: Rewriting before isolating the trigger risks re-creating the same bug in new code and discards the evidence in the working service.

text: Broaden refactor across unrelated modules
explanation: Broadening scope across unrelated modules mixes unrelated changes with the investigation, making attribution of the latency spike impossible.

text: Narrow scope using traces and bisect runs
explanation: Reproduce first, then narrow with traces and bisect. Rewriting or broadening scope before isolation wastes effort and hides cause.

text: Allow all network access permanently
explanation: Permanent unrestricted network access removes security's control entirely, violating the constraint the denial exists to protect.

text: Deny installs and break the build
explanation: A blanket deny keeps the builds broken and releases stalled, satisfying security but failing the operational need for the registry.

text: Share personal credentials across runners
explanation: Shared personal credentials are an unmanaged, unauditable secret with broad rights; they solve neither governance nor traceability.

text: Scope registry exception with audit log
explanation: Resolve with a narrowly scoped exception plus audit, not a global allow or a blocking deny. Both extremes fail one constraint.

text: Record success criteria and rollback plan
explanation: Plans need explicit success criteria and rollback plus phased steps. Log dumps or immediate execution skip the alignment value.

text: Attach raw log dumps without success criteria
explanation: Raw log dumps without defined criteria give no shared definition of done, which is exactly why the migration keeps restarting.

text: Break work into phased verifiable steps
explanation: Plans need explicit success criteria and rollback plus phased steps. Log dumps or immediate execution skip the alignment value.

text: Skip planning and execute directly now
explanation: Skipping planning reproduces the churn: without agreed phases and done criteria, the migration restarts yet again.

text: Paste only the suspect function text
explanation: Code review of the function alone already showed no defect; the fault only appears under load, so code text cannot contain the answer.

text: Ask for broad rewrite without evidence
explanation: Requesting a rewrite with no evidence guesses at a cause that code review already failed to reveal, risking new defects without fixing the timeout.

text: Feed logs, metrics, traces with scope
explanation: Operational faults need logs, metrics, and traces bounding the prompt. Code-only context misses environment and timing causes.

text: Retry same prompt with higher temperature
explanation: Raising temperature only randomizes responses; without load evidence the model still lacks the data the dashboards hold.

text: Block the refund tool unless session state holds a verified ID, adding one state check.
explanation: Refunds executed because verification was prompt-only and post-use. The fix is a deterministic pre-use gate on verified customer ID in session state; text parsing is spoofable and caps do not enforce

text: Parse assistant text for a verified token before continuing, risking spoofed text bypass.
explanation: Parsing assistant text for a verified token is spoofable, because the model can generate a fake 'verified' token; this adds no deterministic guarantee that identity was actually checked in state.

text: Stop the loop on any tool request, adding latency and breaking valid refund flows.
explanation: Stopping the loop on any tool request blocks every legitimate tool call, adds latency, and breaks valid refund flows; it does nothing to enforce identity verification.

text: Cap iterations at three to limit skips, leaving unverified refunds still executable.
explanation: Capping iterations only limits loop length; it does not gate the refund on verified identity, so unverified refunds remain fully executable within the cap.

text: Raise the cap and continue in the same context, keeping degraded recall and higher cost.
explanation: Raising the cap keeps the agent in the same degraded long context, so recall loss and cost grow rather than recovering; the fix is persisting findings and delegating to fresh agents.

text: Replace investigation with a fixed pipeline, losing adaptivity for unexpected findings.
explanation: A fixed pipeline strips the investigation of its adaptive loop, so unexpected findings can no longer redirect the work; it sidesteps the recall degradation instead of fixing it.

text: Persist findings and delegate remainder to fresh agents, ending on model completion.
explanation: Degradation comes from long-context recall loss, not the cap value. Persist findings, delegate remainder to fresh agents, and stop on model completion; raising the cap keeps degraded recall and cost.

text: Compress every result to one line after each call, discarding decisive investigation evidence.
explanation: Compressing every result to one line destroys decisive investigation evidence, so later synthesis loses exactly the detail the recall problem threatened.

text: Pass no context since subagents inherit history, causing blind re-investigation.
explanation: Subagents do not inherit coordinator history, so passing no context leaves the subagent blindly re-investigating everything instead of targeting the known inconsistency.

text: Pass only the summary without file evidence, forcing unverifiable conclusions.
explanation: A summary without the underlying file outputs is unverifiable, forcing the subagent to draw conclusions it cannot check against evidence.

text: Pass relevant file outputs plus the inconsistency in a structured prompt.
explanation: Fresh subagents do not inherit coordinator history. They need relevant per-file outputs plus the specific inconsistency framed in a structured prompt; summaries without evidence force unverifiable con

text: Force a first tool call with no prior findings, adding latency without direction.
explanation: Forcing a first tool call with no prior findings redoes work already completed and adds latency without giving the subagent direction about the inconsistency.

text: Assign two more reviewers to grade the same five cases
explanation: gold-plating — duplicating painstaking effort raises gating cost while coverage remains five items.

text: Lists the prior research inputs it actually consumed.
explanation: Plausible results hide missing inputs. Require each subagent to declare consumed inputs, sources, and coverage/gaps. Double execution doubles cost and sequential execution kills parallelism without gu

text: Names the sources consulted for its reported findings.
explanation: Plausible results hide missing inputs. Require each subagent to declare consumed inputs, sources, and coverage/gaps. Double execution doubles cost and sequential execution kills parallelism without gu

text: States coverage and gaps versus its assignment.
explanation: Plausible results hide missing inputs. Require each subagent to declare consumed inputs, sources, and coverage/gaps. Double execution doubles cost and sequential execution kills parallelism without gu

text: Runs every task twice to guarantee completeness, doubling cost.
explanation: Running every task twice doubles cost and still cannot reveal which inputs were skipped; explicit declarations of consumed inputs, sources, and coverage gaps are what make incompleteness detectable.

text: Runs all tasks sequentially to guarantee completeness, adding latency.
explanation: Sequential execution sacrifices parallelism and still cannot detect an omitted prior input inside a plausible result; declared coverage and gaps, not reordering, expose the incompleteness.

text: Gate assessment on verified identity state before using retrieval results.
explanation: Order and handoff quality need two deterministic controls: gate assessment on verified state and validate the 3-field escalation payload before submission. Prompt examples and chaining improve style b

text: Validate the escalation payload with all three fields before submission.
explanation: Order and handoff quality need two deterministic controls: gate assessment on verified state and validate the 3-field escalation payload before submission. Prompt examples and chaining improve style b

text: Add prompt instructions plus a handoff example, leaving spoofed order possible.
explanation: Prompt instructions and examples are probabilistic, so a spoofed or skipped verification can still reorder the flow; deterministic order needs a state gate and validated payload.

text: Use fixed prompt chaining and trust each prompt to enforce order and format.
explanation: Fixed prompt chaining trusts each prompt to enforce order and format, but prompts are bypassable, leaving spoofed ordering and malformed handoffs possible.

text: Resume the old session and reread only the schema, keeping stale assumptions.
explanation: Resuming the old session carries two-week-old stale schema assumptions; rereading only the schema does not correct the invalid references already baked into the context.

text: Start fresh with valid decisions, the new schema, and an explicit change list.
explanation: Two-week-old schema references are stale; resuming, forking, or compacting preserves invalid assumptions. Start fresh with valid decisions, the new schema, and an explicit change list.

text: Fork the stale session to explore the new schema, carrying over invalid context.
explanation: Forking copies the stale session, so invalid schema references are carried into the new branch instead of being replaced by the current schema.

text: Compact the old session before resuming, preserving outdated schema references.
explanation: Compaction summarizes old context but preserves its outdated schema references, so invalid assumptions survive into the resumed work.

text: Early synthesis improves latency with no completeness risk to the final answer.
explanation: Synthesizing after only the first result is inherently incomplete because the other parallel results have not returned, so the latency gain produces a wrong final answer.

text: The loop cannot continue because parallel tool calls are architecturally unsupported.
explanation: Parallel tool calls are fully supported; the turn simply completes once all results are incorporated, so architecture is not the limitation here.

text: A later automatic synthesis always overwrites the early partial synthesis result.
explanation: There is no mechanism that automatically overwrites an early partial synthesis; the actual problem is that early synthesis stays incomplete until all results return.

text: Early synthesis is incomplete; wait until all results arrive and the turn ends.
explanation: Three parallel tools in one turn complete only when all results are incorporated and the model ends the turn. Early custom synthesis after the first result is incomplete; later synthesis does not auto

text: Block amounts above $5,000 before tool execution for deterministic safety.
explanation: Safety needs a pre-use block above $5,000; resilience needs local retry of transient timeouts inside the subagent. Prompt-only thresholds are bypassable, post-checks act too late, and escalating every

text: Retry transaction-service timeouts locally inside the subagent for resilience.
