explanation: Safety needs a pre-use block above $5,000; resilience needs local retry of transient timeouts inside the subagent. Prompt-only thresholds are bypassable, post-checks act too late, and escalating every

text: Put the threshold in the prompt and retry timeouts via a post-use hook.
explanation: A prompt-stated threshold is probabilistic and bypassable, and a post-use hook retries only after the failure has already leaked; safety needs a pre-use block and local in-subagent retry.

text: Check the threshold after refund and escalate every timeout upward immediately.
explanation: Checking the amount after the refund executes lets over-limit refunds complete, and escalating every transient timeout discards cheap local retries that would have succeeded.

text: Move normalization before tool execution, leaving old raw values still mixed.
explanation: Moving normalization before execution does not touch the already-recorded raw values, so old and new formats remain mixed and misordering persists.

text: Restart with the hook active or reissue queries so every result is normalized.
explanation: The hook only normalizes new results; old raw timestamps remain, so mixed formats misorder. Restart with the hook active or reissue queries so every result is normalized; moving normalization pre-exec

text: Tell the model to assume old values are ISO 8601, risking silent misordering.
explanation: Telling the model to assume old values are ISO 8601 is a probabilistic guess; wrong assumptions produce silent misordering instead of true normalization.

text: Route production failures into a weekly human grading queue
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — grading failures after production turns misses into reports, not gates for the next release.

text: Rewrite the full conversation each iteration via another hook, adding heavy cost.
explanation: Rewriting the entire conversation each iteration is disproportionately expensive and remains a prompt-level workaround rather than normalizing the actual data.

text: Uniform checks across 60 files -> chained convention checks. [Set: chained / focused / single / fan-out]
explanation: Uniform checks scale via chained convention checks; the coupled 8-file dataflow needs separate focused integration. A single open investigation blurs concerns and 60-way fan-out explodes synthesis cos

text: Include it for completeness
explanation: Including the key puts a credential into model context where it can be exposed.

text: Put it in the final answer
explanation: Emitting the key in output leaks the credential to the user and logs.

text: Ask the model to ignore it
explanation: Instructions to ignore content do not remove it from context or logs.

text: Record ID, action taken, and resulting status
explanation: Record ID, action, and resulting status make mutations traceable and auditable.

text: Only "done"
explanation: A bare confirmation cannot be traced to a specific record or change.

text: The entire database
explanation: Returning the whole database is excessive, slow, and exposes unrelated records.

text: No result after mutation
explanation: A mutation with no result leaves the agent and auditors blind to what happened.

text: Retry without tracking the request
explanation: Retries without request tracking create duplicate charges after ambiguous failures.

text: Use an idempotency key
explanation: An idempotency key lets safe retries reuse the same request instead of double-charging.

text: Hide the network error
explanation: Hiding the error hides the ambiguity that causes double charges.

text: Return a fake success
explanation: A fake success may report a payment that never happened.

text: A human-style apology
explanation: An apology carries no machine-checkable status.

text: A random text message
explanation: Random text gives the agent no reliable success signal.

text: An explicit status field with structured data
explanation: An explicit status plus structured data lets the agent branch reliably on outcomes.

text: A blank response
explanation: A blank response is indistinguishable from failure or timeout.

text: In the user prompt
explanation: Credentials in prompts leak into context, logs, and possibly answers.

text: In every tool response
explanation: Echoing credentials in responses exposes them to every consumer of the result.

text: Inside the tool description
explanation: Tool descriptions are sent to the model on every call; embedding keys there leaks them.

text: In secure server-side configuration
explanation: Server-side configuration keeps credentials out of prompts, descriptions, and responses.

text: Return a validation error before execution
explanation: Failing fast with a validation error avoids executing with bad or missing data.

text: Silently coerce it to an unrelated value
explanation: Silent coercion fabricates an input value and schedules the wrong slot.

text: Execute with missing data
explanation: Executing with invalid data produces unreliable or harmful outcomes.

text: Ask another tool to invent input
explanation: Inventing input fabricates data instead of correcting the request.

text: A hidden comment
explanation: Hidden metadata is not reliably visible to the model and can be dropped by tooling.

text: A success flag only
explanation: A success flag does not indicate whether results are complete or truncated.

text: A random warning string
explanation: Unstructured warning text is easy to miss and hard to branch on.

text: A truncated flag and retrieval guidance
explanation: A truncated flag with retrieval guidance tells the agent results are partial and how to get more.

text: Run automatically whenever mentioned
explanation: Running on casual mention triggers unintended production changes.

text: Require explicit confirmation or a deliberate action
explanation: Explicit confirmation prevents accidental production changes from ambiguous mentions.

text: Accept a best-effort target guess
explanation: Best-effort guessing on production data is how wrong records get modified.

text: Skip logging to improve speed
explanation: Skipping logging removes the audit trail for production changes.

text: Impose strict legal review as binding rule
explanation: Unilaterally siding with legal ignores product's autonomy mandate and forfeits the architect's role as facilitator of an explicit stakeholder agreement.

text: Split the difference with partial sampling now
explanation: A compromise sampling rate is an arbitrary middle that neither stakeholder agreed to, leaving both mandates nominally violated and the risk decision implicit.

text: Keep both tools and steer compliance searches via prompt preference.
explanation: Prompt preferences cannot fix the underlying problem: the two overlapping tool descriptions still leave the model to guess which applies, and a silent success with empty results during an archive outage would still trigger the refund. Steering by prose leaves both failure modes untouched.

text: Split the tools by scope and return a structured access error on outage.
explanation: Overlapping tools cause misrouting, and silent success on outage causes the refund cascade. Differentiated tools plus a structured access error fix both routing and failure semantics.

text: Force the archive tool for every compliance-related user message.
explanation: Forcing a tool guarantees it is called but does nothing about the overlapping descriptions that cause misrouting, and it still lets an unreachable archive surface as success with empty results. The refund cascade would continue unchanged.

text: 8-file dataflow change -> focused separate integration. [Set: chained / focused / single / fan-out]
explanation: Uniform checks scale via chained convention checks; the coupled 8-file dataflow needs separate focused integration. A single open investigation blurs concerns and 60-way fan-out explodes synthesis cos

text: All files plus dataflow -> single open-ended investigation. [Set: chained / focused / single / fan-out]
explanation: One open-ended investigation mixes uniform convention checks with the coupled cross-file dataflow change, blurring concerns and producing neither reliable checks nor focused integration.

text: All 60 files -> 60 parallel agents with one-pass synthesis. [Set: chained / focused / single / fan-out]
explanation: Spawning 60 parallel agents for uniform checks explodes synthesis cost; uniform convention work scales better with chained checks, keeping the dataflow pass separate.

text: Explore both sequentially in one session, forcing costly mental backtracking.
explanation: Exploring both strategies sequentially in one session forces costly mental backtracking and risks cross-contaminating the two branches' findings.

text: Start two sessions from scratch without the shared analysis, redoing prior work.
explanation: Two from-scratch sessions discard the shared analysis, redoing work a fork would have preserved and adding cost without improving comparison quality.

text: Keep one path in the parent and delegate only the other, biasing comparison.
explanation: Keeping one path in the parent biases the comparison: the parent-held path gets richer context and attention than the delegated one.

text: Fork the shared context into two branches and synthesize their outputs.
explanation: Both strategies need the shared analysis without cross-contamination. Fork the shared context into two branches and synthesize outputs; sequential exploration forces backtracking and scratch sessions

text: Monitoring dashboards and sampling plans
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Eval suite plus agreed trade-offs
explanation: Design owes evals and agreed trade-offs before handoff planning. Load tests and rollback plans belong to the handoff gate, not discovery.

text: Rollback plan and on-call rotation
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Retraining cadence and data contracts
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Restrict tools to read and write only, removing email exfiltration risk.
explanation: Least privilege plus state gating is required: restrict tools to read/write only and gate writes on recorded scan completion. Prompt-only email bans are bypassable and checking after reading without g

text: Gate writes on recorded scan-completion state before any save occurs.
explanation: Least privilege plus state gating is required: restrict tools to read/write only and gate writes on recorded scan completion. Prompt-only email bans are bypassable and checking after reading without g

text: Allow email but forbid it in the prompt, leaving exfiltration still possible.
explanation: A prompt prohibition leaves the email tool attached, so exfiltration remains technically possible; least privilege requires removing the capability, not asking the model to avoid it.

text: Check completeness after reading without gating writes, allowing early saves.
explanation: Checking completeness only after reading provides no enforcement, so the subagent can still save before the scan completes; writes must be gated on recorded scan-completion state.

text: Parse assistant text for a pass phrase before deploy, risking spoofed approval.
explanation: Assistant text is generated and spoofable, so a pass phrase proves nothing about the actual test result; deploy must gate on the recorded tool success.

text: Gate deploy on a recorded success result from the test tool execution.
explanation: Text parsing for 'tests passed' is spoofable and ordering definitions does not enforce results. Gate deploy on a recorded success result from the test tool; caps control length, not dependencies.

text: Order tool definitions so deploy appears after test, without checking results.
explanation: The order of tool definitions has no effect on execution ordering or dependencies, so deploy can still run before a successful test.

text: Use an iteration cap so deploy cannot occur too early, ignoring test outcome.
explanation: An iteration cap limits loop length only; it cannot express a dependency on the test tool's outcome, so deploy can still precede a test pass.

text: Discard the session and reconstruct from memory, losing provenance and accuracy.
explanation: Reconstructing a three-day investigation from memory loses provenance and detail, degrading accuracy even though the facts are still current.

text: Fork the full long context without reducing it, keeping bloat and high cost.
explanation: Forking the full context copies the bloat verbatim, so the new branch stays near the limit with the same high cost and no compaction benefit.

text: Resume the session, compact it, and continue from preserved findings.
explanation: Facts are still current but verbose tool output fills context. Resume, compact, and continue from preserved findings; discarding, forking full context, or deleting arbitrary messages loses provenance

text: Delete arbitrary prior tool messages before resuming, risking key evidence loss.
explanation: Deleting arbitrary tool messages can silently remove decisive evidence; compaction summarizes deliberately and preserves findings instead.

text: Terminate immediately because any blocked tool call ends the agent loop.
explanation: A blocked tool call does not terminate the agent loop; the denial is appended as a normal tool result, so terminating is based on a false premise.

text: Convert the block reason to end_turn automatically, skipping model recovery.
explanation: Auto-converting the denial to end_turn skips the model's chance to recover or escalate, discarding the control flow the structured denial was designed for.

text: Make the hook call escalation itself and end the conversation immediately.
explanation: The hook should not hijack the flow by calling escalation itself and ending the conversation; its job is to deny the tool and let the model choose the recovery path.

text: Append the denial result and continue so the model can choose escalation.
explanation: A pre-use block does not end the loop; its structured denial result is appended so the model can choose escalation. Treating blocks as terminal or auto-ending the turn removes the model's recovery pat

text: Put rules in root README
explanation: A README is documentation, not auto-loaded configuration, so rules there never apply.

text: Copy CLAUDE.md everywhere
explanation: Duplicated CLAUDE.md files drift apart and bloat every session.

text: Use .claude/rules with globs
explanation: Path-scoped rules in .claude/rules load only for matching Terraform paths, avoiding duplication.

text: Let model guess conventions
explanation: Guessed conventions will contradict the team's actual Terraform practices.

text: In repo CLAUDE.md file
explanation: Repository CLAUDE.md is versioned and auto-loaded for every session in that project.

text: Only in shell history
explanation: Shell history is personal, ephemeral, and never loaded by Claude Code.

text: Paste prompt each task
explanation: Manual pasting is error-prone and does not reach other developers.

text: Only in CI variables
explanation: CI variables apply to CI runs only, not to developers' sessions.

text: Edit first failing file
explanation: Editing before understanding the migration's full scope risks breaking dependent files.

text: Ask for one-line patch
explanation: A one-line patch cannot cover a multi-system migration.

text: Run change blindly in CI
explanation: Blind CI runs waste cycles and can push a half-migrated state.

text: Use planning mode first
explanation: Planning mode explores the migration, API impact, and designs before any edits.

text: Keep in personal directory
explanation: Personal directories are not shared; teammates never see the command.

text: Add project command in .claude/commands
explanation: Project slash commands under .claude/commands are shared via version control.

text: Put text in code comment
explanation: A code comment is not executable and invisible to Claude Code's command system.

text: Add to test fixture
explanation: Test fixtures are for test data, not shared workflows.

text: Decompose message into three tracked items.
explanation: Decomposition tracks each intent separately so each gets its own checks and routing.

text: Single reply for all; mixes preconditions, risks policy breach.
explanation: A single reply mixes preconditions and can breach refund or address-change policy.

text: Handle refund only; ignores two commitments, harms satisfaction.
explanation: Handling only the refund ignores the address change and the complaint entirely.

text: Enforce per-item preconditions before each action.
explanation: Per-item preconditions (identity for refund and address change, routing for complaint) gate each action correctly.

text: Keep prompt rule; cheap but violable under load.
explanation: Prompt-only ordering rules are advisory and get violated under load or drift.

text: Block downstream tools until get_customer returns verified ID.
explanation: A programmatic precondition guarantees verification precedes refund, credit, and escalation.

text: Embed verification in each tool; duplicates logic, inconsistent.
explanation: Duplicating verification inside each tool creates inconsistent, hard-to-maintain logic.

text: Force get_customer first turn; no guarantee for later turns.
explanation: Forcing the first turn does not guarantee verification before later-turn actions.

text: Write longer prose; increases extraction time further.
explanation: Longer prose increases the triage extraction time the scenario is trying to cut.

text: Escalate earlier; less context, more premature load.
explanation: Earlier escalation shifts unfiltered load to specialists without the context to resolve it.

text: Emit structured handoff: id, reason, tried, next step.
explanation: Specialists need machine-readable triage fields; structured handoff cuts extraction time.

text: Attach full transcript; complete but slow to triage.
explanation: Full transcripts are complete but slow to triage, which is the current pain.

text: Cache stable SOP prefix across calls
explanation: Caching the stable SOP prefix removes the repeat-token cost of the 4k preamble on every call.

text: Extract shared instructions into modular template
explanation: A modular template isolates the shared instructions once instead of pasting them into every prompt.

text: Duplicate SOP text into every prompt
explanation: Duplication preserves exactly the repeat tokens that are driving cost up.

text: Upsize model to memorize SOP implicitly
explanation: A bigger model charges more per token and does not remove the repeated prefix.

text: Define role, rules, refusal in system
explanation: System-level role and refusal rules resist injection pressure because they are not carried inside user text.

text: Add input-output guardrails against injection attacks
explanation: Input and output guardrails screen hostile text before it reaches the model and actions before they execute.

text: Rely only on few-shot refusal examples
explanation: Few-shot refusal examples are patterns, not controls; injection text can override them.

text: Hide rules in user message footer
explanation: Rules placed inside the user message travel with the hostile text and are trivially bypassed.

text: Summarize stale turns; keep salient facts
explanation: Summarization keeps salient facts within the per-call budget while dropping stale detail.

text: Retrieve only query-relevant context chunks now
explanation: Relevance retrieval targets only the chunks the current query needs, preserving recall within budget.

text: Append full history to every prompt
explanation: Full-history appends are what blow the budget; they waste tokens on irrelevant turns.

text: Add chain-of-thought to compress long history
explanation: Chain-of-thought adds tokens rather than compressing history; it does not target relevance.

text: Skip chain-of-thought; deploy fast classifier now
explanation: Chain-of-thought adds 1.5s against a 200ms p99 budget; a fast classifier with rules preserves the SLA.

text: Avoid overlap -> assign non-overlapping source sets. [Set: partition / provenance / negotiate / sequence]
explanation: The coordinator must partition sources and require provenance for dedup. Direct negotiation adds coordination latency and sequential execution only hides overlap without attribution.

text: Enable dedup -> require provenance with each finding. [Set: partition / provenance / negotiate / sequence]
explanation: The coordinator must partition sources and require provenance for dedup. Direct negotiation adds coordination latency and sequential execution only hides overlap without attribution.

text: Coordinate sources -> let subagents negotiate access directly. [Set: partition / provenance / negotiate / sequence]
explanation: Peer-to-peer negotiation of source access adds coordination latency and races; the coordinator should own source routing and assign non-overlapping sets.

text: Ensure coverage -> run sequentially so later agents infer prior coverage. [Set: partition / provenance / negotiate / sequence]
explanation: Running sequentially does not create coverage, because later agents cannot reliably infer what was already covered; only explicit non-overlapping partitioning guarantees it.

text: Normalize extraction deterministically to avoid ordering errors.

explanation: Hooking every stage including the soft style preference spends scarce deterministic-hook budget where a prompt suffices and adds latency on every call.

text: Hook only sensitivity and leave normalization entirely to prose.
explanation: Leaving normalization entirely to prose reintroduces the ordering errors the hook exists to prevent; a prompt-based format instruction is not deterministic.

text: Data exposure — redact sensitive fields server-side before anything reaches the logs
explanation: Sensitive fields enter the context window or the logs where they should not, so the mitigation is server-side redaction of those fields before anything is written to the audit store.
