text: Give each agent a longer procedure but keep their inputs fully independent.
explanation: Longer procedures with fully independent inputs do not create a shared interface, so each agent still invents its own data shape and the incompatibility remains.

text: Merge all work into one agent and avoid decomposition, losing parallelism.
explanation: Merging everything into one agent abandons decomposition and parallelism to solve a contract problem that a shared interface fixes directly.

text: Define a common contract first, delegate against it, then verify integration.
explanation: Incompatible shapes come from independent delegation without a shared interface. Define a common contract first, delegate against it, then verify integration; longer isolated procedures or end-stage r

text: Let the coordinator rewrite conflicting components at the end, adding rework.
explanation: Rewriting conflicting components at the end is expensive rework; a shared contract defined before delegation prevents the shape conflicts from arising.

text: Specify the goal, quality criteria, and tools, allowing adaptive tool decisions.
explanation: Exact procedures go brittle when intermediate data surprises; mechanical completion misses quality goals. Specify goal, quality criteria, and tools while allowing adaptive tool decisions; further rest

text: Restrict tools further so deviation from the procedure becomes impossible.
explanation: Restricting tools further reduces the subagent's ability to adapt when intermediate data surprises it, deepening the brittleness instead of fixing the prompt framing.

text: Assign one subagent to each procedural step, multiplying handoff overhead.
explanation: One subagent per procedural step multiplies handoff overhead and still encodes the brittle procedure, only spread across more agents.

text: Add an iteration cap equal to the listed steps, preserving procedural rigidity.
explanation: An iteration cap equal to the step count enforces the same rigid procedure; it does not let tool decisions adapt to unexpected intermediate data.

text: Keep text parsing and add a sequence example, leaving spoofed completion possible.
explanation: Keeping text parsing leaves completion spoofable, and adding a sequence example still relies on probabilistic prompt compliance for KYC ordering.

text: Use a fixed iteration count and order tools in the definition list for control.
explanation: A fixed iteration count and tool-definition ordering control neither when the loop stops correctly nor whether KYC actually succeeded before account opening.

text: Stop on tool_use so the first requested action ends the loop prematurely.
explanation: Stopping on tool_use ends the loop at the very first requested action, before the KYC flow or onboarding work can complete.

text: Stop on end_turn and gate account opening on recorded KYC success.
explanation: Text matching 'done' is spoofable and prompt-only KYC is unenforceable. Stop on end_turn and gate account opening on recorded KYC success; fixed counts and tool ordering do not enforce outcomes.

text: Enable request logging so assessors can trace every eligibility call
explanation: compliance-theater — logging produces an audit trail but does not place the workload inside an authorized boundary.

text: Route the workload through a FedRAMP-authorized government cloud environment
explanation: FedRAMP authorization attaches to the cloud service and environment, not the model; the delivery route must be authorized at the workload's required impact level and the workload must run exclusively through it.

text: Add a compliance notice to the eligibility assistant's system prompt
explanation: prompt-as-guarantee — a compliance notice in the prompt asserts the deployment's posture without placing any component inside an authorized boundary.

text: A signed BAA, HIPAA compliance enabled, and only eligible features
explanation: PHI through a third party requires a signed Business Associate Agreement; the evidence a reviewer accepts is the signed BAA, the admin setting showing HIPAA compliance enabled, and the eligible-feature list.

text: The SOC 2 Type II report, which attests HIPAA processing
explanation: compliance-theater — a SOC 2 report attests security controls under another framework; it is not a BAA and does not by itself authorize PHI processing.

text: A confidentiality clause added to the assistant's deployed system prompt
explanation: prompt-as-guarantee — a confidentiality instruction is unenforced model guidance; it satisfies none of the contractual or configuration requirements HIPAA imposes.

text: Index table rows with cell metadata
explanation: Text recall clears target; table-cell lookup fails because flattening destroys structure. A row-level structured index fixes the failing half.

text: Widen prose chunks to 1024 tokens
explanation: Wider prose chunks still contain flattened tables, so cell-level lookups keep failing even though more text is retrieved per hit.

text: Raise top-k from 5 to 15
explanation: Retrieving more passages cannot restore cell structure that flattening destroyed, so extra prose still lacks the row and column boundaries the metric measures.

text: Retrain embeddings on manuals
explanation: Embedding quality is not the failure; the source text lost its table structure before indexing, so retraining embeddings cannot bring cell boundaries back.

text: Delete first, then sample for quality
explanation: Sampling for quality after deletion cannot restore incorrectly deleted accounts or the legal holds the retention list protects.

text: Add a prompt to delete more carefully
explanation: A prompt asking the agent to delete more carefully is not an enforcement control and does not stop scope exceeding legal retention needs.

text: Require approval of scope before execution
explanation: Irreversible bulk deletion needs a gate before execution with scope preview and approval. Post-hoc sampling cannot restore deleted accounts.

text: Speed deletion to cut compute cost
explanation: Speeding deletion increases the blast radius of an unapproved irreversible action, making the missing approval gate more dangerous.

text: Close out now and merely note the drift risk
explanation: Noting drift risk without thresholds, an owner, or a cadence leaves nobody accountable to act when the seasonal input mix shifts.

text: Keep the build team on retainer indefinitely
explanation: Keeping the build team on retainer adds cost indefinitely without defining what triggers review or who owns quality decisions.

text: Define thresholds, owner, and review cadence
explanation: AI quality drifts, so closeout needs thresholds, a named owner, and review cadence. Retainers, wider dashboards, or noted risks without tied action are monitoring only.

text: Extend dashboard coverage for all operators
explanation: Wider dashboard coverage adds visibility but sets no thresholds and names no owner, so drift still produces no response.

text: Add few-shot examples for each language
explanation: Per-language few-shot examples still fork the disclaimer text across six languages and multiply the maintenance surface where mutation occurs.

text: Let each team fork prompt freely
explanation: Letting each team fork freely guarantees the disclaimer keeps mutating, which is the exact failure the design must stop.

text: Use modular template with shared variables
explanation: Consistency-flexibility trade-off: per-language forks diverge on the disclaimer; a modular template with shared variables localizes tone while locking legal text.

text: Switch to flagship model for consistency
explanation: A flagship model cannot stop prompt content from diverging across teams; the variation lives in the prompts, not the model.

text: Freeform prompt written per incident
explanation: Freeform prompting per incident recreates the per-operator variation the incident process already suffers from.

text: Packaged Skill embedding runbook checks
explanation: On-call needs a packaged Skill embedding the runbook, checks, and escalation. Freeform prompting varies by operator.

text: Personal user memory from last on-call
explanation: Personal memory from the last on-call is stale, individual, and invisible to whoever picks up the next night.

text: Global style rule describing incidents
explanation: A global style rule shapes tone, not the runbook steps, verification checks, or escalation path the incidents need.

text: Add aggregate success dashboards
explanation: Aggregate dashboards are the counts that already exist; more aggregation still cannot reproduce a single failing request.

text: Expand offline eval question sets
explanation: Offline eval question sets measure lab accuracy, which already passes, and say nothing about the production path where errors occur.

text: Sample only successful traces
explanation: Sampling only successful traces systematically misses the failing 8% whose diagnosis is blocked.

text: Emit spans with tool I/O, outcome labels
explanation: Counts cannot reproduce failures. Per-request spans with retrieval and tool I/O plus outcome labels make errors diagnosable.

text: Run independent extractors in parallel for each field
explanation: Parallel extraction with a supervisor merge fits independent fields plus conflict resolution; chained debate on every field wastes latency for little accuracy gain.

text: Chain all agents sequentially debating every extracted field
explanation: Sequential debate on every field adds latency to independent extractions that need no reconciliation, buying no accuracy for the cost.

text: Add supervisor merging outputs and resolving field conflicts
explanation: Parallel extraction with a supervisor merge fits independent fields plus conflict resolution; chained debate on every field wastes latency for little accuracy gain.

text: Let agents bid for tasks in open marketplace negotiation
explanation: Open-marketplace task bidding adds coordination overhead and non-determinism that independent field extraction does not need.

text: Randomize assignment and isolate single variable
explanation: A and D enforce randomization, isolation, and held-out confirmation. Costs: A/D cost traffic and discipline; B confounds time with treatment; C overfits selection to tuned data.

text: Run variant A mornings variant B evenings
explanation: Assigning variants to different times of day confounds weekly seasonality with the treatment, so any win rate is uninterpretable.

text: Select winner on the tuning dataset
explanation: Selecting the winner on the tuning dataset overfits selection to data the variants were tuned against, so the result will not generalize.

text: A stricter code-based threshold on per-answer accuracy
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — tightening a per-answer check cannot see a failure that only emerges across turns.

text: Rules workflow triaging cases, LLM drafting customer rationales
explanation: Pure rule-based triage cannot cover the variety of return reasons, so escalations keep manual labor high and the 30% cost cut slips.

text: Autonomous agent negotiating refunds directly with customers
explanation: An agent negotiating refunds directly with customers makes probabilistic decisions on money, raising exactly the wrong-refund rate leadership froze.

text: Deterministic workflow routing refunds, LLM extracting reasons only
explanation: Deterministic routing holds the wrong-refund rate while LLM extraction cuts handling time; full agent autonomy trades accuracy for speed under a fixed date.

text: Fine-tuned model replacing policy engine for refund decisions
explanation: A fine-tuned model replacing the policy engine is probabilistic and needs retraining on every policy change, so wrong refunds rise and auditability drops.

text: Add more simple lookup cases now
explanation: Adding more of the case type already overrepresented deepens the skew and inflates scores while the 10% adversarial tail stays unmeasured.

text: Sample randomly from raw chat history
explanation: Random sampling from raw history reproduces noise and still underrepresents rare adversarial edges in any finite draw, so measured risk stays distorted.

text: Stratify to match production failure mix
explanation: C stratifies to production risk including the 10% adversarial tail. Costs: A inflates scores and hides risk; B preserves skew and noise; C costs curation effort; D hardens bias and false confidence.

text: Duplicate high-scoring cases for score stability
explanation: Duplicating cases the system already passes pads stability numbers without measuring anything new, hardening false confidence in the eval.

text: Ask the model to self-check refunds
explanation: A model self-check is probabilistic and steerable by prompt content, so it can approve over-limit refunds and leaves no deterministic audit trail.

text: Log refunds for monthly sampling review
explanation: Monthly sampling reviews refunds after they have already issued, so over-limit payouts still occur and are only caught late.

text: Enforce refund policy in tool authorization
explanation: Tool calls need deterministic policy enforcement on amount, recipient, and approval state. A model self-check is bypassable and unauditable.

text: Add few-shot examples of fair refunds
explanation: Few-shot examples nudge behavior but cannot enforce a hard dollar threshold or guarantee that approval state was checked before the tool ran.

text: Confirm residency constraint before routing design
explanation: A constraint mentioned in passing must be confirmed before routing or storage decisions. Designing past it or adding monitoring without confirming scope leaves the violation intact.

text: Keep US routing and note assumption later
explanation: Proceeding on an unconfirmed assumption means the violation ships as designed if the residency constraint turns out to be real.

text: Schedule load tests before confirming residency
explanation: Load testing measures performance, not compliance, so it consumes time while the routing decision still rests on an unconfirmed constraint.

text: Add residency dashboards without confirming scope
explanation: Dashboards cannot confirm the scope of the constraint, so they would monitor the wrong boundary while the routing decision remains unvalidated.

text: Add more few-shot invoice examples
explanation: More examples improve formatting tendencies but cannot guarantee schema validity, which the current few-shot setup already demonstrates with 8% malformed output.

text: Switch to larger model only
explanation: A larger model reduces but does not eliminate malformed JSON, and it leaves the brittle downstream parser exposed to every remaining violation.

text: Enforce structured output with schema
explanation: Reliability-generality trade-off: few-shot hints at format but structured output plus system instruction enforces the invoice schema; examples alone leave 8% malformed.

text: Enable chain-of-thought for invoice parsing
explanation: Chain-of-thought adds reasoning about the task, not constraints on output syntax, so malformed JSON persists at the parser.

text: Single root rule applied to all paths
explanation: A single root rule applies one convention set to both subsystems, which is precisely the misfiring the team is trying to fix.

text: Personal user override for every developer
explanation: Personal overrides differ per developer, so behavior becomes inconsistent across the team and the rules never travel with the repository.

text: Directory CLAUDE.md inside frontend folder
explanation: Subsystem differences call for directory-scoped CLAUDE.md. A root-wide rule would force frontend conventions onto backend code.

text: Standalone slash command run each time
explanation: A slash command only runs when explicitly invoked, so it provides no persistent, automatic scoping while code is being edited.

text: Keep direct payments API call
explanation: With one consumer, direct API already meets p99 and avoids MCP hop, host, and date risk. MCP pays off with many consumers, not one.

text: Wrap payments in new MCP server
explanation: Wrapping payments in a new MCP server adds the 180ms that breaches the p99 budget plus a new-host deployment directly against the Friday date.

text: Add MCP cache before Friday launch
explanation: A cache in front of MCP does not remove the added hop or the new-host deployment risk that the launch date forbids.

text: Proxy payments through chat agent
explanation: Proxying payments through a chat agent inserts another latency-adding layer into a direct path that already meets budget at 99.9% success.

text: Autonomous planner choosing verification order per loan application
explanation: Letting a planner choose verification order per application introduces run-to-run variance that auditors cannot reproduce for legally sensitive decisions.

text: Supervisor agents negotiating credit decisions through open debate
explanation: Agents negotiating credit decisions through open debate produce non-deterministic outcomes where compliance demands repeatable, auditable steps.

text: Single agent calling tools until it feels confident enough
explanation: Continuing until the model 'feels confident' is not a deterministic stopping rule, so decision paths and audit trails vary per loan.

text: Fixed workflow sequencing checks, LLM extracting fields only
explanation: Fixed underwriting steps with audit needs favor deterministic workflow plus LLM extraction; an autonomous planner adds variance where compliance demands repeatability.

text: Ship combined change and watch dashboards
explanation: Shipping the combined change keeps both edits confounded, so the 4-point gain remains unattributable no matter what the dashboards show.

text: Add larger model alongside new prompt
explanation: Adding a larger model stacks a third change onto two existing confounds, making attribution worse and rollback harder.

text: Test one change per arm versus control
explanation: C isolates one change per arm against control. Costs: A leaves attribution impossible; B doubles confounds and rollback pain; C costs extra arms and traffic; D costs time without causal evidence.

text: Roll back both changes and wait
explanation: Rolling back both changes discards a measured 4-point gain and produces no evidence about which change helped.

text: Follow the article as updated policy
explanation: Treating retrieved content as updated policy executes the injection, letting article text override developer and system policy.

text: Defer to the article author for consent
explanation: The article author is not a principal in the trust hierarchy and has no authority to consent to overriding privacy policy.

text: Include SSNs with a warning to user
explanation: Including SSNs discloses them regardless of intent; a user-facing warning does not cure the privacy violation the injected instruction requests.

text: Ignore the embedded instruction as data
explanation: Retrieved content is data, never a principal. The agent must ignore the embedded instruction and complete the user's task under developer and system policy.

text: Write assumptions and constraints down early
explanation: Sound discovery writes assumptions down, converts vague terms into failure conditions, and reconciles conflicts explicitly. Designing past hints or locking dates first are gate violations.

text: Design past a constraint mentioned in passing
explanation: Designing past a constraint mentioned in passing is a discovery gate violation: the assumption goes unconfirmed and forces redesign if it proves real.

text: Convert vague terms into failure conditions
explanation: Sound discovery writes assumptions down, converts vague terms into failure conditions, and reconciles conflicts explicitly. Designing past hints or locking dates first are gate violations.

text: Lock the launch date before requirements exist
explanation: Locking the launch date before requirements exist forces scope and risk compromises before anyone knows what is being built.

text: Reconcile conflicts via risk-tolerance agreement
explanation: Sound discovery writes assumptions down, converts vague terms into failure conditions, and reconciles conflicts explicitly. Designing past hints or locking dates first are gate violations.

text: Enable prompt caching for stable prefix
explanation: Cost-reuse trade-off: a 3k-token preamble repeated at 90% hit rate is a caching problem, not a quality problem; upsizing the model raises cost without cutting repeats.

text: Upgrade to flagship model for efficiency
explanation: A flagship model costs more per call and does nothing about the real expense driver, the 3k-token prefix repeated on 90% of calls.

text: Add few-shot examples to each request
explanation: Appending few-shot examples adds tokens to every request, raising cost while quality is already acceptable.

text: Use chain-of-thought to reduce token cost
explanation: Chain-of-thought generates additional reasoning tokens, so it increases per-call cost instead of reducing it.

text: Store team command in user home only
explanation: A command stored in one user's home directory is invisible to teammates, so nobody else can discover or run it.

text: Store command in project commands directory
explanation: Team commands must be project-scoped with descriptive frontmatter and parameters. User-scoped or undescribed commands do not scale.

text: Omit description to keep files shorter
explanation: Without a description the command is undiscoverable and its parameters undocumented, defeating the reuse the squad wants.

text: Add frontmatter with args and description
explanation: Team commands must be project-scoped with descriptive frontmatter and parameters. User-scoped or undescribed commands do not scale.

text: Lengthen every tool description text
explanation: Longer descriptions add tokens and only nudge routing probabilistically; the 22% wrong-tool rate needs capability reduced, not better advertised.

text: Add retries on wrong-tool calls
explanation: Retrying wrong-tool calls repeats the same routing failure while adding latency, leaving the error rate above target.

text: Upgrade model to follow instructions
explanation: Accuracy once routed correctly already clears target, so a stronger model spends cost on the half that is passing.

text: Scope minimal tool subset per task
explanation: Correct-tool accuracy clears target; excess capability drives misrouting. Least-privilege per-task subsets cut the failing wrong-tool rate.

text: Bigger model parsing invoices plus richer accuracy dashboards
explanation: Richer dashboards observe drift but never feed corrections back into extraction, and a bigger model does not stop monthly format shifts.

text: Input validation plus sampled review feeding extraction improvements
explanation: Upstream validation plus sampled human review closes the loop on extraction drift; downstream dashboards alone detect errors without correcting the pipeline.

text: Parallel agents debating each invoice field before posting
explanation: Parallel agents debating each field multiply per-invoice latency and cost without adding any mechanism that detects or corrects format drift.

text: Faster OCR engine plus lower temperature for output stability
explanation: A faster OCR engine and lower temperature improve throughput and stability but neither detect nor correct the monthly format changes causing errors.

text: Cache with TTL plus explicit invalidation rules
explanation: A caches with TTL plus invalidation and names staleness risk. Costs: A costs invalidation logic; B pays full price per repeat; C risks stale refunds silently; D costs latency with no savings.

text: Disable caching and pay full price
explanation: Disabling caching pays full retrieval price on 40% repeat traffic, surrendering the savings the $900 monthly bill is demanding.

text: Cache indefinitely without any invalidation control
explanation: Indefinite caching with no invalidation serves stale policy answers silently after updates, an unacceptable correctness risk for refund guidance.

text: Retry every query with fresh full retrieval
explanation: Retrying every query with fresh retrieval is a full-price retrieval every time, raising both cost and latency with zero savings.

text: Add searchable tool discovery on demand
explanation: On-demand discovery plus per-intent scoping fix tokens and misrouting together. Bigger windows or retries preserve the bloated context.

text: Inject full catalog into bigger window
explanation: A bigger window accommodates the 41k-token bloat instead of removing it, so token cost and misrouting pressure both persist.

text: Inject task-scoped tool subsets only
explanation: On-demand discovery plus per-intent scoping fix tokens and misrouting together. Bigger windows or retries preserve the bloated context.

text: Retry wrong-tool calls automatically
explanation: Automatic retries on wrong-tool calls add latency and cost while leaving the 140-tool catalog that causes the misrouting untouched.

text: Autonomous agent filing briefs without lawyer approval step
explanation: Filing briefs without the lawyer approval step removes the sign-off every filing legally requires, breaking accountability for speed.

text: General chatbot answering legal questions without source citations
explanation: A general chatbot without source citations cannot support filings that require cited precedent.

text: Batch summarizer rewriting all precedents without review queue
explanation: Rewriting all precedents in batches without a review queue risks silent legal errors entering every downstream filing.

text: Draft-then-verify workflow with lawyer approval and citations
explanation: Draft-then-verify keeps the lawyer accountable while cutting drafting time; autonomous filing optimizes speed while violating the accountability constraint.

text: Lab accuracy alone proves user acceptance
explanation: Lab accuracy celebrates model quality while agents override 20% of drafts in production, so it never reveals user acceptance.

text: Override rate flags rejected agent drafts
explanation: B/C/E reflect acceptance: overrides, reopens, resolution. Costs: downstream plumbing costs effort; A celebrates lab-only gains; D hides failures behind infrastructure health.

text: Ticket reopen rate signals unresolved work
explanation: B/C/E reflect acceptance: overrides, reopens, resolution. Costs: downstream plumbing costs effort; A celebrates lab-only gains; D hides failures behind infrastructure health.

text: Server uptime alone proves task success
explanation: Server uptime measures infrastructure health, not whether agent tasks actually succeed for users.

text: Resolution rate confirms completed user goals
explanation: B/C/E reflect acceptance: overrides, reopens, resolution. Costs: downstream plumbing costs effort; A celebrates lab-only gains; D hides failures behind infrastructure health.

text: Stay commercial since data is encrypted
explanation: AES-256 and SOC 2 do not confer FedRAMP authorization, which the agency requires regardless of encryption strength.

text: Add a prompt ban on sensitive topics
explanation: A prompt ban on sensitive topics is a software instruction, not the authorized operating environment the pilot requires.

text: Move to a FedRAMP-authorized offering
explanation: FedRAMP requires operating in an authorized environment with inherited controls and continuous monitoring. Encryption on a commercial endpoint is insufficient.

text: Self-attest controls without assessment
explanation: FedRAMP requires third-party assessment and continuous monitoring; self-attestation satisfies neither.

text: Weekly quality report with no tied action
explanation: A weekly report with no tied action is monitoring only; nothing in the loop changes the system when quality degrades.

text: Breach pages the owner who runs runbook
explanation: A closed loop pairs an agreed signal with an agreed response that changes the system. Reports and ad-hoc dashboards without tied action are monitoring only.

text: Analyst dashboard explored ad hoc each month
explanation: An ad-hoc dashboard explored monthly has no agreed signal threshold or predefined response, so it never triggers a change.

text: Override spike triggers agreed rollback now
explanation: A closed loop pairs an agreed signal with an agreed response that changes the system. Reports and ad-hoc dashboards without tied action are monitoring only.

text: Allow chain-of-thought for offline batch scoring
explanation: Latency-accuracy trade-off: with no user waiting and budget for tokens, step-by-step reasoning buys proof accuracy; forcing direct answers would trade correctness for unneeded speed.

text: Force direct answers to save tokens
explanation: Forcing direct answers trades away the proof accuracy that dominates this workload to save tokens that are explicitly budgeted.

text: Use smallest model without any reasoning
explanation: The smallest model without reasoning minimizes cost at the expense of the accuracy that is the stated priority for nightly proofs.

text: Cache prompts to replace step reasoning
explanation: Caching reuses prompts but cannot perform the multi-step reasoning the proofs require, so it does not substitute for step reasoning.

text: Searchable catalog loading schemas on demand
explanation: Progressive discovery loads schemas on demand and scopes per intent; full injection and prompt-stuffed credentials are monolithic context.

text: Full 140 schemas injected every turn
explanation: Injecting all 140 schemas every turn is the definition of monolithic context: everything loads regardless of current intent.

text: Confirm winner on held-out evaluation set
explanation: A and D enforce randomization, isolation, and held-out confirmation. Costs: A/D cost traffic and discipline; B confounds time with treatment; C overfits selection to tuned data.

text: Send full charts since channel is encrypted
explanation: Encryption protects the transport, not the scope of disclosure; sending full charts still violates the minimum-necessary standard.

text: Extract only needed fields before the call
explanation: HIPAA minimum necessary requires limiting PHI to what the purpose needs, before the call. TLS plus BAA alone does not satisfy it.

text: Rely on BAA plus TLS cover as sufficient
explanation: A BAA and TLS govern the vendor relationship and channel security, not how much PHI each individual request discloses.

text: Add a prompt telling model to ignore extras
explanation: Sending full charts and instructing the model to ignore extras still discloses unneeded PHI upstream of any instruction that follows.

text: Encode both demands as runtime toggles
explanation: Encoding both demands as runtime toggles defers the risk decision into code configuration instead of resolving it explicitly with stakeholders.

text: Facilitate risk agreement before designing now
explanation: Conflicting mandates are resolved by facilitating explicit risk agreement before designing. Encoding toggles, imposing one side, or splitting difference avoids the decision.

text: Impose manual approval as binding rule
explanation: Unilaterally imposing manual approval ignores the fixed quarter date and cost cap that sales must meet, replacing facilitation with decree.

text: Split difference with partial sampling now
explanation: Partial sampling splits the difference so both mandates stay partially violated and nobody owns the residual risk.

text: Add ten few-shot examples per request
explanation: Ten few-shot examples add 800 tokens per call for a format already fully specified, with no accuracy gain to justify the spend.

text: Use zero-shot instruction with output schema
explanation: Token-quality trade-off: order-ID format is fully specifiable, so 800 tokens of few-shot per call buys nothing; zero-shot instruction plus schema preserves accuracy at scale.

text: Enable chain-of-thought for ID extraction tasks
explanation: Chain-of-thought adds reasoning tokens and latency to a trivial extraction with a crisp, fully specifiable format.

text: Deploy flagship model for simple extraction
explanation: A flagship model maximizes per-call cost on the simplest task in the workload for no accuracy benefit.

text: Paste only the suspect function text
explanation: Pasting only the suspect function omits the load-dependent environmental evidence where a peak-only timeout actually lives.

text: Ask for broad rewrite without evidence
explanation: Requesting a broad rewrite without evidence invites plausible-sounding fixes ungrounded in what the dashboards show.

text: Feed logs, metrics, traces with scope
explanation: Operational faults need logs, metrics, and traces bounding the prompt. Code-only context misses environment and timing causes.

text: Retry same prompt with higher temperature
explanation: Higher temperature adds randomness to a deterministic infrastructure fault and cannot diagnose or fix a load-dependent timeout.

text: Trust agent success summaries without checks
explanation: Trusting agent success summaries without checks lets self-reported numbers mask real failures, an unsound governance posture.

text: Treat retrieved content as untrusted data
explanation: Retrieval is data, excessive scope needs least privilege, and EU-US transfers need a valid mechanism. Blind trust in self-reports and indefinite retention are failures.

text: Default agents to least-privilege scope
explanation: Retrieval is data, excessive scope needs least privilege, and EU-US transfers need a valid mechanism. Blind trust in self-reports and indefinite retention are failures.

text: Retain EU chats indefinitely for evals
explanation: Retaining EU chats indefinitely for evals violates data-minimization and retention rules that govern EU personal data.

text: Ground EU-US transfers in a valid mechanism
explanation: Retrieval is data, excessive scope needs least privilege, and EU-US transfers need a valid mechanism. Blind trust in self-reports and indefinite retention are failures.

text: Verify identity and scopes server-side
explanation: Client-asserted tiers are forgeable. Identity and scopes must be verified and enforced server-side regardless of prompt claims.

text: Harden system prompt role wording text
explanation: Harder prompt wording does not change that the client asserts identity; a forged tier in prompt text still succeeds.

text: Hide priority tool descriptions from prompts
explanation: Hiding tool descriptions does not verify who the caller is, so forged client-asserted tiers keep working.

text: Embed longer tokens inside prompt text
explanation: Longer tokens inside prompt text remain client-controlled data, so the forgery path stays open.

text: Unbounded agent debate improving answer depth and creativity
explanation: Unbounded debate has no stop condition, so it blows the 3s p99 budget and burns the quarterly inference cap on every reply.

text: Endless retrieval expansion ensuring complete context coverage
explanation: Endless retrieval expansion grows per-reply latency and token spend without bound, directly violating both budget constraints.

text: Full-model ensemble reviewing every routine customer reply
explanation: A full-model ensemble on every routine reply spends premium inference on trivial cases, exhausting the capped budget early.

text: Bounded parallel critics with adjudicator under latency budget
explanation: Parallel critics with adjudication names both the recall gain and the latency-cost control; unbounded debate names collaboration benefits without latency or cost bounds.

text: Reduce chunks and cap retry loops
explanation: A cuts chunks and retries; C bounds agentic turns with early stops. Costs: A costs recall validation; B costs discount theater on bloated volume; C costs stop-rule tuning; D costs blind quality loss.

text: Chase small discount retaining full volume
explanation: The 10% discount reprices an already bloated 10-cent workflow, leaving chunks, retries, and turn count untouched.

text: Task-scoped subset injected per intent
explanation: Progressive discovery loads schemas on demand and scopes per intent; full injection and prompt-stuffed credentials are monolithic context.

text: All docs and secrets in system prompt
explanation: Stuffing all documents and secrets into the system prompt is monolithic context and also needlessly exposes credentials.

text: Faster dashboard showing existing underwriting queue status
explanation: A faster dashboard improves visibility into the existing queue without changing how underwriting decisions get made, so turnaround stays in days.

text: Straight-through pipeline auto-deciding all standard loan applications
explanation: Transformation changes the operating model with measured turnaround gains; a faster dashboard improves visibility without redesigning underwriting itself.

text: Better search across current policy document store
explanation: Better search over current documents accelerates lookup but leaves the underwriting process itself unchanged.

text: Copilot autocompleting underwriter notes without process change
explanation: A copilot autocompleting notes is incremental assistance that leaves the operating model and turnaround untouched.

text: Keep schedule comparing raw win rates
explanation: The Monday-morning versus Friday-evening windows confound weekday seasonality and the midweek reranker change with the prompt variants.

text: Collect more Monday Friday traffic samples
explanation: Collecting more traffic from the same biased windows adds volume but preserves the time confound and the midweek treatment contamination.

text: Pause tests until traffic fully stabilizes
explanation: Pausing until traffic stabilizes delays the decision without removing the confounding from the data already shaped by mixed windows.

text: Randomize interleave both prompts with logging
explanation: D removes weekday and midweek confounds via randomization. Costs: A costs time-confounded attribution error; B costs more biased data; C costs delay without fixing bias; D costs router and logging wor

text: Prompt the model to try its best anyway
explanation: Instructing the model to try its best cannot extend a six-month-old knowledge cutoff, so confident outdated answers continue.

text: Ground answers in dated retrieved sources
explanation: Stale-model silence needs freshness grounding and version-aware abstention. Telling the model to try harder does not fix a stale cutoff.

text: Hide the model version from the UI view
explanation: Hiding the model version removes the user's ability to judge answer freshness while fixing nothing about the stale figures.

text: Abstain when data exceeds knowledge cutoff
explanation: Stale-model silence needs freshness grounding and version-aware abstention. Telling the model to try harder does not fix a stale cutoff.

text: Eval suite always precedes model selection
explanation: Evals gate model selection; rollback and owner gate handoff. Returning to discovery or accepting monitoring-alone readiness misplaces gates.

text: Rollback plan always precedes production handoff
explanation: Evals gate model selection; rollback and owner gate handoff. Returning to discovery or accepting monitoring-alone readiness misplaces gates.

text: Production handoff always requires a named owner
explanation: Evals gate model selection; rollback and owner gate handoff. Returning to discovery or accepting monitoring-alone readiness misplaces gates.

text: Iteration returns to discovery, not design
explanation: Iteration moves between design and build once requirements are clear; returning to discovery every cycle erases the requirements already gathered.

text: Monitoring alone satisfies handoff readiness checks
explanation: Monitoring alone lacks an owner, thresholds, and rollback, so it does not satisfy the readiness checks production handoff requires.

text: Cache stable SOP prefix across calls
explanation: Cost-consistency trade-off: caching the stable SOP prefix and extracting it into a modular template both attack repeat tokens; duplication and upsizing preserve or grow cost.

text: Extract shared instructions into modular template
explanation: Cost-consistency trade-off: caching the stable SOP prefix and extracting it into a modular template both attack repeat tokens; duplication and upsizing preserve or grow cost.

text: Duplicate SOP text into every prompt
explanation: Duplicating SOP text into every prompt pays for the 4k tokens on all 100k daily calls, the exact cost the moves should cut.

text: Upsize model to memorize SOP implicitly
explanation: A bigger model cannot reliably reproduce the SOP content and still costs more per call, growing rather than cutting expense.

text: Index quota snapshots every five minutes
explanation: Five-minute snapshots narrow the staleness window but still serve outdated quota data, keeping the 28% error source alive.

text: Route live quota to direct tenant API
explanation: Help docs are stable and suit RAG; quota is live state needing a direct tenant API. Faster snapshots or rerankers keep the staleness failure.

text: Add reranker over quota snapshot data
explanation: A reranker reorders already-stale snapshot records, so it changes ranking without fixing the underlying staleness.

text: Tune embeddings on quota field names
explanation: Tuning embeddings on field names improves retrieval relevance but cannot make snapshot data reflect current quota state.

text: Upgrade reasoning model for better field interpretation logic
explanation: A stronger reasoning model improves interpretation but still ingests the same garbled scans, so the input-quality failure remains.

text: Add multi-agent review debating each garbled scan result
explanation: Multi-agent debate re-reasons the same corrupted pixels, adding cost without addressing why the scans are unreadable.

text: Add capture validation rejecting all low-quality scans upstream
explanation: Garbled scans are an input-quality failure, so capture validation gates the pipeline; a stronger reasoning model improves processing but ingests the same noise.

text: Expand context window to include more invoice history
explanation: A wider context window adds invoice history that cannot recover text the scan never captured clearly.

text: Keep long prompt accepting error rate
explanation: Accepting a 24% violation rate on a 5% bar means shipping non-compliant extractions while the fix is still available.

text: Route everything to flagship model always
explanation: Routing everything to the flagship model blows the 2-cent-per-document cost cap on every document, not just hard ones.

text: Add constraints to same long prompt
explanation: Piling more constraints into the same long prompt asks the smaller model for MORE instruction-following, deepening the violation rate.

text: Simplify prompt fitting smaller model limits
explanation: D fits prompt complexity to the smaller model's instruction-following. Costs: A costs persistent 24% violations; B costs flagship latency and spend; C costs more constraints the model cannot follow; D

text: Evaluate accuracy disaggregated by group
explanation: Fairness needs disaggregated metrics plus reconstructable decision logs for proxy audits. Aggregate accuracy and log deletion hide disparity.

text: Report only aggregate accuracy overall
explanation: Aggregate accuracy averages away subgroup disparity, which is exactly what the proxy-bias complaint alleges.

text: Delete decision logs to protect privacy
explanation: Deleting decision logs destroys the evidence needed to reconstruct decisions and investigate the alleged proxy bias.

text: Keep versioned logs enabling proxy audits
explanation: Fairness needs disaggregated metrics plus reconstructable decision logs for proxy audits. Aggregate accuracy and log deletion hide disparity.

text: Brief the CIO privately to lock support
explanation: Privately locking in the CIO bypasses the board's deliberation and collapses if the alliance shifts, leaving the decision undefended on its merits.

text: Compare options against business priorities
explanation: Contested decisions are defended by side-by-side comparison against stakeholder priorities and a recorded decision with revisit conditions.

text: Deep-dive only the chosen design's internals
explanation: Deep-diving only the chosen design ignores the alternative the board favors, so the comparison the decision needs never happens.

text: Record decision, rationale, revisit triggers
explanation: Contested decisions are defended by side-by-side comparison against stakeholder priorities and a recorded decision with revisit conditions.

text: Zero-shot plus schema suits clear extraction tasks
explanation: Fit-to-purpose trade-off: zero-shot plus schema, offline CoT, and system-carried rules match their constraints; few-shot cannot enforce schemas and CoT violates tight latency budgets.

text: Few-shot alone guarantees schema-valid JSON output always
explanation: Few-shot examples shape style but cannot guarantee schema validity; the workload already shows format violations under few-shot prompting.

text: Chain-of-thought best fits offline complex reasoning tasks
explanation: Fit-to-purpose trade-off: zero-shot plus schema, offline CoT, and system-carried rules match their constraints; few-shot cannot enforce schemas and CoT violates tight latency budgets.

text: Chain-of-thought always meets tight latency budgets easily
explanation: Chain-of-thought adds generation steps that violate tight latency budgets rather than meeting them easily.

text: System instructions carry role and refusal rules
explanation: Fit-to-purpose trade-off: zero-shot plus schema, offline CoT, and system-carried rules match their constraints; few-shot cannot enforce schemas and CoT violates tight latency budgets.

text: Return bigger one-shot MCP verdicts now
explanation: A bigger one-shot verdict is still a single call with no dialogue, so the 4-6 turns of evidence negotiation remain impossible.

text: Use agent-to-agent evidence dialogue now
explanation: Multi-turn rights negotiation needs agent-to-agent dialogue, not a one-shot tool. Single verdict calls cannot deliberate evidence across turns.

text: Add more rights inputs to MCP
explanation: Adding more inputs to a one-shot MCP call does not create the multi-turn deliberation the 0.90 target requires.

text: Cache past verdicts to cut latency
explanation: Caching past verdicts speeds up old answers but cannot conduct the new negotiation turns the clearance case needs.

text: Weekly quality report with no tied action
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Breach pages the owner who runs the runbook
explanation: A closed loop pairs an agreed signal with an agreed response that changes the system. Reports and ad-hoc dashboards without tied action are monitoring only.

text: Analyst dashboard explored ad hoc each month
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Override alert triggers agreed prompt rollback
explanation: A closed loop pairs an agreed signal with an agreed response that changes the system. Reports and ad-hoc dashboards without tied action are monitoring only.

text: Freeze versioned output schema and baseline quality metrics
explanation: Feedback loops need a versioned output baseline to attribute change; tuning prompts from raw complaints skips the measurement that makes iteration meaningful.

text: Tune prompts weekly from anecdotal support ticket complaints
explanation: Tuning weekly from anecdotal complaints has no baseline or versioning, so any change is unattributable and may regress silently.

text: Add more agents to explore alternative answer styles
explanation: More agents exploring answer styles multiplies variation when the problem is that nobody agrees what good output even is.

text: Collect user thumbs signals without defined response owner
explanation: Collecting thumbs signals without a defined owner means nobody is accountable to act on the feedback, so the loop never closes.

text: Track lab accuracy demo win rates
explanation: Lab accuracy and demo win rates are the optimism the scenario already contradicts with a 20% agent override rate.

text: Monitor uptime average token usage only
explanation: Uptime and token usage measure infrastructure consumption, not whether users accept the agent's work.

text: Sample chats for subjective vibe scores
explanation: Subjective vibe scores sample opinions without the outcome rates leadership needs as acceptance proof.

text: Track overrides reopens task resolution rates
explanation: D measures overrides, reopens, and resolution as acceptance. Costs: A costs lab optimism while agents override; B costs infrastructure health mistaken for success; C costs vibe scores without outcomes

text: Recommend the faster option without stating cost
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Present both options costed without recommending one
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Defer the decision until after the launch date
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Recommend cheaper option, name sacrifice, set trigger
explanation: Trade-off communication costs both options, recommends one, names the sacrifice, and sets a revisit trigger. No recommendation or unstated cost avoids informed consent.

text: Add sprint-end architect inspection gates
explanation: Sprint-end inspection gates catch divergence after the team has already built the wrong thing instead of preventing it.

text: Specify behaviors with acceptance criteria
explanation: Handoff must transfer intent in buildable form: behavioral specs plus acceptance criteria the team can verify. Oversight catches drift; guidance prevents it.

text: Draw deeper component structure diagrams
explanation: Deeper component diagrams describe structure, not the observable behaviors and verifiable criteria the team improvised around.

text: Remove all skill output
explanation: Removing output destroys the discovery results the task needs.

text: Put output in CLAUDE.md
explanation: CLAUDE.md loads every session and would bloat all contexts with one task's output.

text: Run skill with context:fork
explanation: context:fork isolates verbose discovery output from the main session.

text: Disable permissions fully
explanation: Permission settings do not isolate context; they govern tool access.

text: Fix directly and verify
explanation: A clear single-file bug needs only direct fix plus focused verification.

text: Start long architecture plan
explanation: A long plan is disproportionate for one identified missing validation.

text: Delegate repo to subagents
explanation: Spawning subagents for one localized fix wastes budget.

text: Skip tests entirely
explanation: Even a simple fix needs verification that it works.

text: Ask politely in description
explanation: Description text is advisory; it cannot prevent shell execution.

text: Restrict skill allowed-tools
explanation: The allowed-tools list enforces the read-only boundary instead of prose.

text: Hide shell from docs
explanation: Documentation hiding does not restrict actual tool access.

text: Use longer prompt
explanation: A longer prompt is still prose and still not an enforcement mechanism.

text: tests/*.tsx
explanation: This misses *.test.tsx naming and only covers one folder depth.

text: *.test.tsx/**
explanation: This pattern matches contents under such files, not the files themselves.

text: src/test.tsx
explanation: A single literal path matches one file only.

text: **/*.test.tsx
explanation: **/ matches any directory depth for *.test.tsx files.

text: -p or --print
explanation: Print mode (-p) runs non-interactively and never waits for input.

text: --resume
explanation: --resume continues a saved session; it does not make execution non-interactive.

text: --verbose only
explanation: Verbosity changes logging detail, not interactivity.

text: --interactive
explanation: Interactive mode is the opposite of what CI needs.

text: Free-form Markdown report
explanation: Free-form Markdown is not reliably parseable by CI tooling.

text: Terminal screenshot only
explanation: Screenshots are neither machine-readable nor diffable.

text: --output-format json + schema
explanation: JSON output with a schema gives machine-readable, validated findings for CI.

text: Longer CLAUDE.md alone
explanation: A longer CLAUDE.md changes guidance, not output format.

text: Global env variable
explanation: An environment variable cannot carry a review prompt or restrict tools.

text: Random terminal alias
explanation: An alias launches commands; it does not package a focused review agent.

text: Project subagent definition
explanation: Subagents package a focused prompt with limited tools for review tasks.

text: Longer commit message
explanation: Commit messages document changes; they do not configure review agents.

text: Enable all shell commands
explanation: Enabling all shell commands removes the boundary the regulated team requires.

text: Allow only specific test command
explanation: An allow rule pre-approves only that test command; other shells stay blocked.

text: Put command in README
explanation: A README entry is documentation, not a permission rule.

text: Disable all config
explanation: Disabling config removes the mechanism that would enforce the boundary.

text: Start session with no context
explanation: Starting empty loses the prior conversation the developer wants to continue.

text: Use --print only
explanation: Print mode is for non-interactive runs, not for resuming prior conversations.

text: Delete session history
explanation: Deleting history removes the context that should be restored.

text: Use --resume
explanation: --resume restores prior context instead of starting empty.

text: $ARGUMENTS
explanation: $ARGUMENTS exposes trailing command arguments inside the prompt.

text: $SESSION_ID
explanation: Session identifiers do not carry the user's review targets.

text: $PATHS_ONLY
explanation: This placeholder does not exist in the command system.

text: Join daily standups to answer questions
explanation: Joining daily standups makes the architect a permanent answer source instead of transferring design intent in buildable form.

text: Caching: stable legal preamble repeated daily
explanation: Fit-to-mechanism trade-off: caching matches stable repeated preambles and Skills match cross-agent workflows; upsizing for prefix cost and few-shot for schema enforcement misplace valid techniques.

text: Skill: Jira-branch-PR workflow across agent teams
explanation: Fit-to-mechanism trade-off: caching matches stable repeated preambles and Skills match cross-agent workflows; upsizing for prefix cost and few-shot for schema enforcement misplace valid techniques.

text: Bigger model fixes repeated prefix cost
explanation: A bigger model does not fix repeated-prefix cost; the duplication persists per call regardless of model size.

text: Few-shot: enforcement for strict output schema
explanation: Few-shot examples hint at format but cannot enforce a strict output schema, which is exactly the misplaced pairing here.

text: Searchable catalog loading schemas on demand
explanation: Progressive discovery loads schemas on demand and scopes per intent; full injection and prompt-stuffed secrets are monolithic context. Full mapping: A progressive, B monolithic, C progressive, D monol

text: Full 150 schemas injected every turn
explanation: Injecting all 150 schemas every turn is monolithic context by definition, the opposite of loading schemas on demand per intent.

text: Task-scoped subset injected per intent now
explanation: Progressive discovery loads schemas on demand and scopes per intent; full injection and prompt-stuffed secrets are monolithic context. Full mapping: A progressive, B monolithic, C progressive, D monol

text: All runbooks plus secrets in system prompt
explanation: All runbooks plus secrets in the system prompt is monolithic injection, and it also exposes secrets regardless of intent.

text: Consumer sign-in upgraded to the vendor's most expensive enterprise tier
explanation: scale-not-strategy — the top tier buys capacity, not the signed agreement and the enabled configuration the obligation actually names.

text: The signed residency clause agreed with the infrastructure procurement contract
explanation: stale-fact — the clause was true at signing; it cannot show where this month's copies, including monitoring writes, actually land.

text: A quarterly attestation that the configured region setting remains EU
explanation: compliance-theater — the setting never changed; residency covers copies in logs and caches, which a setting attestation never inspects.

text: A convergence check comparing the primary database's regional replica copies
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — replica convergence concerns the primary store, while the drift was a monitoring path writing outside the approved boundary.

text: A data-flow record tracing every copy the deployment retains
explanation: Data residency covers processing and storage within the approved region, including copies in logs, caches, and retention paths; a living data-flow record, kept by an accountable owner, would have flagged the second-region write when it happened.

text: A feature list mirroring the sponsor's experience words
explanation: louder-not-explicit — repeating the experience word more prominently still records a preference; the bounded constraint beneath it is what the design actually needs.

text: A stakeholder-approved summary of the current claims workflow
explanation: stale-fact — a workflow summary describes what happens today; it leaves the unconfirmed experience word standing in for a testable constraint.

text: A prototype demonstrated at the next steering committee
explanation: valid-but-early — the sketch feels like progress, but it ends the questioning that would surface the latency budget, the handoff rule, and the failure path.

text: Testable constraints: a latency target, handoff rule, failure path
explanation: Follow-up questions convert the experience word into testable constraints: a bounded latency target, a handoff rule, and a failure state that hides internals. That costs minutes of questioning and buys a design the team can actually build and measure against.

text: A feature list mirroring the sponsor's words
explanation: louder-not-explicit — the outcomes were already captured; asking for them again spends discovery time on a bucket the call has answered.

text: The must-not-do boundaries: prohibited actions and human-escalation cases
explanation: The call holds must-do outcomes, a cost constraint, and a proof obligation; missing is the must-not-do bucket. Stakeholders rarely volunteer boundaries, so the architect asks which actions are prohibited and which cases route to a human.

text: A prototype demonstrated at the next steering meeting
explanation: knobs-not-design — the ceiling is already stated; stress-testing it is a design exercise, not the missing requirement category.

text: Testable constraints: latency target, handoff rule, failure path
explanation: compliance-theater — the proof obligation is on the table; the gap is the unasked must-not-do question, not stronger evidence.

text: One row: implied constraint, forced decision, documented assumption
explanation: Each discovery item becomes one translation-table row: the statement, the implied constraint, the decision it forces, and the assumption documented while unconfirmed. An unlabeled assumption inherits silently into the design, which is how ownership gaps resurface. One extra column, traceability.

text: A priority ranking of the sponsor's stated expectations
explanation: scale-not-strategy — ranking preferences preserves their wording, not the constraint, and never separates what is confirmed from what is assumed.

text: A sketch the sponsor approves during the call
explanation: valid-but-early — a sketch accelerates the meeting, but it stops the questioning that turns the remark into a constraint with an owner.

text: An escalation route reserved for later compliance blockers
explanation: convenience-over-safety — reserving a future path defers the confirmation; the assumption ships unmarked and the blocker arrives at review, when changing course costs the most.

text: Record the proposed sketch as the agreed design
explanation: valid-but-early — the sketch is useful, but adopting it as agreed ends the four-category questioning before licensure and retention rules surface.

text: The server verifies each caller's credential, then injects the verified role
explanation: Identity verification belongs on the server before the Claude call: the platform checks the caller's token and injects role and authorized scope, so enforcement is deterministic and auditable rather thanprompt-trusted, at the cost of building the verification step.

text: Five separate deployments, one per hospital group, each with its own model
explanation: scale-not-strategy: multiplying deployments scales the surface but each copy still trusts whatever identity its conversation text asserts.

text: Alerting whenever p95 end-to-end latency crosses its agreed four-second threshold
explanation: eval-blindness: latency was never the failing dimension, and speed alarms say nothing about whether retrieval grounded the answers.

text: Logging model version and input token count with cache hit-or-miss per request
explanation: Model version plus per-request token accounting, including whether the cache hit, makes any regressions attributable to a prompt, model, or caching change rather than mysterious, at modest logging cost.

text: Capturing retrieval precision per request, measured against the grounding documents themselves
explanation: Retrieval quality is invisible in the output and must be measured against the retrieved evidence; recording it per request turns silent retrieval drift into an alertable, owned metric.

text: A weekly manual review, by one engineer, of ten sampled conversations
explanation: louder-not-explicit: a small hand-read sample cannot measure precision across the day's traffic or attribute a regression to any change.

text: Hybrid lexical BM25 plus vector search, fused by reciprocal rank
explanation: BM25 rewards rare literal tokens such as endorsement codes, where embeddings blur them, while vector search carries the paraphrases; reciprocal rank fusion merges both lists so neither failure class recurs, at the cost of dual indexing.

text: Switching to the largest available embedding model and re-embedding everything
explanation: gold-plating: more capable embeddings still cannot guarantee exact token matches for rare codes, so the literal-lookup symptom survives untouched.

text: Lowering the decoding temperature so clause citations become more deterministic
explanation: wrong-layer-fix: decoding affects generation, not selection; the wrong clause was already retrieved before any generation began.

text: Re-embedding the clause index nightly so no document ever goes stale
explanation: stale-fact: freshness was never the symptom, since codes retrieve wrongly on the day they are published.

text: An hourly re-embedding job so the FAQ index lags by one hour
explanation: stale-fact: shortening the snapshot lag narrows, but never zeroes, the window; the answer is still built from stored, potentially superseded data.

text: A tool call that queries the scheduling system of record at question time
explanation: Live state, data that changes within a conversation's lifetime, must come from the source of truth at question time; retrieval suits static knowledge, and the trade-off is the dependency on the scheduling system's availability.

text: Widening the context window until the entire appointment book fits every call
explanation: wrong-layer-fix: a larger window still holds a snapshot, so the 10:05 appointments are simply wrong in more of them.

text: Routing every appointment change through the model to rewrite the index
explanation: extra-hop: inserting the model into each update adds cost and latency, while the requirement is only reading current state.

text: Prompt caching on the shared summarization instructions, reused across all transcripts
explanation: valid-but-early: caching trims repeated-prefix spend, but forty thousand one-shot transcripts share almost no long, stable context, so savings stay marginal.

text: Splitting the workload across many concurrent streams to finish before dawn
explanation: over-orchestration: parallel streams raise throughput but pay full price on every one of the forty thousand transcripts.

text: Shortening each summary's target length to shrink output tokens by a quarter
explanation: premature-optimization: trimming outputs yields a small, quality-risky fraction of the targeted fifty-percent saving.

text: Message Batches, trading a 24-hour window for a fifty-percent discount
explanation: The workload already runs overnight and polls for results, matching the asynchronous, no-latency-SLA design of the Message Batches API while halving inference spend; only truly interactive traffic must stay synchronous.

text: Decision logging capturing inputs, retrieved context, model output, and routing, later queryable
explanation: Transparency is instrumented: a decision must be replayable from a durable, queryable record of what drove it; a guardrail stack proves outputs passed, but explains nothing about why any single decision happened.

text: A judge model scoring each denial for consistency against the previous hundred decisions
explanation: louder-not-explicit: scoring after the fact still leaves each decision unreconstructable when the underlying record was never logged.

text: Mandatory pre-action human approval on every near-threshold permit before it takes effect
explanation: over-orchestration: review changes who decides, not whether the reasoning can be shown afterward, and the volume floods the approval queue.

text: A quarterly fairness evaluation comparing assistant approval rates across applicant demographic groups
explanation: eval-blindness: aggregate measures miss the per-decision reconstruction a regulator asks for, because skew can hide inside an unlogged path.

text: Send fewer items by routing on stakes, and surface the flag reason
explanation: valid-but-early: this names both symptoms, yet the mechanism question is what precisely the two halves must be keyed to, which this option never states.

text: Simply move the reviewer placement from post-action audit to the pre-action approval
explanation: scale-not-strategy: placement adds latency but does nothing about queue volume or what the reviewer sees, so consent fatigue persists.

text: Route on confidence, reversibility, and cost, and surface inputs plus the flag reason
explanation: Two mechanisms are needed because either failure alone keeps review broken: confidence, reversibility, and cost of a wrong answer shrink the queue to decisions warranting attention, while inputs plus the flag reason give the reviewer something to weigh instead of a bare output.

text: Accept the missing downstream signal, since no real adjuster ever grades the shadow output.
explanation: The cost of shadow testing is losing downstream signal: with no user receiving the shadow output, grading relies on golden answers and offline rubrics instead of acceptance and retry signals — exactly the cost the committee asked to have named.

text: Split production traffic equally, because three hundred daily interactions reach a meaningful statistical sample quickly.
explanation: scale-not-strategy — three hundred interactions a day cannot reach a meaningful sample quickly, so the live split measures little before the rollout date the quarter already promised.

text: Ship to every adjuster at once, reading complaint volume afterward as the regression signal.
explanation: eval-blindness — complaint volume after a full rollout exposes every adjuster to the unvalidated prompt first, which is precisely the exposure the policy requires the design to avoid.

text: Offline scoring cannot measure the response latency, and time-to-answer decides much of the checkout conversion here.
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — conversion depends on many product factors at once; pinning it to latency drops the downstream behavior from the decision, which is the very signal the rollout needs.

text: Only real live users produce downstream behavior signals like acceptance and follow-ups that offline scoring misses.
explanation: The mechanism is signal: downstream behavior — acceptance, retries, follow-up tickets — only exists when real users receive the output. A bounded small share of this two-million-session volume buys exactly those signals, at the cost of the small exposure the engineer wanted to avoid.

text: A cheaper prompt must clear procurement sign-off before it touches any shopper conversation at all.
explanation: eval-blindness — procurement sign-off records the business agreement but measures nothing about whether answers improved, which is what the adoption decision actually turns on.

text: Two million sessions guarantee the split reaches significance within the very first exposure day.
explanation: premature-optimization — significance is necessary but not the point: a significant token win can ship while users quietly reject more answers, because acceptance never entered the measurement.

text: Pin the model version and subscribe to provider release notes so every update is announced.
explanation: convenience-over-safety — announcements depend on provider diligence and human attention; the next silent change reaches customers exactly as quietly as this one did.

text: Run the frozen golden set against every deployment, gating service on captured scores.
explanation: The mechanism is release discipline: any model change is a change in the system's behavior, and the frozen golden set is the regression harness that notices. Because the gate runs before customers feel the difference, the trade-off is slower deployments bounded by scoring runs.

text: Alert when nightly token counts deviate, because longer summaries always herald the behavior change.
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — token growth is one symptom among several; watching it alone misses the dropped fault codes, which cost more than the longer summaries.

text: Log request and response hashes so behavioral differences are provable at the next postmortem.
explanation: compliance-theater — hashes prove after the fact that outputs differed, which the postmortem already established; they distinguish nothing before the next behavioral change reaches a customer.

explanation: extra-hop — distillation inserts a second model, its own calibration debt, and staleness between judge updates, duplicating grading that the code layer already performs for free.

explanation: scale-not-strategy — grading every record with the flagship judge maximizes consistency but prices the routine majority, which code settles for free, at generation cost again.

text: Sample one percent for expert human review and let the remaining traffic ship ungraded.
explanation: convenience-over-safety — sampling guards the sample, not the population; the ungraded remainder exports every grading failure into production, where defects cost the most to find.

text: Run code checks wherever the rule is expressible, judging only genuinely interpretive outputs.
explanation: Code grading is free, deterministic, and instant wherever a check is expressible, so it absorbs the routine records; the judge, priced at roughly the generation itself, is spent only where interpretation actually decides the score, which caps its cost where it earns it.

text: The frozen set no longer mirrors a production distribution that drifted beneath it.
explanation: A frozen set measures the launch quarter forever; once the production distribution drifts beneath it, steady scores report fidelity to a world that no longer exists, so the new mobile mix and dispute types never appear in the number.

text: Provider model updates change deployed behavior even when nothing in the repositories has changed.
explanation: Provider updates change deployed behavior in place: the same request, prompt, and configuration returned different answers after the mid-quarter patch, while the repository stayed silent — so the absence of changes proved nothing about what production was doing.

text: Steady quarterly scores were treated as proof of production quality without any continuous measurement.
explanation: premature-optimization — steady scores prove the frozen set passed, not that production held; without continuous measurement the committee read launch-time fidelity as current quality, which nothing established.

text: Token cost per classification climbed steadily after launch, correlating closely with the new dispute volumes.
explanation: scale-not-strategy — cost per classification tracks volumes and pricing, not correctness; its climb correlates with the card launch but explains none of the degradation the steady scores masked.

text: Model-grade every record with the flagship judge, maximizing verdict consistency across all categories.
explanation: scale-not-strategy — flagship grading on every record maximizes consistency but re-prices the routine ninety percent, which code settles deterministically for free, at the judge's generation parity.

text: Sample one percent for expert human review and ship the remaining transcripts without any grading.
explanation: eval-blindness — expert sampling protects the sample, not the population; the ungraded majority ships without a verdict, so drift surfaces only in production complaints.

text: Distill the flagship judge into a local classifier and grade the corpus with that copy.
explanation: extra-hop — the distilled copy adds a second model, its own calibration debt, and staleness between judge updates, duplicating grading the code layer already performs for free.

text: Grade in code wherever the check is expressible, and judge only genuinely interpretive outputs.
explanation: The grading ladder runs code first: programmatic checks are cheap, deterministic, and instant, so they cover the routine field-and-format majority; the judge, priced at roughly the generation itself, is reserved for the interpretive tenth where interpretation actually decides the verdict.

text: Run both models against the identical versioned set, scored by the identical grading rubric.
explanation: Both models must see the identical versioned set and be scored by the identical grading rubric, because a comparison only means something when the instrument is held constant; change anything else and the headline number stops attributing to the swap.

text: Set the rollback criterion before the swap, so a verdict arrives without debate.
explanation: The rollback criterion is decided before the swap, not after: without a pre-agreed threshold, a disappointing model becomes a debate about interpretation rather than a decision — exactly how the last fifteen-output swap shipped its unnoticed regression.

text: Adopt the new model once fifteen outputs, eyeballed by the rewriting engineer, look better.
explanation: convenience-over-safety — fifteen curated outputs are an eyeball, not a measurement; the quarter's earlier swap showed exactly how much regression fifteen impressions can miss.

explanation: wrong-layer-fix — prompt caching changes unit economics, not capability; the committee's question was whether the newer model behaves better, which token pricing never answers.

explanation: prompt-as-guarantee: a stated constraint answers no cross-unit request at runtime; the rule still needs an executable control.

explanation: Trained alignment handles general harmful output, but unit-scoped access is deployment-specific, so it must be enforced by an application control; nothing downstream can enforce a rule that no layer encodes.

explanation: valid-but-early: a larger staging set would still pass, because the control itself was never built for cross-unit records.

explanation: FedRAMP compliance is a property of the environment, not the model: the reviewer accepts the route's authorization record together with evidence the workload stays exclusively inside it, an artifact that can be revalidated when configurations drift.
