text: Revert to self-review for context (restores the original bias)
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Share full generation context (destroys independence, reintroduces bias)
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Flag only issues found by both reviewers (intersection hides real bugs)
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Lower figure + footnote: conservative choice still drops evidence.
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Average both figures: fabricates a value neither source supports.
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Both values with attribution and dates -> coordinator reconciliation.
explanation: Conflicts need preserved attribution plus dates passed to the coordinator for reconciliation, not silent arbitrary choice or averaging.

text: Discard both for a third source: wastes evidence and delays synthesis.
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Single pass with longer context window (same attention dilution, same miss)
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Per-file reviews in dependency order only (no integration view, misses contract)
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Per-file reviews plus a separate integration pass on dataflow and contracts
explanation: Gate the review: per-file passes for local defects, then a dedicated integration pass on contracts and cross-service dataflow.

text: Review only per-file summaries (discards the very interface details needed)
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Exclude both as unreliable, discarding valid temporal signal.
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Keep only the recent figure, losing trend context.
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Average both years, fabricating a value from neither period.
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Include publication dates to interpret the shift temporally.
explanation: Different collection dates explain the shift. Including dates reframes the pair as temporal change, not contradiction.

text: Route everything to human review (discards working bug triage, overloads humans)
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Use self-review for security findings (reintroduces generation bias)
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Require two-instance agreement (doubles cost, still uncalibrated)
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Calibrate confidence thresholds per finding type on a labeled validation set
explanation: Confidence miscalibration is type-specific. Calibrate thresholds per finding type on a labeled set instead of one global cutoff.

text: Set the output judge to fail open so denied applicants always receive replies
explanation: convenience-over-safety: for decisions where a wrong pass causes harm, the guidance is failing closed, because an unscreened pass merely looks guarded.

text: A recorded discovery session note promising the experience the adjusters described
explanation: valid-but-early — Recording what was said preserves the preference, not the constraint; the design still cannot be tested or traced against it.

text: A capabilities list confirming which product features the adjusters will see
explanation: eval-blindness — A feature list carries no measurable target, so nothing in the agreement can fail, warn, or prove itself later.

text: A stakeholder preference rewritten into much more precise, technical-sounding vocabulary
explanation: louder-not-explicit — Translating the words alone still yields the experience preference; the constraint underneath it is what the design needs.

text: Testable, bounded constraints written as requirement rows with their assumptions labeled
explanation: The preference signals where to dig: only follow-up questions surface the latency target, integration rule, or failure path hiding underneath. Written as a requirement row with its assumption labeled, the item stays testable, bounded, and traceable to the business case rather than to architect preference.

text: Raising the classification model to the strongest tier currently offered
explanation: scale-not-strategy — Even the strongest models remain probabilistic, so the miss rate shrinks but never reaches the zero misses the wording promises.

text: Measured commitments: a target accuracy rate on a defined evaluation set
explanation: The system is probabilistic and no configuration makes its output a guarantee, so the commitment promises a measured accuracy rate on a defined evaluation set plus an escalation path for low-confidence shipments — a number someone can verify, rather than determinism nobody can deliver.

text: Bound tool turns with early-stop rules
explanation: A cuts chunks and retries; C bounds agentic turns with early stops. Costs: A costs recall validation; B costs discount theater on bloated volume; C costs stop-rule tuning; D costs blind quality loss.

text: Truncate outputs blindly across all cases
explanation: Blind truncation cuts output content without targeting waste, degrading answer quality across all cases indiscriminately.

text: Injection via docs: treat output as data
explanation: Injection is contained by treating outputs as data with input screening; excessive agency by least privilege plus tool gates. Prompt-only fixes and fail-open postings mismatch the risks.

text: Excessive agency: add a caution prompt
explanation: Excessive agency is a scope control problem; a caution prompt is probabilistic and does not restrict what tools the agent can actually invoke.

text: Filter outage: fail open to protect latency
explanation: Failing open during a filter outage lets unvetted content through, trading a safety control away to protect latency.

text: Excessive agency: least privilege plus gates
explanation: Injection is contained by treating outputs as data with input screening; excessive agency by least privilege plus tool gates. Prompt-only fixes and fail-open postings mismatch the risks.

text: Runbook, alerts, rationale, owner
explanation: What transfers is the ability to operate: runbook, alerting, rationale, and an owner. The system alone leaves operators unable to respond.

text: Source code and credentials only
explanation: Source code and credentials alone give operators no runbook, alerting, or rationale for detecting and responding to degradation.

text: Demo video and launch slides
explanation: A demo video and launch slides are launch artifacts; they contain no operational procedures or failure response.

text: Vendor support phone number
explanation: A vendor phone number is an escalation path at best and provides nothing for detecting or diagnosing degradation day to day.

text: RAG for guides, live API for orders
explanation: Conceptual guides suit semantic RAG with a live order API; exact IDs also need keyword fusion. Snapshots or one index preserve staleness.

text: Fuse BM25 with vectors for identifiers
explanation: Conceptual guides suit semantic RAG with a live order API; exact IDs also need keyword fusion. Snapshots or one index preserve staleness.

text: Snapshot work orders nightly into vectors
explanation: Nightly snapshots into vectors reproduce the 24% stale-answer problem; snapshots cannot reflect live order state.

text: Use one semantic index for everything
explanation: One semantic index serves conceptual guides poorly for exact WID-7734 identifiers and preserves snapshot staleness for orders.

text: Platform-wide autonomous agents resolving cases end to end
explanation: Platform-wide autonomous agents end to end demand the eval harness and safety maturity the team lacks, an unacceptable risk for a six-week audited launch.

text: Proven workflow plus LLM drafting with human approval
explanation: A six-week audited rollout favors proven workflow plus targeted LLM assistance; platform-wide autonomous agents need eval and safety maturity the date forbids.

text: Custom multi-agent swarm learning policies from live traffic
explanation: A swarm learning policies from live traffic produces unauditable, drifting behavior that regulators requiring audit trails cannot accept.

text: Experimental planner discovering new resolution paths in production
explanation: An experimental planner discovering resolution paths in production treats audited dispute handling as a research surface.

text: Renegotiate token rate keeping volume fixed
explanation: Renegotiating the token rate lowers unit price while every inefficiency in volume remains, so the 9-cent case barely moves toward 3 cents.

text: Deduplicate chunks and cache repeated prefixes
explanation: B/D cut quantity via dedup, caching, and bounded retries; A/C only reprice or scale unchanged volume. Costs: A costs unchanged volume at lower rate; B costs dedup validation; C costs headroom without

text: Raise concurrency limits without volume change
explanation: Raising concurrency limits adds headroom without changing per-case cost or volume, so neither budget nor p99 improves.

text: Cap retries with targeted fallback policy
explanation: B/D cut quantity via dedup, caching, and bounded retries; A/C only reprice or scale unchanged volume. Costs: A costs unchanged volume at lower rate; B costs dedup validation; C costs headroom without

text: Check caller roles via prompt instructions
explanation: Prompt-based role checks are advisory and bypassable; the privilege bypasses persist because enforcement is not server-side.

text: Authorize each payout call server-side
explanation: Bypasses need per-invocation server-side checks; untraceable payouts need I/O spans with outcome labels. Prompt checks and counters do neither.

text: Track aggregate success counters only now
explanation: Aggregate success counters average away the rare bypasses and provide no trace linking payout writes to an approval.

text: Trace tool I/O with outcome labels
explanation: Bypasses need per-invocation server-side checks; untraceable payouts need I/O spans with outcome labels. Prompt checks and counters do neither.

text: Automate standard renewals while preserving 2s SLA compliance
explanation: Efficiency requires both unit-cost reduction and SLA preservation; pure automation without the guardrail converts cost savings into breach penalties.

text: Automate renewals ignoring latency to maximize throughput gains
explanation: Ignoring latency maximizes throughput by converting cost savings into SLA breaches, the regression the board explicitly forbids.

text: Add agents researching each renewal history before quoting
explanation: Agents researching each renewal history before quoting add latency and cost per case, jeopardizing the SLA and the unit-cost goal.

text: Hire reviewers checking every automated renewal manually
explanation: Reviewers checking every automated renewal manually reintroduce human cost per case, erasing the efficiency the automation was meant to deliver.

text: Log every tool call together with its producing token
explanation: compliance-theater — logging records misuse after the fact; any foreign token is still accepted.

text: Issue a single shared service token for all sessions
explanation: convenience-over-safety — one shared token collapses per-user authorization and widens the blast radius.

text: Validate audience binding and mint a separate downstream token
explanation: Audience binding stops replayed foreign tokens at the door, and a separately minted downstream token replaces pass-through; both facts in the review are addressed.

text: State the token requirements in each tool description
explanation: prompt-as-guarantee — tool descriptions guide the model, they enforce nothing at the protocol layer.

text: Retrieve more chunks per query to raise recall
explanation: knobs-not-design — more of the same near-identical chunks raises noise, not discriminability.

text: Swap the embedding model for a larger variant
explanation: scale-not-strategy — serials that are near-identical stay near-identical in a larger embedding space.

text: Re-embed the manuals at each weekly publication
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — freshness improves, but the lexical miss on TR-90442-B remains.

text: Fuse keyword and vector search, weighted by query type
explanation: Keyword/exact matching wins where embeddings lose — the serial — and query-type weighting keeps concept questions on the vector side; both symptoms, one change.

text: Expand every tool description for clearer discrimination
explanation: louder-not-explicit — longer descriptions add tokens to every call; near-duplicates stay near-duplicates.

text: Prune unused and overlapping tools before adding more
explanation: Pruning the unused third shrinks exactly the surface the failures scale with, before the queued six enlarge it.

text: Move to a stronger model to handle the bigger catalogue
explanation: scale-not-strategy — failures grew with catalogue size, not with model capability.

text: Serve the catalogue through progressive discovery per intent
explanation: Progressive discovery keeps the model's working set at intent-size, so the queued growth stops compounding the error.

text: Ship direct now; revisit MCP at the second consumer
explanation: Direct meets the p99 today; the revisit trigger (second consumer) arrives next quarter, so the costly migration is not owed yet.

text: Wrap payments in MCP so the coming services inherit it
explanation: valid but early — inheritance benefits accrue next quarter while the p99 breach and new-host risk land this month.

text: Put MCP behind a cache to recover the added latency
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — a checkout check is not repeated within any TTL; the hop, and its latency, remain.

text: Proxy the launch through the existing chat agent's MCP
explanation: extra-hop — coupling the launch deadline to the chat agent's deploy adds the same latency problem it was meant to dodge.

text: Finish the four-category question set before proposing anything
explanation: The protective move is deliberately boring: run must-do, must-not-do, must-cost, and must-prove to completion before any sketch. A confident proposal is what makes a sponsor stop volunteering constraints, precisely the ones a compliance review later misses.

text: Treat each 'quick check' remark as a constraint
explanation: Every 'it's just a review' hides an architectural gate: who authorizes, when, and with what evidence. Chasing the remark costs one question; skipping it plants a constraint that resurfaces when changing the design costs most.

text: Demonstrate a prototype within the same week
explanation: gold-plating — a same-week prototype adds motion, not requirements; it does not recover the must-not-do and must-prove answers the call skipped.

text: What the choice gains for the initial design effort
explanation: louder-not-explicit — the gain was named and heard; repeating the simplicity argument cannot recover the element the approval actually lacked.

text: What the choice gives up at production retrieval quality
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — the sacrifice was partly covered when the per-call price came up; what was never spoken was the cost of the unwind.

text: What unwinding the decision costs at production volume
explanation: Every tradeoff carries three elements: what the choice gains, what it gives up, and what reversal costs once the system is built around it. The third is what most presentations skip; it turns a correct verdict into a defensible choice.

text: Whether the choice also alters the later compliance posture
explanation: compliance-theater — the posture question matters in regulated rooms, but this approval failed on a business number, not on an obligation.

text: One or two limitations named upfront as intentional scope
explanation: Naming one or two constraints in advance, framed as what the solution deliberately does not do, signals discipline. In regulated rooms a stated boundary reads as rigor, while a mid-flow discovery drops confidence. Less impressive, but trust that survives scrutiny.

text: Ask each engineer to mirror the conventions into their personal user settings
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — user-level settings are personal scope that no pasting keeps synchronized, so the drift continues across laptops exactly as before.

text: Version the conventions in an internal wiki and link it from onboarding
explanation: louder-not-explicit — a wiki page documents the baseline but nothing loads it into the assistant, so conventions reach nobody's session automatically.

text: Check the project instructions file and shared settings into the repository
explanation: Project-scoped instructions and settings are meant to be versioned in the repository, so every collaborator inherits identical conventions, permissions, and MCP configuration automatically from source control.

text: Upgrade everyone to the most capable model tier for consistent output behavior
explanation: scale-not-strategy — a larger model does not distribute shared permissions or project context; each laptop still starts from whatever was configured locally.

text: Bundle the procedure into an owner-managed plugin with version-controlled updates and rollback
explanation: Plugins carry the governance this failure exposed: version-controlled updates from a connected repository, group targeting, and a documented path back, so one bad edit stops shipping to everyone at once.

text: Split the work across subagents coordinated by one orchestrator
explanation: over-orchestration — a coordinator plus subagents adds delegation overhead where a single call covers the whole task.

text: Upgrade the loop to the largest reasoning model tier
explanation: scale-not-strategy — a bigger model does not fix a pattern that is wrong for a bounded, deterministic task and raises cost further.

text: Add a longer system prompt that forbids looping retries
explanation: prompt-as-guarantee — instructions are guidance, not enforcement, and leave the unnecessary agent loop in place.

text: Replace it with a single augmented call plus a schema
explanation: A bounded, single-shot extraction is the case for one augmented call: the simplest solution meeting the requirement comes first and structure is added only when a measured failure demands it, cutting the loop and its cost.

text: Index frequent snapshots of past order history for faster recall
explanation: valid-but-early — a prebuilt index serves stable reference material, but the contract here is with a value that changes minute to minute.

text: Make an external system the call-time source of truth
explanation: Retrieval indexes static documents and stale snapshots, so it is the wrong tool for values that change during the conversation; answering from live state queried at call time is exactly the mechanism the notes prescribe.

text: Fine-tune the model on past order records each quarter
explanation: stale-fact — weights learned last quarter carry yesterday's statuses, which is precisely the staleness the constraint rules out.

text: Cache frequently asked order answers at the network edge
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — caching answers shortens the path but still serves the 10:00 snapshot to the 10:05 question.

text: Route each classified ticket to its specialized single handler
explanation: Routing classifies an input and directs it to a specialized follow-up task, which is well suited when distinct categories are better handled separately; stable, well-understood categories are exactly the routing case, fixing both the overpay and the shallow handling.

text: Add one autonomous agent for every ticket category
explanation: over-orchestration — per-category agent loops are heavier than the dispatch to specialized single handlers they replace.

text: Cache the shared prompt prefix to cut token cost
explanation: premature-optimization — caching trims the cost of the wrong design while every ticket still takes one undifferentiated path.

text: Grow the catch-all prompt with instructions per category
explanation: louder-not-explicit — piling more instructions into one prompt stays less maintainable and never separates the categories.

text: Enable thinking by default since deeper reasoning reliably lifts accuracy
explanation: knobs-not-design — deeper reasoning helps some tasks, but the documented order still puts prompt optimization first at far less latency.

text: Enable thinking only when also upgrading to the strongest model
explanation: scale-not-strategy — pairing thinking with a bigger model stacks two latency costs before evaluations show either one is needed.

text: Exhaust prompt optimization first; think only if accuracy stays short
explanation: The documented rule: evaluate without thinking first, and enable extended thinking only when accuracy still misses requirements after prompt optimization. Thinking tokens are billed as output and add latency, which the two-second inline target pays for on every interaction.

text: Raise the sampling temperature so the generation explores more possibilities
explanation: knobs-not-design — temperature reshuffles word choice rather than adding the reasoning steps the failing scores want.

text: Keep stdio but tunnel the streams through a permanent SSH tunnel
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — a tunnel masks the hop, but stdio still requires the client to launch the server as a subprocess on the same machine.

text: Switch the integration to streamable HTTP across the two networks
explanation: stdio only works when client and server run on the same machine, while streamable HTTP carries the JSON messages between networked hosts, which is exactly what a second data center demands.

text: Embed the conversion service directly inside the pricing engine process
explanation: scale-not-strategy — collapsing the service into one application couples the pricing engine to conversion logic and answers nothing about the remote deployment requirement.

text: Duplicate the server beside each client and use stdio locally
explanation: gold-plating — duplicating the service beside every client multiplies deployment, versioning, and consistency work just to avoid a networked transport.

text: Fail over to a smaller model whenever 429 responses appear
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — a different model tier does not govern admission control; 429 responses concern request pacing, not model capability, so the incidents repeat.

text: Move to the enterprise tier so the rate limits disappear
explanation: scale-not-strategy — higher limits move the threshold, but the burst behavior, the 429 semantics, and the incident noise stay exactly the same.

text: Enqueue every single request through a second fairness-queueing service
explanation: over-orchestration — a queueing layer adds infrastructure between the caller and the API without implementing the documented cure for transient 429 and 529 responses.

text: Retry transient responses with exponential backoff, waits doubling each attempt
explanation: 429 and 529 are transient conditions that normally clear with backoff, so exponentially longer waits, typically doubling each attempt, absorb the afternoon bursts without ever failing the whole rebalancing run.

text: The client's InitializeRequest triggers a capabilities reply from the server
explanation: valid-but-early — the InitializeRequest does open the exchange, but it names only the first message; the early failures come from tool calls fired before the exchange completed.

text: The Initialized Notification requires a matching result from the server
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — the Initialized Notification is the one handshake message sent without expecting any reply, so awaiting a result stalls every connection at startup.

text: Agent for both, because both follow several gates
explanation: over-orchestration — granting a planning loop to work whose order is known adds unpredictability the filing process never benefits from.

text: Agent for both, since both take several steps
explanation: over-orchestration — granting planning autonomy to a fixed extract-validate-quote chain pays for flexibility the sequence never uses.

text: Workflow for both, hardened until forensics becomes predictable
explanation: prompt-as-guarantee — predefining steps for an inquiry whose next step is discovered mid-task replaces adaptation with guesswork.

text: Single augmented call for both, keeping the design simplest
explanation: valid-but-early — sufficient for the extraction step alone, but neither a fixed sequence nor adaptive investigation fits in one call.

text: Fixed workflow for quotes, autonomous agent for forensics
explanation: A workflow wires fixed steps in your code, exactly what a requirement that never varies needs; the investigation whose path emerges from intermediate results is the case for an agent planning its sequence. Each requirement gets the pattern it needs.

text: The synthesis is strictly linear, each step consuming the previous
explanation: over-orchestration — a dependent sequence is prompt chaining, not parallel breadth-first work; splitting it into agents adds coordination the task cannot use.

text: The problem is breadth-first with many independently explorable directions
explanation: Multi-agent systems earn their keep on breadth-first queries: many independent directions can be pursued at once, which is precisely the shape of a landscape scan.

text: Reducing total token consumption per run is the primary goal
explanation: scale-not-strategy — multi-agent designs spend more tokens than a single chat, so picking them to cut cost inverts the documented trade-off.

text: Every thread's source material exceeds a single context window
explanation: When source material exceeds one window, parallel subagents each carrying their own isolated window is exactly the mechanism that helps; isolated context per subagent is what raises coverage without overflowing.

text: Restate the verification rule once more at the prompt's start
explanation: louder-not-explicit — repeating wording adds emphasis, not an enforcement point; the payout can still precede verification.

text: Raise the model tier so that instruction adherence improves
explanation: scale-not-strategy — adherence improves statistically while the requirement stays probabilistic, which the controller does not accept.

text: Add a programmatic precondition that blocks payouts before verification
explanation: Programmatic enforcement, hooks and preconditions, gives a deterministic guarantee where prompt guidance stays probabilistic; blocking the downstream call until a verified customer ID exists is exactly the mechanism for requirements that must never be skipped.

text: Summarize the twelve confirmation flows into the policy prompt
explanation: prompt-as-guarantee — an enlarged prompt documents what should happen while the ordering still depends on the model remembering it.

text: Knowledge boundary, since new resume formats appeared
explanation: stale-fact — nothing in the incident is about training data; the same inputs produced differing outputs.

text: Context rot, because long sessions degraded recall
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — accuracy here degraded across identical short jobs, not inside an accumulating session window.

text: Non-determinism, so demos cannot certify repeated behavior
explanation: The same input can produce different outputs across runs, which is why evaluation frameworks exist: you cannot certify behavior you only observed once; a clean demo is not evidence of determinism.

text: Working-memory limits, because documents exceeded the window
explanation: scale-not-strategy — the requests were small; a window ceiling would return errors, not divergent categorizations.

text: The four discovery buckets: do, not-do, cost, prove
explanation: A preference like seamless signals that discovery is needed, not a requirement; forcing the statement into what the system must do, must not do, must cost, and must prove turns it into testable, bounded constraints the design can build against.

text: A reference architecture that realizes the stated preference
explanation: valid-but-early — the pattern matters, but selecting it against an untested experience word inherits assumptions into the design.

text: A translation of the vendor's preferences into constraints
explanation: valid-but-early — translating is the right move, but without the four question buckets the yield stays whatever happens to come up.

text: The escalation path for cases the assistant cannot resolve
explanation: valid-but-early — a handoff rule is one likely constraint, yet it emerges from the must-not-do category rather than anchoring the whole call.

text: The direct route, for flexibility in renegotiating the agreement
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — the route is chosen for the cloud commitment, while the entry point serves the user, so one layer cannot dictate the others.

text: AWS Bedrock, because the existing BAA agreement covers it
explanation: compliance-theater — the same model underneath does not merge the questions; each layer answers to a different stakeholder.

text: Google Vertex, since another health network runs there
explanation: Entry point is chosen for the user and the work, build-time interface for the engineering team, delivery route for cloud commitments and compliance posture; three conversations with three different stakeholders, and one layer rarely dictates the others.

text: Microsoft Foundry, to diversify the model provider dependency further
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — convenience for the coding team answers the build-time question only and leaves the audience and procurement decisions unfixed.

text: The direct route, for flexibility in renegotiating the agreement
explanation: valid-but-early — flexibility is real but costs a second agreement negotiation, while one route is already covered.

text: AWS Bedrock, because the existing agreement covers it
explanation: Governance and regulated-industry constraints rule out a route before any cost or latency trade-off applies; the agreement that already covers the governed configuration closes the compliance question, exactly how the healthcare-network case is decided in the notes.

text: Google Vertex, since another capital-markets desk runs there
explanation: stale-fact — another deployment's precedent does not extend this network's agreement; coverage is what decides.

text: Run claude init per clone; costs rework, misses custom rules
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Move conventions to project .claude/CLAUDE.md and commit
explanation: User-level ~/.claude applies only to one workstation; project .claude/CLAUDE.md is versioned and shared.

text: Serve via MCP config; costs infra, bypasses versioning
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Commit entire ~/.claude/; costs leaking personal settings
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Add max_tokens and prompt rule to check both tools — keeps overlap, wastes calls
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Rename to classify_ticket_intent; rewrite both with distinct contracts and boundaries
explanation: Distinct names and non-overlapping I/O contracts fix selection at the source. Merging loses precision; prompt tricks keep ambiguity.

text: Merge into one process_ticket tool — loses precision, returns unneeded data
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Add few-shot prompt examples only — fragile, overlap remains
explanation: Defensible but weaker than the credited key(s).

text: Microsoft Foundry, to diversify the model provider dependency
explanation: gold-plating — adding a third route adds procurement and operations surface with no requirement in the brief behind it.

text: The accumulated history finally reached the window limit
explanation: stale-fact — the scenario says the window is far from its limit; an exceeded edge errors the request instead of bending recall.

text: Attention degraded well before the window's hard limit
explanation: Context that accumulates turn over turn pays cost and latency scaling linearly with input, and attention quality can degrade on long contexts well before the hard limit; that is the mid-morning codes coming unstitched while the morning answers stayed accurate.

text: The model tier is too small for billing work
explanation: scale-not-strategy — the morning answers were correct on the same tier; capability is not what changed by late afternoon.

text: A prompt edit shifted the insurance code definitions
explanation: prompt-as-guarantee — nothing reports a prompt change, and the same instructions produced the correct morning codes.

text: Enable a second breakpoint immediately after the promotions banner
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — a second breakpoint still freezes a prefix that changes on every call, so reads stay near zero.

text: Move the static policy text into each user message
explanation: knobs-not-design — relocating blocks does not alone create a stable prefix; the dynamic fields still lead every request.

text: Place the dynamic fields after the policy and breakpoint there
explanation: Caches match identical prefixes, and a breakpoint marks where the prefix ends. With dynamic fields first, the shared static tail sits after them, so nothing before the breakpoint repeats; ordering static content first, with the breakpoint on its last block, turns the policy into cheap reads.

text: Double the model tier so the long prompt processes faster
explanation: scale-not-strategy — the prompt already fits the window; a bigger model changes neither the prefix order nor its reuse.

text: Resend the complete conversation history with every new API request
explanation: The API is stateless: it stores nothing between requests, so memory lives entirely in what the client resends. Appending each assistant reply and sending the full history restores the reference every follow-up question needs.

text: Store the transcript in the portal and show it above replies
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — a readable transcript improves the interface while the model still never receives prior turns in the request.

text: Tell the model inside the prompt to remember earlier answers
explanation: prompt-as-guarantee — instructions cannot reference turns the request never carried; guidance does not substitute for the missing history.

text: Lower the sampling temperature so replies track the newest question
explanation: knobs-not-design — sampling controls affect wording variety, not which turns of the conversation reach the model.

text: The one-hour cache lifetime expires between these sparse calls
explanation: stale-fact — the hour matters only after something qualifies; nothing here ever entered the cache to expire.

text: Raise every diagnostic prompt above one thousand padded tokens
explanation: valid-but-early — padding prompts past the threshold can qualify them, yet short, varying diagnostics rarely amortize the write.

text: Cache the generated answers so repeated questions skip generation
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — the cache stores input preprocessing work, not the generated answers, so copying questions buys nothing.

text: Content below the 1024-token minimum never qualifies for caching
explanation: Caching has a minimum threshold: everything being cached must sum to at least 1024 tokens. These brief, ever-changing diagnostics sit far under it, so each request is processed and billed as ordinary input and usage shows no read.

text: Prompt caching stores the generated answers rather than the input
explanation: stale-fact — the cache stores input preprocessing work, so the model still generates every answer fresh at reply time.

text: Cached prefixes still occupy the window; caching changes their price
explanation: A cached prefix remains fully present in the context; the usage fields distinguish cheap cache reads from fresh processing. Caching is a billing optimization, so the fix for sagging late-conversation quality is curation, not a billing change.

text: Cache reads prove the history no longer consumes window space
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — reads measure the billing side, not occupancy; the cached prefix still sits fully in the window, so a read proves price, never presence.

text: Changing one character inside the cached prefix forces a fresh write
explanation: Cache content must be identical up to the breakpoint; even adding one word invalidates it and pushes the changed portion through a fresh, costlier cache write.

text: Move every workload to the flagship because premium quality pays
explanation: scale-not-strategy — the most capable tier spends more on workloads whose quality the labeled outputs already measure.

text: Logging every classification so that any disputed shipment can be audited later
explanation: compliance-theater — Auditing documents breaches after they occur but leaves the promised wording unchanged, so every miss still triggers the same dispute.

explanation: wrong-layer-fix — Availability was never the disputed dimension; the wording outran the probabilistic technology, so changing the promise's subject answers a question nobody asked.

explanation: Each discovery item becomes one row: the statement, the constraint it implies, the decision that constraint forces, and any assumption documented when it is not yet confirmed. Volume and the explainability duty are requirements; the changing policy stays only an assumption until it is confirmed with the stakeholder.

text: A capability agreement enumerating what the assistant will do for reviewers
explanation: valid-but-early — It records the preference, not the constraint; nothing in it is testable, so later design choices cannot trace back to the enrollment facts.

explanation: Private settings cannot be shared through git and will diverge per developer.

explanation: An untracked file is never distributed to the team.

text: A single requirement: latency under one second, assumed for every reviewer
explanation: eval-blindness — One metric cannot carry the volume, proof, and change-frequency constraints; whatever goes unstated gets inherited silently by the design.

text: A backlog noting each fact for review once a prototype exists
explanation: convenience-over-safety — Deferring the record lets the confident sketch end the questions; unstated constraints survive into compliance review, where redesign costs the most.

text: Volume, latency, and error rate say the system runs, not what it changed
explanation: Technical metrics confirm the deployment runs, but none of them are a business outcome. The fields that answer the CFO are the before-and-after on the business metric the use case targeted, backed by the control that makes the comparison auditable rather than asserted.

text: The document needed shorter sections so executives read past the first page
explanation: valid-but-early — Tighter sections would not have added what is missing; the document proves the deployment runs, which was never what the CFO asked it to prove.

text: The targeted business metric's before-and-after and its auditable control were never captured
explanation: The before value is what turns the after number into a story, and the control is what turns the comparison into evidence instead of assertion. Those fields exist for a different reader than the observability stack: the sponsor who must justify the deployment upward.

text: The observability stack exporting its operational metrics more slowly than needed
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — The failure sits in the document's fields, not its sources; the metrics were collected, they simply were never the ones a CFO could spend on.

text: Threshold alerts on the error rate so any slowdown pages someone
explanation: convenience-over-safety — The drift never breached the error threshold, so another alert wired to the same metric reproduces the silence it was meant to end.

text: A longer retention window so weeks of history stay directly comparable
explanation: scale-not-strategy — The signals were already collected and visible; deeper history changes what is stored, not who decides a signal matters.

text: A monthly summary report sent to every stakeholder on the loop
explanation: compliance-theater — Reporting distributes what happened, but no rule decides it mattered; the ninety-day trace already had attentive readers and still produced no review.

text: A governance table mapping each signal to its trigger, owner, and action
explanation: Monitoring is not a feedback loop: a dashboard collects and displays signals, while the loop maps each signal to a trigger, an owner, and a required action. Slow score drift never crossed the error threshold, so only a governance row defined before launch would have forced the stakeholder review.

text: Read access to the design sessions' recordings and working chat archives
explanation: valid-but-early — The reasoning exists in the recordings but never reached the page; reconstructing it from archives is exactly what fails, and the rationale dies with the archives' context.

text: The decision log records the rejected alternative and the tradeoff each choice resolved
explanation: The completeness test is whether a competent architect who was not in the room can make a safe change. explanation: gold-plating — Availability extends effort, not reasoning; purchased hours cannot tell the successor which choice the residency constraint made load-bearing.

explanation: Merging makes routing ambiguity worse by widening the single tool's applicability, and preserving successful empty results during outages means an access failure is still indistinguishable from no matches, so the incorrect refund still happens.

text: Rewrite misrouted fetch calls in a post-use hook after execution.
explanation: Rewriting after execution means the wrong tool has already run with the wrong reference, so side effects or bad data may already have landed. Misrouting must be fixed at selection time through clear tool boundaries, not patched retroactively.

text: Remove ambiguous verbs only from the system prompt text.
explanation: Tool descriptions, not the system prompt, are the primary selection signal, so editing prompt wording leaves the broad fetch tool overlapping the dedicated tools. The ambiguity that causes misrouting remains intact.

text: Scope external retrieval to its tool; reserve customer/local data.
explanation: The broad fetcher overlaps dedicated tools. Scoping external retrieval to its tool and reserving customer/local data for dedicated tools removes ambiguity at selection time.

text: Extend the customer tool to retrieve every URL and file.
explanation: Widening the customer tool increases the overlap instead of removing it, making selection between it and the local-file tool even more ambiguous. This moves in the opposite direction from a clear per-tool contract.

text: Force the SQL tool on every turn and forbid DROP in prose.
explanation: Forcing on every turn over-corrects: the SQL tool should only be forced on query turns, and a prose prohibition on destructive statements is not an enforcement mechanism and can be ignored by the model.

text: Use any tool choice and block destructive output afterward.
explanation: Leaving choice as any does not solve the skipped-execution problem, and filtering the output afterward means the destructive statement may already have been generated; blocking must happen server-side before execution.

text: Keep auto choice and rely on a read-only tool description.
explanation: Auto choice is exactly why the tool is sometimes skipped, and a description claiming read-only is only advisory — the model can still issue destructive statements that nothing deterministically rejects.

text: Force SQL only for query turns and reject DDL/DML server-side.
explanation: Skipped execution needs forced routing on query turns; destructive input needs server-side rejection. Prompt prose or output filtering alone is bypassable.

text: Replace the general tool with tenant-scoped domain tools.
explanation: Tenant-scoped tools enforce boundaries; structured partial-failure errors stop masked outages. Together they fix isolation and observability; either alone is incomplete.

text: Return structured partial-failure errors instead of silent success.
explanation: Tenant-scoped tools enforce boundaries; structured partial-failure errors stop masked outages. Together they fix isolation and observability; either alone is incomplete.

explanation: A tenant_id parameter does not give the tool a scoped description that improves selection in a large toolset, and keeping silent partial success still masks outages so downstream decisions keep consuming incomplete data.

text: Inject missing tenant fields after the tool returns.
explanation: Post-return field injection is a cosmetic fix: it neither establishes tenant isolation at the data-access boundary nor surfaces partial outages, so silently incomplete results still propagate into downstream decisions.

text: Block refunds only when account_id is null.
explanation: The account_id is present in this scenario, so the gate never fires; the problem is a pending verification status being read as verified. Null-checking an unrelated field does nothing to stop the refund.

text: Return transient indeterminate error; require verified status to refund.
explanation: Success with pending status must not read as verified. A transient indeterminate error plus a verified-status gate blocks the refund cascade and permits retry.

text: Use auto tool choice so verification can be skipped in outages.
explanation: Skipping verification during an outage makes the refund decision even less informed, and tool choice has no bearing on how a pending verification status is interpreted. This would widen the failure, not gate it.

text: Add 'verify first' instruction to the refund tool description.
explanation: A description instruction is advisory prose, not an authorization check: the coordinator can still read a pending status as verified and issue the refund. Enforcement must be a deterministic gate on verified status.

text: Keep only the output advice filter
explanation: Malicious upload content is consumed on the input path before any response is generated, so it never reaches an output-only filter intact. Dropping input screening leaves the injection and PII risks entirely uncovered.

text: Screen uploads at input, answers at output
explanation: Uploads need deterministic input screening for injection/PII while answers need output screening for disallowed advice. One output filter cannot cover both decision points.

text: Add a prompt to ignore bad uploads
explanation: A prompt instruction is probabilistic and can itself be overridden by injected content inside the uploads, so it cannot serve as a deterministic screening control for untrusted input.

explanation: Caching reduces cost of the catalog but keeps all 140 schemas consuming context every turn.

text: A consumption forecast at production volume with the spend-control posture named
explanation: Cost is the expectation that breaks most often: production volume routinely runs one to two orders of magnitude above the pilot. A consumption forecast at expected volume, with caching, model tiering, and budget alerts named, frames the spend story before the first invoice.

text: A rollout pause until every prompt is retuned for the token cost
explanation: premature-optimization — Tuning before production volume arrives optimizes blind; the forecast and control posture are what the first invoice rewards, and tuning follows measured usage.

text: Candidate patterns with the tradeoffs each gives, gives up, and risks
explanation: Arriving with a candidate pattern whose tradeoffs are already named means the session refines choices and tests assumptions instead of assembling basics. What each option gives, gives up, and risks is the shared starting point that keeps the conversation worth the specialists' time.

explanation: valid-but-early — A finished, priced design forecloses exactly the refinement the session exists for; you bring a point of view, not a verdict.

explanation: gold-plating — The discovery work and demo already proved problem understanding; a rehearsed showcase adds enthusiasm while answering none of the questions this session was called to resolve.

text: Open questions scoped to what only the Applied AI specialists can answer
explanation: The session exists to resolve questions needing specialist input: model behavior, scaling constraints, evaluation approach, or safety considerations. Requirements and candidate patterns arrive prepared; only what the Applied AI team is best positioned to answer deserves to be asked inside the session itself.

text: The approving agent reuses the producing session's context, assumptions, and blind spots
explanation: The champion absorbs early friction, builds local examples, and becomes first-line support so the Architect is not the single question-answering dependency, while batch seeding deliberately spreads usage instead of leaving it to early enthusiasts.

text: Freeze licenses until usage parity is reached, then relaunch adoption all at once
explanation: valid-but-early: parity is the outcome, not the mechanism; an all-hands relaunch recreates the spike of confused first-time prompts the notes warn produces a quiet retreat to old habits.

text: Mandate weekly usage reports per engineer so laggards are identified and coached individually
explanation: louder-not-explicit: measurement documents lumpy adoption without spreading it; the champion-and-batch pattern, not surveillance, is what deliberately distributes usage beyond enthusiasts.

text: Consolidate everyone into one department's proven workflow so a single expert supports everyone
explanation: scale-not-strategy: a single expert recreates the Architect-as-bottleneck problem at larger scale; enablement must travel through a local champion per department, not through one central power user.

text: The approving agent reuses the producing session's context, assumptions, and blind spots
explanation: stale-fact: intent.md is human-readable and machine-actionable precisely so anyone can read it; format, not permissions, and format never explains why self-review misses its own blind spots.

text: Auditing rules forbid one Claude instance from holding both author and reviewer roles
explanation: compliance-theater: the requirement is an architectural consequence of shared context, not a regulatory convention; naming an audit rule describes the paperwork, not the mechanism that makes a same-session review weaker.

text: Model context limits mean the reviewing session no longer fits the production conversation
explanation: wrong-layer-fix: even with infinite context, the reviewer would still share the same assumptions and blind spots; the independence requirement comes from reasoning, not from capacity.

text: The approving agent inherits the producing session's context, assumptions, and blind spots
explanation: A session reviewing its own output shares the same context and reasoning path that produced the error, so the mistake looks consistent and passes; only a separate check — a deterministic gate or an adversarial reviewing agent — can decide the output on fresh evidence.

text: Record the corrected pattern in the project CLAUDE.md so future agent sessions inherit it
explanation: extra-hop: human review adds a dependency the AI-native loop is meant to collapse; each review catches one instance while the knowledge stays in one head instead of becoming machine-readable team configuration.

text: Pin the project to the model version that happened to regenerate the consumer correctly
explanation: knobs-not-design: model choice governs capability, not institutional memory; pinning the version neither records the acknowledgment-mode convention nor stops the next agent on the next checkout repeating it.

text: Record the corrected pattern in the project CLAUDE.md so every future session inherits it
explanation: The AI-native build stage maintains institutional knowledge as versioned machine-readable CLAUDE.md files: a lesson captured once in the repository travels with the code, so agents on every checkout apply the convention without the quirk's expert being present.

text: Add the acknowledgment-mode rule as an inline comment in whichever consumer happens to fail next
explanation: valid-but-early: comments educate whoever opens one file, while CLAUDE.md is loaded by every session project-wide; a comment documents one instance rather than encoding the convention as shared configuration.

text: Managed settings apply only when engineers authenticate from approved corporate networks
explanation: stale-fact: managed settings deploy via MDM or the admin console and bind regardless of network location; a network-conditional statement describes nothing about hooks, which are enforced by the action, not by the connection.

text: The gate condition is enforced on every action, for everyone, without exception
explanation: A hook is an approval gate, so the condition runs each time the governed action occurs for every user; allow and block decisions are logged with a timestamp, giving leadership the durable, checkable enforcement record rather than discretionary review.

text: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly lets each engineer enable additional hooks from their own repository
explanation: wrong-layer-fix: that key widens nothing per engineer — it stops project files and command-line flags from widening permission rules; it governs permission rules, not the separate question of which hooks may run alongside the managed ones.

text: Each gate defines what counts as approval, such as an approved change ticket
explanation: The gate itself defines the approval criterion — an approved change ticket or the release manager's sign-off — so the production boundary is a documented condition the hook enforces, not a judgment call left to whoever runs the deploy that day.

text: Expose tool search, load schemas on demand
explanation: Accuracy clears target; tokens and p99 breach. On-demand schemas fix the failing cost/latency half.

text: Recommend cheaper option, name sacrifice, set trigger
explanation: Trade-off communication costs both options, recommends one, names the sacrifice, and sets a revisit trigger. No recommendation or unstated cost avoids informed consent.

text: Rewrite all eighteen tool descriptions with much longer, detailed wording
explanation: louder-not-explicit — longer descriptions do not remove the overlap that produced the misselections; eighteen partly relevant tools still ride along on every single call.

text: Scope each conversation's toolset to the four or five role-relevant tools
explanation: Selection reliability drops as the registered tool count grows, so each conversation performs best when it sees only the handful of tools its role actually needs, with cross-role utilities narrowly granted.

text: Upgrade to a stronger model before touching any tool configuration
explanation: scale-not-strategy — a stronger model does not shrink the catalogue that diluted selection; the traced billing-utility misselections would recur on the same eighteen choices.

text: Force the model to justify its choice before every invocation
explanation: knobs-not-design — a spoken justification adds latency and tokens while the competing, oversized catalogue that caused the wrong pick remains unchanged.

text: Retrieve the newest dispatch snapshot from the nightly indexed corpus
explanation: stale-fact — a snapshot that was correct at ten can be wrong at 10:05, because retrieved data may already be stale by the time the model reads it.

text: Re-embed the dispatch corpus every fifteen minutes around the clock
explanation: knobs-not-design — quarter-hourly re-embedding narrows the staleness window but never closes it, and dispatch state keeps moving between indexing runs.

text: Increase retrieval depth so more tracking articles reach the context
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — deeper retrieval raises recall over the same stored articles; the returned-to-depot case stays wrong until the next nightly indexing run completes.

text: Call the dispatch system through a tool whenever status is needed
explanation: Retrieval suits static or slow-moving knowledge, but an answer that changes by the minute needs the system of record, so a tool call to dispatch delivers the true current state at question time.

text: Retry the timeout with backoff and keep successful partials.
explanation: Timeout is retryable, invalid range is locally repairable, quota exhaustion must propagate with partial coverage. Blanket retries waste calls and discard useful partials.

text: Repair the invalid date range locally without another call.
explanation: Timeout is retryable, invalid range is locally repairable, quota exhaustion must propagate with partial coverage. Blanket retries waste calls and discard useful partials.

text: Propagate quota status with explicit partial-result coverage.
explanation: Timeout is retryable, invalid range is locally repairable, quota exhaustion must propagate with partial coverage. Blanket retries waste calls and discard useful partials.

text: Retry every failure uniformly, then return one generic error.
explanation: A uniform retry treats a non-retryable validation error and a permanent quota exhaustion as if they were transient, wasting calls without progress, and collapsing everything into one generic error discards which partial results succeeded — exactly the coverage the caller needs.

text: Move both checks into one output filter
explanation: Upload content is screened on the input path and never appears intact at the output filter, so a single output check cannot cover both decision points. The guarded path requires distinct control points per path.

text: Return retryable transient error and mark affected stock unknown.
explanation: Null conflates genuinely out-of-stock with unreachable warehouse. A retryable transient error plus unknown marking blocks backorder creation and enables retry.

text: Treat null as unknown through prompt instructions alone.
explanation: Prompt instructions are advisory: the tool still returns null, so the conflation between a confirmed empty result and an access failure persists in the data itself. Downstream consumers reading the raw value can still trigger backorders.

text: Force another stock call whenever any null value appears.
explanation: Forcing a retry on every null wastes calls on legitimately out-of-stock items, and if the warehouse remains unreachable the second call returns null again, so backorder creation is still possible.

text: The sacrificed cost term was never stated
explanation: An approval without the stated downside is not informed consent even with quorum and agenda. The recall and latency cost was never put forward.

text: The approval quorum was too small here
explanation: Quorum size does not affect the validity of the decision; the flaw is that the board approved without hearing the cost, not that too few people voted.

text: The meeting ran without a formal agenda
explanation: An agenda is procedural hygiene, not the substance of informed consent; a fully documented agenda would not have fixed the unstated downside.

text: The decision lacked a second vendor bid
explanation: Competitive bidding is a procurement practice unrelated to informed consent; a single vendor's option can be approved validly if its trade-offs are disclosed.

text: Write assumptions and constraints down early
explanation: Sound discovery writes assumptions down, converts vague terms into failure conditions, and reconciles conflicts explicitly. Designing past hints or locking dates first are gate violations.

text: Design past a constraint mentioned in passing
explanation: A constraint surfaced in passing is unconfirmed, so designing past it risks building directly into an unstated legal or operational violation.

text: Convert vague terms into failure conditions
explanation: Sound discovery writes assumptions down, converts vague terms into failure conditions, and reconciles conflicts explicitly. Designing past hints or locking dates first are gate violations.

text: Lock the launch date before requirements exist
explanation: Committing a date before requirements exist forces design decisions to fit an arbitrary deadline instead of the actual testable criteria.

text: Scope every rule to file paths, including planning rules.
explanation: Incorrect: planning-critical rules are needed before any file is edited, so path-scoping all rules would hide them during planning.

text: Scope editing-only rules to their relevant file paths.
explanation: Correct: editing-only rules load only when relevant, preserving planning context.

text: Compact repeatedly while keeping all imports global.
explanation: Incorrect: compaction does not remove the global import bloat and can discard useful planning history.

text: Keep planning-critical rules imported during planning.
explanation: Correct: these rules inform decisions before edits begin.

text: Lengthen every tool description text
explanation: Longer descriptions add tokens and still leave all 42 tools competing for selection.

text: Add retries on wrong-tool calls
explanation: Retrying wrong calls multiplies cost without fixing the routing itself.

text: Upgrade model to follow instructions
explanation: Correct-tool accuracy is already 0.93; the model follows fine once routed correctly.

text: Scope minimal tool subset per task
explanation: Correct-tool accuracy clears target; excess capability drives misrouting. Least-privilege subsets cut the wrong-tool rate.

text: Merge all conventions into one root file; delete local files.
explanation: Merging everything into one root file loses locality and assumes local guidance automatically overrides root imports, which is not guaranteed.

text: Assume local guidance overrides all root imports automatically.
explanation: Local guidance does not automatically override all root imports; assuming it does leaves conflicting rules active.

text: Scope modern rules to non-legacy paths; drop global import.
explanation: Scoping modern rules to non-legacy paths stops global pollution while keeping local legacy guidance authoritative.

text: Keep modern rules global; remove only legacy root import.
explanation: Keeping modern rules global leaves them polluting legacy paths even after removing the legacy import.

text: Commit testing standards to versioned project rules.
explanation: Versioned project rules fix portability: every clone and CI run receives the same standards.

text: Require testing fields in the structured output schema.
explanation: Schema fields constrain output shape but cannot share tacit testing standards across machines.

text: Keep user config; append existing tests to each prompt.
explanation: Keeping user config preserves the single point of failure and appends tests without sharing the standards.

text: Review generated tests with an independent instance.
explanation: An independent reviewer has no stake in the implementation, removing self-review bias.

text: Document assets in CLAUDE.md and ask manual recreation.
explanation: Documenting for manual recreation causes drift: each developer recreates a different artifact.

text: Copy assets manually during each developer onboarding.
explanation: Manual copying adds toil and invites divergence between copies over time.

text: Share the lead's full home config via a dotfiles repository.
explanation: Sharing a personal dotfiles repository leaks unrelated personal configuration into team machines.

text: Move assets to project .claude dirs tracked in version control.
explanation: Project .claude directories tracked in version control make assets portable to every clone as a governed artifact.

text: Delegate discovery to subagents returning concise evidence.
explanation: Subagents with evidence summaries keep the main context lean and grounded.

text: Load all files during planning before implementation.
explanation: Loading everything upfront centralizes bloat and causes the same degradation.

text: Fan out one reader per file and merge unrelated summaries.
explanation: One reader per file multiplies sessions without relevance filtering, returning noise.

text: Compact on a fixed cadence and continue in one session.
explanation: Compacting an already overloaded session risks losing specific evidence.

text: Planning mode without supplying or discovering tests.
explanation: Planning mode does not supply the existing tests or standards the generator needs.

text: Additional abstract input-output examples in instructions.
explanation: More abstract examples repeat the gap; they cannot reveal actual helpers or library conventions.

text: Relevant existing tests plus shared testing standards.
explanation: Existing tests plus shared standards supply reusable helpers, library choice, and edge cases that abstract examples omit.

text: Schema naming the required library and helper reuse.
explanation: A schema can name requirements but cannot ground generation in the actual test suite.

text: Always disable isolation to inherit full conversation.
explanation: Disabling isolation bloats the skill context with unrelated conversation history.

text: Pass a concise design summary in the skill invocation.
explanation: An explicit summary preserves isolation benefits while bridging the visibility gap.

text: Compact the parent and assume the fork receives history.
explanation: Compaction relies on a false inheritance mechanism; an isolated skill does not receive parent history.

text: Let the skill read the parent log directly from disk.
explanation: Reading parent logs from disk does not transfer the relevant decisions and invites context noise.

text: Plan silently and infer all requirements from the code.
explanation: Silent inference hallucinates requirements instead of exposing the consistency and failure constraints.

text: Implement during interview after the first partial answer.
explanation: Implementing after the first partial answer risks rework once the real constraints surface.

text: Execute directly with a popular cache and default policy.
explanation: Executing with defaults risks silent policy assumptions on invalidation and failure behavior.

text: Plan plus ask targeted questions on consistency and failure.
explanation: Planning plus targeted questions resolves consistency, invalidation, and failure modes before commitment.

text: Provide prior findings and request only new or unfixed issues.
explanation: A fresh run has no memory, so prior findings must be supplied explicitly with a new-only filter.

text: Switch to free-text output to ease manual comparison.
explanation: Free-text output loses the structure needed for automated deduplication and comparison.

text: Use planning mode so the reviewer recalls prior runs.
explanation: Planning mode does not supply prior state; a stateless rerun still has no memory of earlier findings.

text: Add an inferred flag for previously reported findings.
explanation: An inferred flag has no data to infer from without the prior findings being supplied.

text: Add domain categories as required schema output values.
explanation: Schema categories enforce output shape but cannot replace semantic review knowledge.

text: Convert criteria to environment variables for the prompt.
explanation: Environment variables bloat every invocation and bypass the versioned shared baseline.

text: Run from the project root so project guidance loads.
explanation: Project CLAUDE.md loads by working directory, so running from the root restores the versioned domain criteria.

text: Duplicate all criteria into every CI prompt unconditionally.
explanation: Duplicating criteria into prompts creates drift from the maintained project baseline.

text: Return only the concise answer
explanation: A concise answer alone gives auditors nothing to verify against.

text: Return separate summary and evidence fields
explanation: Separate fields let users read the summary while auditors check the evidence without mixing them.

text: Put all evidence in the user greeting
explanation: Burying evidence in a greeting hides it from both audiences and is not machine-readable.

text: Hide evidence from every output
explanation: Hiding evidence makes audit verification impossible.

text: Build an eval set and compare prompt variants against it
explanation: A fixed eval set built from failures lets the team measure whether a variant really fixes the problem.

text: Change several prompts at once without measurement
explanation: Changing several prompts at once makes it impossible to know which change helped or hurt.

text: Choose the longest prompt
explanation: Length is not a quality criterion and adds token cost without evidence of improvement.

text: Test only the happiest path
explanation: Testing only the happy path misses exactly the failures the saved examples represent.

text: Ask for numbers in natural language
explanation: Prose requests do not enforce a type; the model can still emit text totals.

text: Define the field as a number in the JSON Schema
explanation: Typing the field as a number enforces machine-readable output and fails fast on violations.

text: Re-add Read access even though the skill already has it.
explanation: Read is already granted; re-adding it does not provide discovery of existing tests or naming patterns.

text: Grant Grep and Glob for discovery of tests and helpers.
explanation: Without Grep and Glob the skill cannot discover helpers or naming patterns, so it hallucinates duplicates.

text: Remove all tool limits and grant unrestricted access.
explanation: Unlimited tools add risk without addressing the missing discovery capability.

text: Remove isolation so the skill inherits full conversation.
explanation: Removing isolation inherits unrelated conversation noise instead of targeted discovery.

text: Fix and review directly in the same conversation.
explanation: Same-session review repeats the author's confirmation bias; the reviewer rationalizes its own changes.

text: Fix trivial failures directly without full planning.
explanation: A trivial one-file syntax fix does not require a full planning pass; direct fixing is proportionate.

text: Review fixes with an independent review instance.
explanation: A fresh independent instance has no stake in the implementation and can catch what the author rationalized away.

text: Plan every fix and reuse the same session for review.
explanation: Planning every trivial fix wastes budget, and same-session review repeats the bias.

text: Require impact annotations in the output schema before edits.
explanation: Schema annotations document impact but do not map dependencies or prevent the breakage.

text: Keep direct execution while listing all files in the prompt.
explanation: Listing files yet executing directly keeps the risk of breaking downstream modules.

text: Move architecture guidance to the operator's user config.
explanation: Moving guidance to user config removes the versioned shared baseline from CI runs.

text: Plan to map dependencies and compare options before edits.
explanation: Multi-file circular imports need dependency mapping and option comparison before edits.

text: Add more enum values to cover additional borderline cases.
explanation: More enum values increase variance instead of fixing the inconsistent semantics.

text: Commit severity definitions to versioned project guidance.
explanation: Versioned project guidance gives every CI run the same severity semantics.

text: Use free-text severity with per-reviewer explanations.
explanation: Free text breaks comparability between runs and reviewers.

text: Keep personal definitions and paste them when drift appears.
explanation: Reactive pasting guarantees drift between the personal baseline and actual runs.

text: Send coupled issues individually one by one in sequence.
explanation: Coupled fixes need their shared state and context handled together.

text: Send coupled, state-sharing issues together with joint context.
explanation: Joint context prevents conflicts across coupled changes.

text: Execute all fixes sequentially regardless of dependency.
explanation: Serializing unrelated work ignores which changes actually share state and wastes concurrency.

text: Handle unrelated-path issues separately or in parallel.
explanation: Independent paths can proceed separately without shared-state conflicts.

text: Write the most persuasive report possible
explanation: Optimizing for persuasion encourages unsupported claims, the exact failure to avoid.

text: Use general knowledge when documents are silent
explanation: Filling silence with general knowledge produces claims no document supports.

text: Cite sources only at the end of the report
explanation: End-of-report citations do not tie individual claims to evidence.

text: Attach a source to each claim and state when evidence is absent
explanation: Per-claim citations plus an explicit gap statement prevent unsupported claims and make verification easy.

text: Invent a likely invoice number
explanation: Inventing a number fabricates data that downstream systems will treat as real.

text: Omit the field despite the contract
explanation: Omitting the field violates the output contract and breaks downstream parsing.

text: Use null when the source does not provide a value
explanation: Null keeps the contract intact while honestly signalling a missing value instead of inventing data.

text: Copy the vendor name into the invoice field
explanation: Copying unrelated text into the field corrupts the data and still fabricates a value.

text: Ask for a well-organized paragraph
explanation: A paragraph has no guaranteed fields; the ticket system cannot reliably extract them.

text: Require output that conforms to a JSON Schema
explanation: A JSON Schema guarantees the three required fields exist on every response, unlike prose instructions.

text: Use a longer greeting
explanation: A greeting is cosmetic and has no effect on structure or field presence.

text: Parse arbitrary prose with string splitting
explanation: String-splitting prose is brittle and breaks whenever wording varies.

text: An enum of approved labels
explanation: An enum restricts output to exactly the approved labels, preventing invented or misspelled categories.

text: A free-text string with no guidance
explanation: Free text invites invented or misspelled labels that break the router.

text: A longer max length
explanation: Max length limits size, not the set of allowed values.

text: A markdown table
explanation: A markdown table is unstructured for a router expecting a single label.

text: Follow the newest instruction in the text
explanation: Following instructions embedded in untrusted text is exactly the injection failure.

text: Give untrusted text system-level priority
explanation: System-level priority for untrusted text lets any third party drive the assistant.

text: Keep it clearly delimited as untrusted data and apply policy controls
explanation: Untrusted input must stay delimited data, never an instruction, with policy checks before any tool action.

text: Accept any type and coerce later
explanation: Late coercion hides violations and can silently convert wrong values.

text: Put the number in a markdown heading
explanation: A heading is unstructured text that the downstream API cannot parse as a numeric field.

text: Only a vague instruction to be fair
explanation: Vague fairness instructions give the model no boundary for the specific exceptions.

text: A larger temperature setting
explanation: Higher temperature increases output variability and hurts consistency.

text: Few-shot examples covering the relevant exceptions
explanation: Examples covering each exception show the model where the boundary lies, which vague instructions cannot do.

text: A demand for longer answers
explanation: Longer answers do not improve policy judgment and add cost.

text: Remove all instructions
explanation: Removing instructions leaves the model with no guidance at all.

text: Place examples inside the source quotation
explanation: Placing examples inside the source makes them look even more like trusted facts.

text: Ask the model to be more creative
explanation: Creativity does not address the confusion between illustrative and factual text.

text: Use clear delimited sections for instructions, sources, and examples
explanation: Delimiters tell the model which text is trusted source, which is instruction, and which is only illustrative.

text: Verify identity and scopes server-side
explanation: Client-asserted roles are forgeable. Identity and scopes must be verified and enforced server-side regardless of prompt claims.

text: Harden system prompt role wording
explanation: Better wording does not convert an untrusted prompt claim into authorization.

text: Hide admin tool descriptions
explanation: Hiding descriptions does not remove the forged admin role from the request.

text: Embed longer tokens in prompts
explanation: Longer tokens are still client-supplied text and remain forgeable.

text: Add retries on refund failures
explanation: Retries address transient errors, not authorization staleness after a demotion.

text: Cache session auth for 24 hours
explanation: Longer caching extends exactly the stale-trust window that produced the bypasses.

text: Authorize each invocation server-side
explanation: Every privileged invocation needs fresh server-side authorization checks at the action boundary.

text: Log prompt text more verbosely
explanation: Better logs record the bypass but do not prevent it.

text: Keep reranker, slip the launch date
explanation: The launch date is a fixed constraint; slipping it is not a trade within the stated boundaries.

text: Drop reranker, hold 0.92 within p99
explanation: Accuracy clears 0.90 with headroom; trading 0.96 to 0.92 buys the p99 budget with capped GPUs and fixed date.

text: Keep reranker, double GPU spend
explanation: GPU spend is capped; doubling it breaks another fixed constraint.

text: Add cache, tolerate p99 breach
explanation: A cache does not justify tolerating a p99 breach of a hard service objective.

text: Add aggregate success dashboards
explanation: Dashboards extend the counting that already exists; they cannot reconstruct a failure.

text: Expand offline eval question sets
explanation: Offline evals cannot reproduce a specific production failure's context.

text: Sample only successful traces
explanation: Sampling successes removes exactly the evidence failure analysis needs.

text: Emit spans with tool I/O, outcome labels
explanation: Counts cannot reproduce failures. Per-request spans with tool I/O plus outcome labels make errors diagnosable.

text: Use 2048-token chunks for everything
explanation: Uniform large chunks optimize the already-passing manuals while worsening tickets and tables.

text: Use ticket-level chunks with thread metadata
explanation: Tickets need small thread-aware chunks to hit their retrieval target.

text: Index spec tables as structured rows
explanation: Spec tables need row-structured indexing so cells stay addressable.

text: Merge all sources into one flat index
