explanation: A flat index imposes one shape on three different data structures with different needs.

text: RAG for guides, live API for orders
explanation: Conceptual guides suit semantic RAG; live work-order status needs the system of record, not a snapshot.

text: Fuse BM25 with vectors for identifiers
explanation: Exact WO-XXXXX identifiers need keyword matching fused with vectors to hit the 0.95 target.

text: Snapshot orders nightly into vectors
explanation: Nightly snapshots preserve the 22% staleness causing wrong answers.

text: Use one semantic index for all
explanation: One index cannot serve both static guides and live state with different freshness needs.

text: Add searchable tool discovery on demand
explanation: On-demand discovery removes the 140-schema injection driving the 41k-token prompts.

text: Inject full catalog into bigger window
explanation: A bigger window holds the bloat but keeps paying for it in tokens and latency.

text: Inject task-scoped tool subsets only
explanation: Per-intent scoping fixes misrouting and tokens together by exposing only relevant tools.

text: Retry wrong-tool calls automatically
explanation: Automatic retries repeat the misrouting without addressing the bloated catalog.

text: Recommend the faster option without stating cost
explanation: Recommending a $31k/mo option while hiding its cost denies the CFO the budget information needed to give informed consent to the trade-off.

text: Present both options costed without recommending one
explanation: The CFO explicitly asked for a recommendation today; presenting a neutral comparison stalls the decision and leaves the stakeholder without architectural judgment.

text: Defer the decision until after the launch date
explanation: Deferring past a fixed launch date makes the choice by default under deadline pressure, which is precisely when trade-offs get accepted unexamined.

text: Automatically execute any requested tool call
explanation: Automatic execution of requested calls removes the policy checkpoint that blocks injected actions.

text: Ask for a more confident recommendation
explanation: Confidence phrasing does not separate facts from judgment; it makes blending worse.

text: Use separate fields or stages for facts and recommendation
explanation: Separating extraction from judgment stops opinions from leaking into facts and makes each stage checkable.

text: Remove the contract from context
explanation: Removing the contract removes the facts the assistant needs.

text: Require a longer final answer
explanation: Length does not fix the mixing of quotes and opinions.

text: An array whose items follow an object schema
explanation: An array of objects enforces one consistent shape per issue while allowing any number of issues.

text: One long unstructured string
explanation: An unstructured string cannot guarantee the same fields per issue for the dashboard.

text: A boolean for the whole report
explanation: A boolean carries no issue data at all.

text: A markdown heading per issue
explanation: Headings are display formatting, not a machine-readable per-issue structure.

text: Mix all text into one paragraph
explanation: Mixing everything into one paragraph erases the hierarchy between rules, data, and format.

text: Put the user request before all rules without labels
explanation: Placing the user request first without labels lets user text outrank the policy.

text: Clearly separate instructions, policy context, user data, and output contract
explanation: Labeled sections establish hierarchy: instructions and policy outrank user data, and the output contract is explicit.

text: Put the output schema inside untrusted input
explanation: Embedding the output contract in untrusted input lets user text alter the required format.

text: Always provide a decisive answer
explanation: Demanding a decisive answer pushes the model to conclude without support.

text: Fill gaps with plausible details
explanation: Plausible details are hallucination when no source supports them.

text: State that the evidence is insufficient and request or identify needed information
explanation: Refusing with a gap statement avoids hallucination and tells the user exactly what evidence is missing.

text: Cite any unrelated source
explanation: Citing unrelated sources fakes support and misleads the user.

text: Separate source facts from proposed actions
explanation: Distinct sections let users see what they wrote versus what the model proposes, avoiding confusion.

text: Blend both into one narrative
explanation: Blending makes quoted input indistinguishable from new suggestions.

text: Remove all user notes
explanation: Removing the notes discards the source material users need to review.

text: Label every sentence as certain
explanation: Labeling everything as certain hides the distinction the users need.

text: A single persuasive paragraph
explanation: A paragraph cannot be parsed for the decision or the numeric confidence.

text: Separate structured decision and confidence fields
explanation: Two typed fields keep the decision machine-readable and the confidence separately calibratable.

text: A confidence emoji only
explanation: An emoji is not a calibrated numeric value a router can use.

text: No confidence information
explanation: Omitting confidence removes the signal the router needs for routing decisions.

text: Make every field optional
explanation: Making every field optional defeats the contract; the app crashes when required fields miss.

text: Use prose to describe optionality
explanation: Prose cannot enforce field presence at validation time.

text: Always invent a customer note
explanation: Inventing an optional note fabricates content the user did not write.

text: List required fields explicitly and omit customer_note from required
explanation: Explicit required lists with the optional field excluded enforce presence where needed and freedom where allowed.

text: Run the change against a representative evaluation set
explanation: Five examples prove nothing; a representative set checks for regressions before shipping.

text: Deploy immediately because scores improved
explanation: Deploying on handpicked cases risks regressions everywhere else.

text: Delete the cases that fail
explanation: Deleting failing cases hides the regression instead of fixing it.

text: Increase output length
explanation: Output length is unrelated to the quality question being raised.

text: Only increase the schema complexity
explanation: Schema complexity does not measure whether recommendations are actually useful.

text: Measure recommendation correctness or usefulness against labeled criteria
explanation: Parseability is necessary but not sufficient; task quality must be scored against labeled expectations.

text: Stop validating JSON
explanation: Dropping JSON validation removes the one guarantee that already works.

text: Count characters in the answer
explanation: Character count measures length, not usefulness of the suggestions.

text: Keep it short if possible
explanation: 'If possible' makes the limit optional and unmeasurable.

text: Use a concise tone
explanation: Tone guidance is subjective; reviewers will still disagree on length.

text: Avoid long answers
explanation: 'Long' is undefined, so the instruction cannot be checked.

text: Return no more than 120 words
explanation: An exact numeric bound is directly checkable, while vague style words are not measurable.

text: Send all 40 fields every time
explanation: Sending all fields wastes tokens and dilutes attention with irrelevant data.

text: Send no tool result
explanation: Dropping the result leaves the next step without the data it needs.

text: Send only the 3 needed fields
explanation: Passing only needed fields reduces context and errors. Full raw data wastes tokens.

text: Send a summary without IDs
explanation: A summary without IDs loses the exact references the next step requires.

text: Add more raw files
explanation: More raw files add noise instead of restoring the lost specific evidence.

text: Save verified facts to a scratchpad
explanation: Writing verified facts to a scratchpad grounds the agent in evidence, not vague memory.

text: Rely on model memory
explanation: Model memory is what degraded into typical patterns in the first place.

text: Delete earlier evidence
explanation: Deleting evidence removes the grounding the agent needs.

text: Send failure detail plus partials
explanation: Structured failure plus partials lets the coordinator retry or adjust correctly.

text: Send only 'search unavailable'
explanation: A bare 'unavailable' discards the partial records already retrieved.

text: Send an empty success
explanation: An empty success hides the timeout and misleads the coordinator into trusting the result.

text: Hide the failure
explanation: Hiding failures prevents any correct recovery decision.

text: Make a friendly exception
explanation: Making an exception invents policy that does not exist and creates unaccountable decisions.

text: Escalate the gap to a human
explanation: Silent policies are gaps. Escalation keeps the decision safe and auditable.

text: Infer policy from sentiment
explanation: Sentiment is not policy and guessing a rule fabricates authority.

text: Ignore the request
explanation: Ignoring leaves the user without an answer or a path forward.

text: Hide it in an appendix
explanation: An appendix buries the finding even deeper.

text: Repeat all raw data
explanation: Repeating raw data adds length without improving visibility of the finding.

text: Move it to a labeled early section
explanation: Early, labeled placement fights lost-in-the-middle effects in long contexts.

text: Remove it to shorten context
explanation: Removing a critical risk finding hides it entirely.

text: Compact with no save
explanation: Compacting without saving loses findings that cannot be reconstructed cheaply.

text: Add more logs first
explanation: Adding logs grows the context that is already near its limit.

text: Restart from zero
explanation: Restarting discards completed work and findings.

text: Save findings, then compact
explanation: Persisting findings before compaction keeps work usable after the context reset.

text: A prompt saying "verify first"
explanation: Prompt instructions can be ignored under drift; they provide no hard guarantee.

text: A longer system prompt
explanation: Length does not turn an instruction into an enforcement mechanism.

text: A programmatic precondition blocking the refund tool
explanation: Code-enforced preconditions cannot be ignored by the model, unlike prompt instructions.

text: An arbitrary maximum loop count
explanation: A loop cap limits iterations but does not order verification before refunds.

text: Each subagent independently
explanation: Subagents see only their own scope, so none of them can aggregate the whole task.

text: The end user
explanation: Asking the user to merge raw findings defeats the purpose of orchestration.

text: The coordinator
explanation: The coordinator owns the full task, so it aggregates findings and routes follow-ups.

text: A random subagent picked each time
explanation: A random subagent lacks the full-task context needed for reliable aggregation.

text: End the conversation immediately
explanation: Ending on tool_use abandons the requested action and the user's task.

text: Run the tool and append its result, then continue
explanation: tool_use means the model waits for tool output before continuing the loop.

text: Scan prose for a completion phrase
explanation: Prose scanning is unreliable; stop_reason is the programmatic signal to act on.

text: Discard the request and retry the prompt
explanation: Discarding and retrying loses the requested action and multiplies calls.

text: Assume the subagent inherits all prior messages
explanation: Subagents start with isolated context; inheritance is not automatic.

text: Pass the relevant facts in a structured subagent prompt
explanation: Subagents do not share context automatically, so facts must be passed explicitly.

text: Ask the subagent to guess missing facts
explanation: Guessed facts are fabrications that contaminate the investigation.

text: Remove the facts to shorten the prompt
explanation: Removing the facts leaves the subagent unable to do its scoped job.

text: Check roles via prompt instructions
explanation: Prompt instructions do not enforce authorization at the action boundary; a controlled prompt can grant anything.

text: Authorize each ledger call server-side
explanation: Bypasses need per-invocation server-side authorization on the ledger action.

text: Track aggregate success counters only
explanation: Aggregate counters cannot link a specific ledger write to its approval.

text: Trace tool I/O with outcome labels
explanation: Untraceable writes need request-level I/O spans with outcome labels for audit reconstruction.

text: Single payments consumer uses direct call
explanation: One consumer does not justify an integration layer; the direct call stays.

text: Shared CRM uses one MCP server
explanation: A shared multi-team service gains a single MCP server as its integration boundary.

text: Multi-turn dispute uses one-shot tool
explanation: Multi-turn negotiation needs agent-to-agent dialogue; a one-shot verdict cannot deliberate.

text: Run more automated checks first
explanation: Automated steps delay a request the policy already grants.

text: Escalate to the human path now
explanation: A clear request for a human must be honored directly without extra automated steps.

text: Check sentiment and wait
explanation: Sentiment gating adds friction to an explicit request.

text: Close the case
explanation: Closing abandons a customer with a legitimate pending request.

text: Keep a fixed case-facts block
explanation: A fixed facts block preserves exact amounts and dates across summarization.

text: Summarize more aggressively
explanation: More aggressive summarization loses even more exact values.

text: Tell the model to remember better
explanation: Instructions to remember better do not change what survives summarization.

text: Remove all dates
explanation: Removing dates destroys information the workflow depends on.

text: Check accuracy by type and field
explanation: Segmented analysis reveals failures hidden by a high overall average.

text: Trust the overall average
explanation: A high average can hide a failing segment entirely.

text: Sample only easy documents
explanation: Easy documents bias the sample toward success and hide failures.

text: Stop labeling
explanation: Without labels there is no ground truth to detect the new failure mode.

text: Pick the newest record
explanation: Recency is not identity; the newest record can belong to the other person.

text: Merge both records
explanation: Merging distinct people corrupts both records.

text: Use sentiment to choose
explanation: Sentiment has no relation to which record is the right person.

text: Ask for another identifier
explanation: An extra identifier avoids acting on the wrong person. Guessing or merging is unsafe.

text: Review only low-confidence cases
explanation: High-confidence outputs can be confidently wrong; reviewing only low-confidence misses that.

text: Stop sampling after launch
explanation: Stopping sampling removes the ability to detect hidden error patterns at all.

text: Sample randomly across segments
explanation: Stratified sampling finds hidden errors even when confidence is high.

text: Trust confidence as correct
explanation: Confidence is uncalibrated until validated against labels; high scores can be wrong.

text: Give all raw files to the coordinator
explanation: All raw files in the coordinator bury the high-level decisions under detail.

text: Skip discovery
explanation: Skipping discovery leaves the task uninformed.

text: Make the coordinator memorize logs
explanation: Memorizing logs is not a mechanism and bloats the coordinator context.

text: Delegate detail work, keep a short summary
explanation: A scoped subagent keeps detail local while the coordinator keeps only decisions.

text: A timeout needing retry
explanation: The call succeeded; retrying would duplicate work.

text: An auth failure
explanation: Auth failures prevent execution; this call executed and returned a result.

text: A valid empty result
explanation: Success with zero rows is valid information, not an error or a reason to retry.

text: A reason to invent a match
explanation: Inventing a match fabricates data the database does not contain.

text: Only final conclusions
explanation: Conclusions without sources cannot be verified by the coordinator.

text: Claims mapped to sources
explanation: Claim-to-source mapping lets the coordinator verify each claim.

text: A confidence emoji
explanation: An emoji conveys no verifiable mapping between claims and evidence.

text: All raw docs, no mapping
explanation: Raw documents without mapping shift the verification burden without enabling it.

text: Calibrate on labeled data
explanation: Only labeled validation shows whether 0.98 means correct in practice.

text: Trust any score above 0.9
explanation: An arbitrary threshold substitutes assumption for calibration.

text: Ask for more certainty
explanation: Asking for higher confidence inflates the number without improving accuracy.

text: Remove confidence scores
explanation: Removing scores loses a useful signal once it is calibrated; the fix is validation, not deletion.

text: Treat it as empty result
explanation: An empty result means valid no-match; an auth error is a different failure class needing different handling.

text: Record it as access failure
explanation: Auth failures need access fixes, not retries or empty-result logic.

text: Retry forever silently
explanation: Retrying an auth failure never succeeds and hides the real problem.

text: Claim no records exist
explanation: Claiming no records exist conflates an access failure with a valid empty result.

text: Retry once, then report
explanation: One bounded retry handles transient faults without hiding the outcome.

text: Invent missing docs
explanation: Inventing documents fabricates evidence.

text: Abort the whole workflow
explanation: Aborting everything for a brief transient fault is disproportionate.

text: Hide the timeout
explanation: Hiding the timeout prevents correct recovery decisions upstream.

text: Present all claims as certain
explanation: Presenting partial evidence as certain invites overconfident decisions.

text: Discard all partials
explanation: Discarding partials throws away usable evidence.

text: Mark what is solid vs incomplete
explanation: Explicit uncertainty marking prevents overconfident decisions from partials.

text: Hide the source list
explanation: Hiding sources removes the ability to weigh evidence quality.

text: Pick the larger value
explanation: Picking by size ignores that the figures cover different dates and may both be true.

text: Average both values
explanation: Averaging figures from different periods fabricates a number that matches neither.

text: Discard both sources
explanation: Discarding both sources loses true information.

text: Report both with dates
explanation: Different dates can both be true. Reporting both with sources preserves truth.

text: Low-confidence cases first
explanation: Limited review time should target the riskiest, most uncertain cases first.

text: Only high-confidence cases
explanation: High-confidence cases are least likely to need correction; reviewing them wastes scarce time.

text: Random safe cases
explanation: Random safe cases spend review capacity where it adds least value.

text: Review nothing
explanation: No review at all leaves uncertain decisions unchecked.

text: See all subagent activity in one place
explanation: A coordinator centralizes observability and error handling without auto-sharing context.

text: Handle subagent errors in one place
explanation: A coordinator centralizes observability and error handling without auto-sharing context.

text: Remove the need for task definitions
explanation: Every subagent still needs an explicit task definition regardless of coordination.

text: Share all context automatically
explanation: Routing through a coordinator does not create automatic context sharing between subagents.

text: Applying the same three checks to every invoice
explanation: A fixed sequence of known checks is exactly what a prompt chain handles well.

text: Investigating an unknown incident where findings guide next steps
explanation: Open-ended investigations need dynamic decomposition because next steps depend on findings.

text: Formatting a known report template
explanation: Template formatting is a deterministic task that does not need dynamic planning.

text: Running a single validation rule
explanation: A single rule is a fixed step, not an open-ended decomposition problem.

text: In a PostToolUse hook
explanation: A PostToolUse hook normalizes tool output programmatically before the model sees it.

text: Only in the final user message
explanation: Waiting until the final message leaves the model consuming inconsistent data throughout.

text: By asking the user to translate formats
explanation: Shifting normalization to users is fragile and unacceptable operationally.

text: By ignoring timestamps
explanation: Ignoring timestamps discards information the support workflow needs.

text: After exactly three iterations
explanation: An arbitrary iteration cap cuts off needed work or permits wasted calls; it is not a completion signal.

text: When stop_reason indicates end_turn
explanation: end_turn signals the model finished and needs no more tool calls.

text: When any tool is available
explanation: Tool availability says nothing about whether the task is complete.

text: When assistant text contains "done"
explanation: Parsing prose for a completion phrase is spoofable and unreliable compared to stop_reason.

text: Inject all 140 schemas every turn
explanation: Injecting the full catalog every turn is monolithic context, not progressive discovery.

text: Bulk export uses direct CLI script
explanation: Bulk exports do not need a chat interface; a direct CLI script is the right tool.

text: Live stock uses nightly vector snapshot
explanation: Live stock changes during a conversation; a nightly snapshot cannot be authoritative.

text: Exact IDs use hybrid keyword plus vector
explanation: Exact identifiers need keyword matching fused with semantic retrieval.

text: Trust identity asserted in prompt text
explanation: Prompt-asserted identity is user-controlled and forgeable; verification belongs server-side.

text: Authorize each privileged call server-side
explanation: Privileged actions need fresh per-invocation server-side authorization.

text: Trace tool I/O with outcome labels
explanation: Incident diagnosis needs request-level traces with tool I/O and outcomes.

text: Searchable catalog loading schemas on demand
explanation: Loading schemas on demand per intent is progressive discovery.

text: Full 140 schemas injected every turn
explanation: Full injection every turn is the definition of monolithic context.

text: Task-scoped subset injected per intent
explanation: Scoping the tool subset to the current intent is progressive discovery.

text: All docs and secrets in system prompt
explanation: Stuffing everything including secrets into the system prompt is monolithic and insecure.

text: Commit the quarter-end date before clarifying
explanation: Committing a date while the success criterion is still an undefined adjective guarantees a launch judged by taste rather than testable conditions.

text: Design around the assumed friction meaning
explanation: Designing against a guessed definition of friction bakes unvalidated assumptions into the architecture, and any mismatch surfaces only after build effort is spent.

text: Probe failure cases before committing dates
explanation: Vague adjectives must become testable failure conditions before any date is committed. Committing, designing, or selecting vendors first acts one gate too early.

text: Select vendors before clarifying friction terms
explanation: Choosing a vendor before the requirement is testable lets tooling drive the definition, so the selection may satisfy criteria the sponsor never actually meant.

text: Confirm residency constraint before routing design
explanation: A constraint mentioned in passing must be confirmed before routing or storage decisions. Designing past it or adding monitoring without confirming scope leaves the violation intact.

text: Keep US routing and note assumption later
explanation: Shipping a known potential residency violation while deferring confirmation leaves the legal exposure live in production, where it is far costlier to unwind.

text: Convert null to false in a post-use hook after return.
explanation: Converting null to false asserts a confirmed out-of-stock state that was never verified, which is precisely what triggers the backorders. The access failure remains masked, just with a different misleading value.

text: Ask the model to self-check refunds
explanation: A model self-check is probabilistic and unauditable, so it cannot provably enforce a hard $50 cap on a side-effecting money-moving action.

text: Log refunds for monthly sampling review
explanation: Monthly sampling reviews refunds only after the money has already moved, so it detects violations too late to prevent them and provides no deterministic pre-execution control.

text: Enforce refund policy in tool authorization
explanation: Tool calls need deterministic policy enforcement on amount, recipient, and approval state. A model self-check is bypassable and unauditable.

text: Add few-shot examples of fair refunds
explanation: Few-shot examples shape model behavior only statistically; they cannot guarantee the $50 cap or the approval requirement on every single refund call.

text: Raise retry limits so real transient failures get more time.
explanation: Raising limits gives the mislabeled validation errors even more room to multiply across orchestration levels, increasing call volume without any progress. The root cause — a non-retryable error classified as retryable — is untouched.

text: Fingerprint errors and stop identical retries on unchanged input.
explanation: Mislabeled validation errors retry identically at every layer. Fingerprinting input+error and refusing identical retries breaks the multiplicative cascade.

text: Trust errorCategory and ignore the isRetryable field.
explanation: In this scenario the category itself is wrong (validation labeled transient), so trusting one field over the other does not fix the misclassification. Identical retries at every level would continue.

text: Retry only at the coordinator, never inside subagents.
explanation: Restricting retries to one level reduces but does not eliminate the loop: the coordinator will still retry the same mislabeled validation error indefinitely on unchanged input. The classification error itself remains.

text: Block payments and queue for review
explanation: For irreversible payments, a safety dependency outage must fail closed: block or queue for review. Fail-open trades safety for latency.

text: Skip the check and post payments
explanation: Skipping the check is failing open: irreversible payments would proceed unscreened during the outage, which is the unsafe failure direction at this risk level.

text: Retry once then post payments anyway
explanation: Posting after a single retry still fails open — if the policy service is genuinely down, irreversible payments execute without the required screening.

text: Warn the user but post payments
explanation: A warning does not change the outcome: irreversible payments still execute unscreened, so this is fail open with extra disclosure rather than a safe failure direction.

text: Follow the article as updated policy
explanation: Retrieved content is untrusted data, not a policy source; following the embedded directive lets an injected instruction hijack the agent and disclose SSNs in violation of privacy policy.

text: Defer to the article author for consent
explanation: The article author has no authority to grant consent or set policy; authorization comes from the user and the system's governance, not from whoever wrote a retrieved document.

text: Include SSNs with a warning to user
explanation: Appending a warning does not neutralize the harm — the SSNs are still disclosed in the answer, which violates privacy policy regardless of the caveat.

text: Ignore the embedded instruction as data
explanation: Retrieved content is data, never a principal. The agent must ignore the embedded instruction and complete the user's task under developer and system policy.

text: Keep broad access for helpfulness
explanation: Broad CRM write plus email-send is exactly the excessive agency that caused the incident; helpfulness does not justify leaving an ungated exfiltration path open.

text: Scope to read-only plus gated writes
explanation: Broad write plus send gives excessive agency. Default to read-only discovery with narrowly scoped writes gated by approval and audit.

text: Add a prompt to be more careful
explanation: A caution prompt is probabilistic and bypassable; it does not remove the agent's technical ability to write to the CRM or email customers, so the exfiltration path remains open.

text: Hide tool errors from the agent
explanation: Hiding errors does not narrow the agent's permissions; it only removes diagnostic signal while leaving the excessive write and send capabilities fully intact.

text: Compare both options against agreed priorities
explanation: Contested calls are defended by comparing both options against agreed priorities and recording decision, rationale, and revisit triggers. Private lock-in or one-sided deep-dives do not.

text: Deep-dive only chosen design internals today
explanation: Presenting only the favored design's internals excludes the board's preferred option from any fair comparison and reads as advocacy rather than defense.

text: Record decision, rationale, and revisit triggers
explanation: Contested calls are defended by comparing both options against agreed priorities and recording decision, rationale, and revisit triggers. Private lock-in or one-sided deep-dives do not.

text: Brief one executive privately to lock support
explanation: Private lobbying bypasses the board's collective review and makes the decision look pre-arranged, undermining its legitimacy if it is later challenged.

text: Keep all tools and require some tool call on every turn.
explanation: Requiring a call every turn does not shrink the overlapping toolset, so the model still picks poorly among too many similar tools — and now it must also fabricate unnecessary calls on turns where none is needed.

text: Add a classifier tool while keeping all tools on one agent.
explanation: Adding a classifier grows the already-overloaded toolset and merely relocates the routing problem to another selection the model must make. The overlapping tools on one agent remain untouched.

text: A multi-agent orchestrator for both, sharing the clause context
explanation: over-orchestration — coordination overhead across subagents buys breadth, not reliability, for a legally fixed filing sequence.

text: Reconcile conflicts via risk-tolerance agreement
explanation: Sound discovery writes assumptions down, converts vague terms into failure conditions, and reconciles conflicts explicitly. Designing past hints or locking dates first are gate violations.

text: Commit to demo accuracy minus a small margin
explanation: An arbitrary margin off a curated demo is still a blind commitment; production traffic is unrepresentative of the ten demo cases, so the true production figure is unknown.

text: Confirm commitment now and evaluate after rollout
explanation: Committing before measuring production performance converts the launch into an experiment the sponsor never agreed to, with the discovery of failures arriving after commitments are locked.

text: Baseline a sample before committing to targets
explanation: A curated demo proves capability, not production performance. Baseline a representative sample before committing; margin-off-demo or post-rollout evaluation commits blind.

text: Refuse every accuracy target as totally impossible
explanation: Refusing all targets overcorrects; accuracy targets are legitimate once grounded in a representative baseline rather than a curated demo.

text: Delete first, then sample for quality
explanation: Post-hoc sampling reviews deletions that have already happened; with legal retention requirements at stake, the wrong sample leaves protected accounts unrecoverable.

text: Add a prompt to delete more carefully
explanation: A prompt instruction is probabilistic and cannot guarantee that legally retained accounts are excluded from a 40,000-account irreversible deletion.

text: Require approval of scope before execution
explanation: Irreversible bulk deletion needs a gate before execution with scope preview and approval. Post-hoc sampling cannot restore deleted accounts.

text: Speed deletion to cut compute cost
explanation: Execution speed is irrelevant to the control failure; faster deletion only accelerates an unreviewed, irreversible action that legal has flagged.

text: Keep the shared tool and omit only obviously irrelevant URLs.
explanation: Manual filtering of only 'obviously' irrelevant URLs is unreliable and still hands each role a general-purpose loader, so cross-role retrieval of invoice or ticket URLs can continue whenever a URL looks plausibly relevant.

text: Move all URL access up to the coordinator agent.
explanation: Centralizing URL access at the coordinator does not give either subagent a role-scoped tool, and the coordinator now fetches content for both domains without a specialization boundary. The mixed-retrieval problem is relocated, not resolved.

text: Rename the shared tool identically in both subagents.
explanation: Renaming changes nothing about the tool's behavior or scope: both roles still share one general URL loader and both still receive invoice and ticket URLs, so cross-role retrieval continues exactly as before.

text: Give each role its loader and pass only role-relevant URLs.
explanation: A shared general loader plus unfiltered URLs guarantees cross-role retrieval. Role-specific loaders with only role-relevant URLs enforce specialization at the data plane.

text: Add more reviewers to same queue
explanation: Adding reviewers to an unchanged queue reproduces consent fatigue at higher headcount; the volume and interface still push toward 3-second rubber-stamping.

text: Prompt reviewers to pay attention
explanation: Exhortation does not change the incentives or the interface that produce 99% approvals in 3 seconds; fatigue is structural, not an attention-willingness problem.

text: Hide model reasoning from reviewers
explanation: Hiding the model's reasoning removes context reviewers need for genuine deliberation and does nothing to fix the queue design causing rubber-stamping.

text: Track latency and audit, redesign gate
explanation: Near-100% approval in seconds signals rubber-stamping. Detect via latency, approval-rate variance, and spot audits, then redesign the gate to force deliberation.

text: Commit server definitions to shared project configuration.
explanation: Server definitions belong in shared project config, secrets belong in environment variables, and an available community ticket server should be reused instead of duplicated.

text: Inject tokens via environment variables, never hardcoded secrets.
explanation: Server definitions belong in shared project config, secrets belong in environment variables, and an available community ticket server should be reused instead of duplicated.

text: Adopt the available community ticket server over a duplicate.
explanation: Server definitions belong in shared project config, secrets belong in environment variables, and an available community ticket server should be reused instead of duplicated.

text: Keep user scope and distribute tokens through team chat.
explanation: User scope keeps team integrations invisible to other collaborators, and sharing tokens through team chat exposes the secret in plaintext history with no revocation path. Both practices contradict shared-config and environment-variable injection.

text: Expose the schema catalog as a first-class MCP resource.
explanation: Repeated describe calls signal undiscoverable schema. Exposing the catalog resource plus enriching tools with columns, relations, and examples lets the model plan without exploration calls.

text: Enrich table tools with columns, relations, and examples.
explanation: Repeated describe calls signal undiscoverable schema. Exposing the catalog resource plus enriching tools with columns, relations, and examples lets the model plan without exploration calls.

text: Merge all tables into one unrestricted query-any-table tool.
explanation: Merging tables into one unrestricted tool removes the per-table descriptions that carry applicability information, making selection guidance worse. It also invites unscoped queries rather than reducing exploration.

text: Require some table tool immediately via forced tool choice.
explanation: Forcing a table tool guarantees a call but not a correct one: with minimally described tools the model still lacks the schema knowledge to pick and query well, so exploratory describe calls continue.

text: Namespace tool names; connect each role subagent to one server.
explanation: Colliding names plus a large flat toolset breaks selection. Namespacing removes collision and one-server-per-subagent shrinks each selection space.

text: Emit per-worker coverage events linked to that trace ID.
explanation: A shared trace ID plus linked per-worker coverage events makes the missing finding attributable.

text: Merge all domains into one broad handle_request tool.
explanation: A single broad tool sacrifices the distinct capabilities each domain tool provided and reintroduces the same ambiguity inside one interface. Capability is reduced, not preserved, and selection guidance does not improve.

text: Route to role-specific subagents with small relevant toolsets.
explanation: One agent with a large overlapping toolset cannot select reliably. Role-specific subagents with small relevant toolsets preserve capability while shrinking each selection space.

text: Reconcile target state before reporting
explanation: Self-reported success is unreliable. Reconcile deterministic side effects - record counts, hashes, target-state reads - before reporting completion.

text: Trust the success summary when confident
explanation: A success summary is the model's claim about its own work, which is exactly what failed here; without independent verification, silent skips go undetected again.

text: Ask the model to double-check itself
explanation: Self-review by the same model that produced the errors cannot be trusted as evidence — it already misreported completion once, and a generator checking its own work is not independent verification.

text: Retry silently until no error appears
explanation: Silent retries hide failures rather than surface them; a retry loop can succeed without errors while still skipping records, reproducing the same silent failure.

text: Remove ordering and let the model choose each next step.
explanation: Removing ordering abandons the workflow guarantee that underwriting runs only after a successful credit check, which is exactly the dependency the scenario violates. It trades a sequencing bug for arbitrary, unguaranteed step order.

text: Keep forcing and add a warning to underwriting's description.
explanation: A description warning is advisory: forced selection will still execute underwriting after the credit failure, so the misleading missing-input error and the misattributed failure point persist unchanged.

text: Gate underwriting on credit success; propagate consent errors directly.
explanation: Forced sequencing without gating executes underwriting on missing consent, producing a misleading second error. Gating plus direct consent-error propagation preserves order and attribution.

text: Map the later missing-input error back to consent after execution.
explanation: Post-hoc remapping is a heuristic patch over a symptom: the underwriting call still runs on missing prerequisites and can fail for other reasons, making the reverse mapping unreliable. Attribution should come from gating, not guessing after the fact.

text: Force search during exploration and lint on every later turn.
explanation: Forcing tool calls on turns is a blunt workaround that doesn't fix the misleading 'analyzes code' description, and it over-constrains turns where neither pattern applies. The selection boundary is still undefined.

text: Remove custom file tools and rely only on lint output.
explanation: Relying only on lint output eliminates the search and read capability the exploration needs, so context bloat is replaced by an inability to investigate. Capability is destroyed rather than correctly routed.

text: Drop linting and invoke an equivalent command through Bash.
explanation: Dropping the lint tool loses its description-based selection guidance entirely, and routing the same linting through Bash reintroduces the same context-heavy outputs without fixing why exploration misuse happened.

text: Scope lint to verification-only; direct exploration to search/read.
explanation: A verification tool described as general analysis gets misused for exploration. Scoping lint to verification-only and routing exploration to search/read keeps capability while cutting context bloat.

text: Send full charts since channel is encrypted
explanation: Encryption secures the transport but does not satisfy HIPAA's minimum necessary standard; shipping full charts exceeds what the medication-summary purpose requires.

text: Extract only needed fields before the call
explanation: HIPAA minimum necessary requires limiting PHI to what the purpose needs, before the call. TLS plus BAA alone does not satisfy it.

text: Rely on BAA plus TLS cover as sufficient
explanation: A BAA and TLS protect the channel and business relationship but place no limit on the volume of PHI disclosed; minimization still requires sending only the needed fields.

text: Add a prompt telling model to ignore extras
explanation: A prompt instruction is not an administrative or technical safeguard under HIPAA, and the excess PHI has already left the clinic's control once it enters the context window.

text: Set bounded retention with scheduled deletion
explanation: Storage limitation requires bounded retention with scheduled deletion for support chats. Consent and encryption do not substitute for a retention schedule.

text: Keep chats indefinitely for future evals
explanation: Indefinite retention is the direct opposite of storage limitation, which GDPR applies regardless of the downstream purpose claimed for the data.

text: Rely on consent plus encryption alone
explanation: Consent and encryption address lawful basis and transport security but impose no time bound on retention, so the storage limitation principle remains unmet.

text: Anonymize only after a breach occurs
explanation: Waiting for a breach leaves personal data retained indefinitely in the meantime; storage limitation demands proactive, scheduled deletion or anonymization.

text: Weekly quality report with no tied action
explanation: A report nobody is obligated to act on is monitoring only; no agreed response changes the system when the signal fires.

text: Breach pages the owner who runs the runbook
explanation: A closed loop pairs an agreed signal with an agreed response that changes the system. Reports and ad-hoc dashboards without tied action are monitoring only.

text: Analyst dashboard explored ad hoc each month
explanation: Ad-hoc dashboard exploration depends on someone choosing to look, with no agreed trigger or response, so degradation can persist unaddressed.

text: Override alert triggers agreed prompt rollback
explanation: A closed loop pairs an agreed signal with an agreed response that changes the system. Reports and ad-hoc dashboards without tied action are monitoring only.

text: A translation table of the statements into constraints
explanation: valid-but-early — the table is where discoveries land, but it records whatever the questions surfaced rather than driving them.

text: Enable citations on the document blocks passed with each question
explanation: Citations enabled on the source documents make the model return the exact quoted text supporting each statement, so adjusters can verify every coverage answer against the precise policy passage without a manual keyword hunt.

text: Nightly eval digest emailed without owner
explanation: An emailed digest with no assigned owner has no agreed responder, so even a visible regression waits for someone to volunteer.

text: Spike auto-freezes rollout per the playbook
explanation: Auto-freeze per playbook and cap via runbook pair signal with agreed response. Digests without owners and charts reviewed on memory are monitoring only.

text: Latency chart reviewed when someone remembers
explanation: A review that happens only when someone remembers has no reliable trigger, so the signal frequently fires without any response at all.

text: Cost overrun alert triggers cap via runbook
explanation: Auto-freeze per playbook and cap via runbook pair signal with agreed response. Digests without owners and charts reviewed on memory are monitoring only.

text: Ask the model to quote its sources politely in output
explanation: prompt-as-guarantee — a courteous instruction yields references that may be invented, not the verified quoted span, and nothing ties the citation to the source document.

text: Raise the maximum output tokens so answers grow longer
explanation: scale-not-strategy — longer answers still arrive unattributed, so the manual clause hunt that motivated the change continues, just with more text to scan.

text: Policy engine decides eligibility from the maintained table.
explanation: Eligibility belongs to the maintained policy table (source of truth); high-value irreversible refunds need a pre-submission human gate. Claude drafts.

text: Human gates high-value refunds before submission.
explanation: Eligibility belongs to the maintained policy table (source of truth); high-value irreversible refunds need a pre-submission human gate. Claude drafts.

text: Claude decides eligibility alone, losing source-of-truth control.
explanation: Eligibility is a policy decision owned by the maintained table as source of truth, so leaving it to model inference bypasses that control and produces unaccountable decisions.

text: Claude issues all refunds alone with sampling, risking irreversible loss.
explanation: High-value refunds are irreversible once submitted, so post-hoc sampling cannot contain the loss; these actions require a human gate before submission.

text: Coded workflow with explicit stages, guards, and logged handoffs.
explanation: Known stages with reconstructability requirement call for an explicit coded workflow with guards and logged handoffs, not autonomy.

text: Autonomous agent with broad tools, at cost of non-reproducible paths.
explanation: Auditors require each stage to be reconstructable, and model-chosen paths are non-reproducible, so autonomy fails the audit requirement regardless of tool breadth.

text: Single call with all context, at cost of lost stage reconstruction.
explanation: Collapsing extract, coverage check, threshold rule, and adjuster note into one call eliminates the per-stage logs and guards auditors need to reconstruct each decision.

text: Peer agent team negotiating results, at cost of needless coordination.
explanation: The stages are fixed and known, so peer negotiation adds coordination cost and nondeterminism while offering no benefit over explicit workflow stages.

text: Review contracts in parallel with validation.
explanation: Independent reviews parallelize; a single aggregation pass preserves portfolio-level synthesis without serial delay.

text: Run one portfolio aggregation pass over validated results.
explanation: Independent reviews parallelize; a single aggregation pass preserves portfolio-level synthesis without serial delay.

text: Chain all reviews sequentially, paying full serial delay.
explanation: The contracts are independent, so sequential chaining pays the full serial delay without any improvement in review quality or portfolio synthesis.

text: Let one agent pick order under budget, losing parallelism and reproducibility.
explanation: Model-chosen ordering forfeits the parallelism the independent reviews allow and makes execution non-reproducible, all without improving the rubric-driven analysis.

text: Stay commercial since data is encrypted
explanation: AES-256 and SOC 2 do not substitute for FedRAMP authorization at the required impact level; the agency's obligation is to operate through an authorized environment, regardless of encryption.

text: Add a prompt ban on sensitive topics
explanation: A prompt restriction is not a compliance control and does not change the authorization status of the underlying endpoint hosting federal data.

text: Move to a FedRAMP-authorized offering
explanation: FedRAMP requires operating in an authorized environment with inherited controls and continuous monitoring. Encryption on a commercial endpoint is insufficient.

text: Self-attest controls without assessment
explanation: Self-attestation provides no independent assessment evidence; FedRAMP requires formal authorization through the prescribed assessment and monitoring process.

text: Ship since the gender field was removed
explanation: Removing the gender field does not make the model fair — zip, first name, and college remain as plausible proxies, so blindness is assumed rather than demonstrated.

text: Trust overall accuracy as fairness proof
explanation: Aggregate 91% accuracy can mask materially worse routing for a subgroup; fairness requires disaggregated measurement, not a single overall number.

text: Add a prompt instructing fair decisions
explanation: A fairness instruction is probabilistic and unauditable; it neither measures the subgroup disparity the pilot hinted at nor tests the proxy features still in use.

text: Measure gaps and test proxy features
explanation: Removing the protected field while keeping zip, name, and college preserves proxies. Fairness requires disaggregated measurement and proxy testing, not blind removal.

text: Deterministic input screening for injection
explanation: Layered safety pairs deterministic input screening with output screening or tool authorization. A prompt reminder or single filter alone is bypassable.

text: Disable one server and rebuild its functions with shell commands.
explanation: Rebuilding server functions as shell commands recreates the same overlapping capability in a less structured form, and it forfeits the server's own tool descriptions and error handling. Collisions simply reappear as overlapping shell tools.

text: Force the colliding tool and rely on server ordering for choice.
explanation: Forcing a specific colliding tool hard-codes one choice regardless of task, and server ordering is an incidental detail the model cannot meaningfully reason about. Neither addresses the name collisions or the oversized toolset.

text: Keep all tools and explain duplicate names in the prompt.
explanation: Prompt prose cannot disambiguate tool invocations, and keeping all servers connected preserves the large flat toolset that degrades selection. The structural causes remain in place.

text: Move the server to shared project configuration for CI.
explanation: User scope plus hardcoded expiring token plus silent 401-as-null produces defective summaries in CI. Project config, environment token, and retryable 401 errors fix scope, secret, and observability.

text: Inject the token from the environment instead of hardcoding.
explanation: User scope plus hardcoded expiring token plus silent 401-as-null produces defective summaries in CI. Project config, environment token, and retryable 401 errors fix scope, secret, and observability.

text: Surface 401 as a structured retryable error, never silent null.
explanation: User scope plus hardcoded expiring token plus silent 401-as-null produces defective summaries in CI. Project config, environment token, and retryable 401 errors fix scope, secret, and observability.

text: Keep user scope and retry whenever a summary field is null.
explanation: Retrying on null summary fields treats an authentication failure as a data problem: the 401 will recur on every call while the scope and hardcoded-token defects persist. Null-triggered retries mask the root cause instead of surfacing it.

text: Use retrieval for stable documentation questions.
explanation: Stable docs suit RAG; live order/account state needs APIs; state changes and human requests need guarded actions and handoff, not one index.

text: Use live APIs for order and account state.
explanation: Stable docs suit RAG; live order/account state needs APIs; state changes and human requests need guarded actions and handoff, not one index.

text: Use guarded actions plus immediate human handoff path.
explanation: Stable docs suit RAG; live order/account state needs APIs; state changes and human requests need guarded actions and handoff, not one index.

text: Put live state in one RAG index, paying stale and unsafe answers.
explanation: Order and account state change minute to minute, so an indexed snapshot serves stale answers, and a retrieval index cannot perform or authorize state-changing actions safely.

text: Use one agent for all intents, losing determinism and auditability.
explanation: Each intent has a well-known handling pattern, so a single free agent adds nondeterminism and loses the auditability that explicit routing per intent preserves.

text: Chain with validated handoffs plus evaluator before release.
explanation: Sequential structured dependency fits a chain with validated handoffs and a pre-release evaluator.

text: Parallel stages with confidence vote, breaking sequential dependency.
explanation: Each stage consumes the prior stage's structured output, so the stages cannot run in parallel; a confidence vote cannot manufacture the dependency the redline flow requires.

text: Route whole contract to one stage by category, skipping required steps.
explanation: Every contract must pass through extraction, classification, and drafting, so routing by category skips mandatory steps and produces redlines without the required analysis trail.

text: Open-ended agent discovering stages per contract, paying irreproducibility.
explanation: The stages are already known and fixed, so agent-discovered paths add irreproducibility without covering any dependency the explicit chain does not already handle.

text: Allow agentic exploration of the unfamiliar repository.
explanation: Unfamiliar repos justify agentic exploration, but edits/tests/publishing stay deterministic with approval before the PR.

text: Enforce deterministic edit-test-review with approval before publishing.
explanation: Unfamiliar repos justify agentic exploration, but edits/tests/publishing stay deterministic with approval before the PR.

text: Run one autonomous loop including approval inference, risking unapproved publishes.
explanation: Approval is a phase gate that must come from a human, not be inferred by the model; folding it into an autonomous loop risks publishing patches nobody approved.

text: Publish majority-voted patches from file agents, losing coherence and review.
explanation: Voting among per-file agents does not substitute for human review, and independently produced patches lack the cross-file coherence a single patch series requires before publishing.

text: Prompt the model to try its best anyway
explanation: Best-effort prompting does not restore knowledge the model lacks; it reliably produces confident answers from a stale cutoff, which is the exact failure occurring here.

text: Ground answers in dated retrieved sources
explanation: Stale-model silence needs freshness grounding and version-aware abstention. Telling the model to try harder does not fix a stale cutoff.

text: Hide the model version from the UI view
explanation: Hiding the version obscures the staleness risk from users without changing the model's outdated knowledge, and it removes transparency rather than adding a safeguard.

text: Abstain when data exceeds knowledge cutoff
explanation: Stale-model silence needs freshness grounding and version-aware abstention. Telling the model to try harder does not fix a stale cutoff.

text: Redact to needed fields before the call
explanation: Minimization is enforced on the data path: extract only needed fields and scope retrieval to the purpose. Broad stuffing plus indefinite logs violates it.

text: Scope retrieval to the stated purpose
explanation: Minimization is enforced on the data path: extract only needed fields and scope retrieval to the purpose. Broad stuffing plus indefinite logs violates it.

text: Stuff full records for better context
explanation: Stuffing full case files maximizes data exposure rather than minimizing it, and it directly conflicts with GDPR's minimum-necessary requirement regardless of any quality benefit.

text: Prompt reminder to behave safely instead
explanation: A prompt reminder is probabilistic and bypassable, especially by injected content in uploads, so it cannot serve as one of the deterministic layers the design needs.

text: Deterministic output screening of responses
explanation: Layered safety pairs deterministic input screening with output screening or tool authorization. A prompt reminder or single filter alone is bypassable.

text: Single keyword blocklist as only control
explanation: A single keyword blocklist is trivially evaded and covers only one narrow pattern; it cannot deterministically screen uploads on the input path and responses on the output path.

text: Evaluate accuracy disaggregated by group
explanation: Fairness needs disaggregated metrics plus reconstructable decision logs for proxy audits. Aggregate accuracy and log deletion hide disparity.

text: Report only aggregate accuracy overall
explanation: Reporting only the 90% aggregate hides exactly the subgroup failure the complaint alleges; fairness validation requires metrics broken out by group.

text: Delete decision logs to protect privacy
explanation: Deleting logs makes decisions unreconstructable, so neither the proxy-bias allegation nor the model versions involved can ever be audited — privacy and accountability must be balanced, not resolved by destruction.

text: Keep versioned logs enabling proxy audits
explanation: Fairness needs disaggregated metrics plus reconstructable decision logs for proxy audits. Aggregate accuracy and log deletion hide disparity.

text: Sample 1% uniformly across all case types
explanation: Uniform 1% sampling is the existing failure: it under-samples high-value and uncertain cases exactly where errors concentrate, regardless of volume spikes.

text: Stratify sampling by risk and uncertainty
explanation: Risk-based oversight stratifies by impact and uncertainty and surges on drift signals. Uniform thin sampling plus complaint-only review misses concentrated risk.

text: Surge review on drift and override signals
explanation: Risk-based oversight stratifies by impact and uncertainty and surges on drift signals. Uniform thin sampling plus complaint-only review misses concentrated risk.

text: Review only user-complained cases instead
explanation: Complaint-driven review catches only the errors users notice, missing the silent high-value and uncertainty-driven errors that sampling exists to surface.

text: Enforce tool limits in code, not prompts
explanation: Deterministic enforcement, fail-closed for irreversible actions, and pre-call redaction are true. Prompt-only tool control and post-display redaction are false placements.

text: Control tool use with prompts alone
explanation: Prompt-only control is probabilistic and bypassable by injected content, so it cannot be a trustworthy placement for side-effecting tool authorization.

text: Fail closed on safety-check outage
explanation: Deterministic enforcement, fail-closed for irreversible actions, and pre-call redaction are true. Prompt-only tool control and post-display redaction are false placements.

text: Redact PII only after model display
explanation: Post-display redaction is a false placement: by then the PII has already entered the model context, the logs, and potentially the rendered output, so the exposure has already happened.

text: Redact PII before the model call
explanation: Deterministic enforcement, fail-closed for irreversible actions, and pre-call redaction are true. Prompt-only tool control and post-display redaction are false placements.

text: Trust agent success summaries without checks
explanation: Success summaries are self-reported claims, not verification; trusting them without reconciliation is the pattern behind silent skipped work and false completion reports.

text: Treat retrieved content as untrusted data
explanation: Retrieval is data, excessive scope needs least privilege, and EU-US transfers need a valid mechanism. Blind trust in self-reports and indefinite retention are failures.

text: Default agents to least-privilege scope
explanation: Retrieval is data, excessive scope needs least privilege, and EU-US transfers need a valid mechanism. Blind trust in self-reports and indefinite retention are failures.

text: Retain EU chats indefinitely for evals
explanation: Indefinite retention of EU chats violates GDPR storage limitation, which requires bounded retention periods regardless of the eval purpose.

text: Ground EU-US transfers in a valid mechanism
explanation: Retrieval is data, excessive scope needs least privilege, and EU-US transfers need a valid mechanism. Blind trust in self-reports and indefinite retention are failures.

text: Injection via docs: treat output as data
explanation: Injection is contained by treating outputs as data with input screening; excessive agency by least privilege plus tool gates. Prompt-only fixes and fail-open postings mismatch the risks.

text: Excessive agency: add a caution prompt
explanation: A caution prompt is not an agency control — it leaves the agent's broad write and send capabilities technically intact, so the risk it is paired against remains unmitigated.

text: Filter outage: fail open to protect latency
explanation: Failing open during a filter outage lets unscreened content through, which is the wrong failure direction wherever screening protects users from real harm.

text: Excessive agency: least privilege plus gates
explanation: Injection is contained by treating outputs as data with input screening; excessive agency by least privilege plus tool gates. Prompt-only fixes and fail-open postings mismatch the risks.

text: Plan handoff before evals and trade-offs settle
explanation: Handoff planning before evals and trade-offs are settled transfers a design whose behavior and accepted sacrifices are not yet established, inverting the lifecycle gate.

text: Require eval suite plus agreed trade-offs pre-handoff
explanation: Evals plus agreed trade-offs gate handoff planning, and iteration returns to design with updated evals. Handoff-first or discovery-placed load testing inverts the sequence.

text: Place load testing inside early discovery work
explanation: Load testing needs a built system with representative traffic; placing it in early discovery tests a design that does not yet exist.

text: Constrain tools and actions to investigation scope.
explanation: Unplannable sequences justify agents only with constrained tools, budgets, stopping criteria, and checkpointed state.

text: Retain full prompts indefinitely by default
explanation: Indefinite retention of full prompts preserves all the excessive personal data minimization was meant to remove, violating both minimization and storage limitation.

text: Read and rewrite every matching file in full.
explanation: Whole-file rewrites discard the surgical precision Edit is designed for and produce large diffs that collide with parallel changes to the same files. Broad discovery plus full rewrites is exactly the pattern that clobbered them.

text: Run a global in-place replacement across the repository.
explanation: A global replacement acts on raw text with no per-match validation, so unintended occurrences of the name (comments, strings, unrelated identifiers) get renamed silently. It also gives no opportunity to review each change site.

text: Grep occurrences, then Edit each with enough context.
explanation: Glob plus whole-file rewrite loses parallelism and clobbers edits. Grep for occurrences then Edit each with enough context for uniqueness keeps changes surgical.

text: Force Edit without changing its ambiguous match input.
explanation: Forcing Edit on ambiguous anchors defeats its safety rejection without resolving the ambiguity, so the underlying multiple-match problem remains and each call still fails or needs guessing.

text: Versioned Skill with procedure, rubric, and validation scripts.
explanation: Repeated governed procedures across clients need a versioned Skill bundling instructions, rubric, and validation scripts.

text: Duplicate prompts per client, paying drift and update cost.
explanation: Duplicated prompts mutate independently in each client, so the governed procedure drifts out of sync and every update must be repeated and re-verified per copy.

text: Expose scripts as tools letting clients reconstruct flow, losing version control.
explanation: Raw scripts as tools leave each client to reassemble the flow itself, so the governed sequence is no longer versioned or enforced as a single unit.

text: Store procedure in model memory, losing versioning and determinism.
explanation: Model memory is not versioned, auditable, or deterministic across runs and clients, so the procedure loses its governance guarantees.

text: Apply one multi-file patch for speed.
explanation: A single multi-file patch can partially apply, leaving some files changed and others untouched — an inconsistent state across coordinated changes. Speed here trades away the atomicity the scenario needs.

text: Expand Edit context per change; use full rewrite only if needed.
explanation: A multi-file patch risks partial application across files. Expanding Edit context per change with whole-file fallback only when necessary keeps each change atomic and validated.

text: Invoke the same patch through Bash instead of MCP.
explanation: Running the same patch through Bash changes the invocation channel, not the partial-application risk: an interrupted run still leaves files half-changed. The failure mode is unchanged.

text: Force the patch tool so validation cannot interrupt it.
explanation: Disabling validation makes partial application more likely and harder to detect, since interrupted or invalid diffs proceed unchecked. Removing safety checks worsens the exact risk the patch tool carries.

text: Add decision records with rationale and alternatives
explanation: Diagrams record what was built; successors and auditors need decision records with context, rejected alternatives, and rationale. Walkthroughs and config detail do not transfer why.

text: Add sequence diagrams of each request path
explanation: Sequence diagrams add more of the same 'what' the successors already have; they still say nothing about why guardrails exist or which options were rejected.

text: Expand deployment configuration detail for operators
explanation: Configuration detail helps operators run the system but does not answer the 'why' questions successors keep asking before an audit.

text: Record live walkthrough videos for all successors
explanation: Videos capture one narrator's view at one point in time; they decay quickly, are unsearchable, and do not constitute auditable decision records.

text: Gate high-value settlements before submission; sample low-value completions.
explanation: Irreversible high-value actions need a pre-submission gate; routine low-value work suits post-hoc sampling.

text: Review everything after submission, allowing irreversible loss plus delay.
explanation: Once a high-value settlement is submitted it is irreversible, so post-submission review permits the very loss oversight exists to prevent while also delaying every routine claim.

text: Gate only on low confidence regardless of value, missing high-stakes errors.
explanation: Confidence gating overlooks the model's confident mistakes, and on high-value irreversible settlements exactly those errors cause unrecoverable harm regardless of expressed confidence.

text: Auto-approve all with aggregate pause, allowing harm before detection.
explanation: Aggregate monitoring detects problems only after many irreversible settlements have already gone out, so the harm occurs before any human can intervene.

text: Read all files completely to avoid missing hidden dependencies.
explanation: Exhaustive full reads are exactly what exhausted the context, and wrapper modules that merely re-export the target contribute no signal. Reading everything trades the investigation's token budget for redundancy.

text: Search names and aliases first, then read only matching sections.
explanation: Exhaustive full reads explode context when wrappers alias the target. Searching names and aliases first then reading only matching sections and wrappers minimizes tokens while preserving recall.

text: List files and read them from smallest to largest.
explanation: File size has no relationship to relevance: a small wrapper re-exporting the target matters more than a large unrelated module. This ordering heuristic still reads everything eventually and exhausts context.

text: Spawn one reader per file and retain every summary.
explanation: Retaining a summary of every file reintroduces the same unfiltered volume in compressed form, and parallel readers cannot see the alias relationships between wrappers that the investigation needs to trace.

text: Behavior specs plus verifiable acceptance criteria
explanation: Drift is prevented by behavioral specs with acceptance criteria plus concrete defaults and fixtures. Inspection gates catch drift late; diagrams alone are not executable.

text: Sprint-end architect inspection gates alone
explanation: Inspection gates only detect drift after it has already been built into the sprint, rather than constraining implementation choices as they are made.

text: Deeper component structure diagrams alone
explanation: Diagrams describe structure, not behavior; they are not executable and cannot stop prompts or thresholds from diverging from design intent.

text: Prompt defaults plus threshold test fixtures
explanation: Drift is prevented by behavioral specs with acceptance criteria plus concrete defaults and fixtures. Inspection gates catch drift late; diagrams alone are not executable.

text: Trajectories are enumerable as a router feeding four chains.
explanation: Enumerable trajectories by document type collapse to a router plus explicit chains; unpredictability of order alone does not justify agents.

text: Arrival order is unpredictable, which alone does not require autonomy.
explanation: Unpredictable arrival order is a property of incoming traffic, not of the processing path; a fixed router and chains handle arbitrary arrival order just as well.

text: Tool choice varies on repeats, showing instability not agent need.
explanation: Varying tool choice on identical repeats is evidence of nondeterministic behavior to be fixed, not evidence that open-ended autonomy is required.

text: Multiple sources need combining, which chains do without agents.
explanation: Combining sources is a synthesis step that can sit inside an explicit chain stage, so it does not force model-chosen trajectories.

text: Force Grep for every search request.
explanation: Forcing literal search on every request discards semantic search entirely, so conceptual lookups where the exact wording is unknown lose their best tool. It over-constrains instead of guiding selection.

text: Delete semantic search and use literal search exclusively.
explanation: Deleting semantic search removes a genuine capability for conceptual queries where no exact string is known. The failure came from a boundary problem, not from the tool existing.

text: Rerank semantic results with Grep after every call.
explanation: Post-hoc reranking does not stop the model from choosing semantic search for literal lookups in the first place, and it adds an extra call to every search. The selection boundary remains undefined.

text: Scope semantic search to concepts; force Grep for literal lookups.
explanation: Broad semantic search hallucinates approximate matches for exact strings. Narrowing it to conceptual use while forcing Grep only for tagged literal lookups guides selection without removing capability.

text: Runbook draft without alerting or owner
explanation: A runbook no alert fires against and no owner executes leaves operators with instructions but no way to detect or respond to degradation in time.

text: Runbook, alerting, owner, plus rationale
explanation: Handoff transfers operability: runbook plus alerting, named owner, and rationale. Partial packages without alerting, owner, or rationale leave operators unable to respond.

text: Dashboards plus extended metric coverage alone
explanation: More dashboards still require someone to watch them and know what to do; without a runbook, alerts, and owner they transfer visibility but not response.

text: On-call rotation without runbook or rationale
explanation: A pager without a runbook produces pages nobody can act on, and without rationale the operators cannot judge which responses are safe.

text: Close out now and merely note the drift risk
explanation: Noting a risk without tied thresholds or an owner records the problem but changes nothing; the seasonal input shift will degrade quality with no one accountable.

text: Keep the build team on retainer indefinitely
explanation: An indefinite retainer is an open-ended staffing commitment, not an operational control; it neither defines drift thresholds nor establishes who responds.

text: Define thresholds, owner, and review cadence
explanation: AI quality drifts, so closeout needs thresholds, a named owner, and review cadence. Retainers, wider dashboards, or noted risks without tied action are monitoring only.

text: Extend dashboard coverage for all operators
explanation: Dashboards are monitoring only; without thresholds, a named owner, and a review cadence, observed degradation still has no agreed response.

text: Validator reconciling totals with bounded correction pass.
explanation: Detectable field errors with a reconciliation rule call for a validator plus bounded correction, not autonomy or voting.

text: Autonomous re-inspection loop, paying nondeterminism without targeted check.
explanation: A free re-inspection loop adds nondeterminism without the targeted reconciliation rule that actually detects the misplaced totals, so it may miss the same errors.

text: More examples while removing validation, increasing silent field errors.
explanation: Removing the reconciliation check removes the only mechanism that detects the errors, so additional examples increase confidence while silent field errors persist.

text: Parallel extractors with majority vote, paying 3x cost without reconciliation.
explanation: Majority vote triples cost but cannot detect a systematic misplacement of totals; only the explicit reconciliation rule checks stated against calculated values.

text: Query system of record at request time; reserve retrieval for stable knowledge.
explanation: Volatile inventory is a system-of-record lookup at request time; retrieval suits stable product knowledge, not live levels.

text: Smaller chunks and larger embeddings, keeping staleness while paying reindex cost.
explanation: Chunking and embedding quality cannot fix a snapshot-based index: answers remain stale between exports regardless of retrieval precision, while reindex cost grows.

text: Faster refreshes with timestamps, still serving stale data between refreshes.
explanation: However fast the refresh, any interval between exports serves outdated quantities; timestamps disclose staleness but do not remove it.

text: Ask model to infer quantity from snapshots, risking hallucinated stock.
explanation: Inferring current quantity from old snapshots invites hallucinated stock levels, worsening the accuracy problem instead of addressing its source-of-truth error.

text: Duplicate high-scoring cases for score stability
explanation: Duplicating cases the system already passes inflates the aggregate score without adding information, manufacturing stability while hiding exactly the failure modes that dominate production losses.

text: Return iteration to design with updated evals
explanation: Evals plus agreed trade-offs gate handoff planning, and iteration returns to design with updated evals. Handoff-first or discovery-placed load testing inverts the sequence.

text: Eval suite always precedes model selection
explanation: Evals gate model selection; rollback and owner gate handoff. Returning to discovery or accepting monitoring-alone readiness misplaces the gates.

text: Rollback plan precedes production handoff
explanation: Evals gate model selection; rollback and owner gate handoff. Returning to discovery or accepting monitoring-alone readiness misplaces the gates.

text: Production handoff always requires a named owner
explanation: Evals gate model selection; rollback and owner gate handoff. Returning to discovery or accepting monitoring-alone readiness misplaces the gates.

text: Iteration returns to discovery, not design
explanation: Iteration refines an existing design, so it re-enters at the design gate with updated evals; restarting from discovery discards already-settled requirements.

text: Monitoring alone satisfies handoff readiness
explanation: Monitoring without rollback planning and a named owner observes failures it cannot respond to, so it does not satisfy handoff readiness.

text: Single augmented call with explicit criteria and reviewable output.
explanation: Fixed input, no external data, and human review favor a single augmented call over workflows or agents.

text: Three-stage draft-classify-regenerate flow, paying latency without gain.
explanation: With fixed input, a strict rubric, and a human reviewer, extra draft-classify-regenerate stages add latency and cost without any accuracy mechanism the task needs.

text: Editing agent iterating to self-rated confidence, risking unbounded loops.
explanation: Self-rated confidence is an unreliable stopping signal, so an iterating agent risks unbounded loops on a task a single reviewed call already satisfies.

text: Multi-agent debate voting on versions, paying coordination without accuracy gain.
explanation: Multi-agent debate pays coordination and token overhead that only pays off when a verifiable accuracy mechanism exists, which a tone rewrite with human review does not need.

text: Source code and credentials alone for operators
