explanation: stale-fact — the exclusion is real but speaks only to training; it says nothing about the retention claim.

text: Retention obligations apply only while training use stays enabled
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — retention exists independently for logging, abuse prevention, legal compliance, and configured audit purposes, whether or not training continues.

text: Disable retention entirely so the training exclusion becomes trustable
explanation: knobs-not-design — retention feeds logging, abuse prevention, legal compliance, and configured audit, so deleting it trades real obligations for a simpler story.

text: Training exclusion and retention are two distinct claims made separately
explanation: Data may be excluded from model training by default while still being retained or monitored for logging, abuse prevention, legal compliance, or configured audit purposes, so diligence asks both questions and the vendor answers each separately.

text: Least-privilege, action-scoped tool credentials enforced at the integration's server side
explanation: Each tool operates with the minimum privileges its action needs, and identity is enforced at the server side rather than trusted from the model, so a wrong-field write stays inside the blast radius of one scoped permission.

text: Longer tool descriptions so the model picks the right fields
explanation: prompt-as-guarantee — better descriptions guide tool selection but leave every credential as powerful as before; guidance is not authorization.

text: A nightly reconciliation sweep that detects any cascading wrong-field writes
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — reconciliation repairs downstream after the cascade; it never constrains what the original write could touch.

text: Longer, more customer-friendly verdict wording drafted with the legal team
explanation: premature-optimization — nicer wording answers only the shipper; the examiner and the tuning team still cannot see what the decision relied on.

text: A louder disputes queue so contested verdicts get human attention
explanation: louder-not-explicit — routing disputes faster never explains the uncontested ones; reconstruction still starts from a bare verdict.

text: Decision logging of inputs, context, output, and routing, replay-keyed
explanation: The same instrumentation answers why a decision happened: the log captures inputs, retrieved context, output, and routing, keyed so one decision replays for the shipper, the regulator, and the tuning team; without reconstruction, no explanation is reliable.

text: A statistics dashboard of aggregate accuracy by coverage decision type
explanation: compliance-theater — aggregates describe the population while each contested decision still cannot be reconstructed from its stored verdict.

text: Retry on the same history until the refusal finally clears
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — the same refused context returns further refusals; the trigger condition never changes, so the retry loop rides the same context.

text: Hardcode all of today's refusal categories into the switch statement
explanation: stale-fact — the enumerated category set changes, so the switch reads the category but the list itself is re-checked at publish time, not frozen.

text: Treat every arriving refusal as one single undifferentiated failure event
explanation: compliance-theater — a single undifferentiated refusal path looks controlled but forfeits the category and explanation the platform already returns.

text: Read stop_reason and stop_details, reset context, and route by category
explanation: Refusals report stop_reason refusal with a stop_details policy category so different refusal classes route differently; after a refusal, reset or clear the conversation context, because the same refused context returns further refusals, and tolerate an absent stop_details.

text: A larger model tier that stabilizes the answer quality
explanation: scale-not-strategy — a bigger model lowers the error rate, but nobody is watching the trend, so the erosion continues unreviewed.

text: Longer trace retention covering the complete ninety-day window
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — deeper traces support diagnosis after the fact; they do not decide when a decline deserves a review.

text: A governance rule: quality trigger, named owner, required action
explanation: A dashboard collects signals; a feedback loop maps each to a trigger, an owner, and a required action, the decision layer the stack lacks. Without it, a drift crossing no hard threshold stays invisible, because nothing decides the signals mattered.

text: An error-rate alert retuned to far stricter failure thresholds
explanation: eval-blindness — the score was already falling; another threshold on the error rate misses a drift that never crosses one.

text: A quarterly compliance-owned output audit, whatever the scores
explanation: Regulated reviews fire on a schedule, not at a threshold: the obligation requires periodic output audits even when every metric looks good. Without a calendar trigger and named owner, the checkpoint surfaces only when a reviewer asks for the record.

text: A pager alert wired to every collected signal
explanation: louder-not-explicit — paging on every signal buries the judgment; a signal routed nowhere still decides nothing.

text: A drift trigger that forces an iterate-versus-re-architect diagnosis
explanation: The quality row turns a signal into a judgment: diagnose prompt, data, or model drift, then decide to iterate or to re-architect. That decision layer separates a feedback loop from monitoring, and it is what a pager cannot supply.

text: A monthly metric report sent to every stakeholder
explanation: compliance-theater — a periodic report records what happened but assigns no trigger, no owner, and no action, so no signal is ever decided to matter.

text: Human understanding — the author can explain what shipped and why
explanation: Diligence requires the human-understanding check: whoever merges the change explains what the code does and why, including inputs it was never tested against, because passing shallow checks is where judgment erosion starts.

text: Correctness — automated tests exist, pass, and match the stated behavior requirement
explanation: eval-blindness — the tests were green and behavior matched, so this dimension passed; the miss was that nobody could explain the code.

text: Security — no secrets committed, inputs validated, and least-privilege external tool access
explanation: valid-but-early — input validation was indeed missing, yet the decisive evidence is that nobody, starting with the author, could explain the deployed behavior.

text: Maintainability — the module reads clearly, follows conventions, and hides no surprises
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — readability governs the merged code after the fact but would not have forced anyone to explain the unvalidated input's behavior.

text: Trace the slowest request span and check whether prompt caching still hits
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — that path answers latency spikes, not gradual quality decline with no code change, so it confirms what nobody disputes.

text: Compare answers against an eval set; check model, prompt, and retrieval drift
explanation: Gradual quality decline without a code change points at a model or prompt change, or retrieval drift as the corpus grew; the eval comparison turns the symptom into a measured cause.

text: Inspect tool authorization, rate limits, and unhandled error paths across integrations
explanation: knobs-not-design — that path diagnoses intermittent tool failures through authorization and rate limits; nothing here failed intermittently or at the integration layer.

text: Check the per-request model tier and the cache hit rate against budget
explanation: eval-blindness — that path explains cost rising without a usage change; this incident says nothing about spend, and its signal is quality, not money.

text: A weekly governance committee reviews every production release after it has deployed
explanation: extra-hop — a retrospective committee adds a hop and a week; the guarantee must hold while the agent acts, not afterward.

text: Schedule the outcome document at a defined post-launch milestone
explanation: The gate needs the before-and-after comparison complete, and the after side requires enough production runtime to measure. Naming when the document completes converts an unfilled gate into a scheduled obligation; expansion decided before the after-metric exists is appetite, not evidence.

text: Freeze configuration until the after-metric can be measured
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — freezing configuration slows drift, but it neither produces the after-metric nor makes the comparison auditable, so the gate stays unsatisfied either way.

text: Name the measurement owner and confirm the control logs
explanation: The week-four action makes the coming document complete in principle: an owner accountable for ongoing measurement, and a control whose evidence accrues automatically. With those, the after-metric needs only time, which further meetings cannot supply.

text: Release-discipline instructions written into the signed prompt the production agent reads
explanation: prompt-as-guarantee — prompt instructions are guidance rather than enforcement and weaken exactly when attention drifts or the prompt gets edited.

text: A production deploy hook requiring a named release manager, with branch protection
explanation: Hooks enforce the production gate: the deploy hook blocks the release until a named release manager authorizes it, and branch protection turns anything the agent writes into a reviewed pull request with no direct route to main.

text: Tiered permission profiles that let the agent deploy anywhere without further approvals
explanation: convenience-over-safety — per-environment tiers set how much the agent may do en route, but without the deploy hook production still ships on the agent's authority alone.

text: The detection script stays deterministic; Claude is invoked only after a breach
explanation: Detection stays deterministic on a rolling baseline, and the model enters only once a control band is breached, so invocation cost tracks anomalies rather than the clock.

text: At the 3σ tier the agent acts only through gated, pre-approved routes
explanation: At 3σ the agent may open a pull request into the review gate or trigger a runbook approved in advance, so autonomy stays inside gates the organization already controls.

text: Claude watches the breach metric continuously and decides when tiers trip
explanation: over-orchestration — the design deliberately keeps a model out of the detection loop; a model there adds cost and nondeterminism to a statistical check.

text: Findings the agent produces ship through its own automated deployment route
explanation: wrong-layer-fix — findings re-enter as intent.md and ship through the normal review gate; a private deployment route would strand the change outside the audit trail.
